### Context

Pommora keeps a user's content in a folder called the Nexus. Pages are Markdown files whose front matter holds their property values; Collections are folders whose `_pagecollection.json` names the properties their pages use, and Spaces hold their values in their own `_space.json`. The property list itself is `.nexus/properties.json`: every definition with a permanent id, a label, a type, and its type's settings. The app reads the Nexus once into the **tree**, its in-memory picture of everything, and a content **index** of every page's values; reads never write. When a property change touches many files, such as a rename, a delete, or an option's removal, Pommora rewrites every affected file in one pass, a **cascade**, writing a crash-recovery note first so the work can finish after a crash or an unreachable file.

The Properties system is everything whose job is properties, wherever it lives: `Core/Properties`, and the property logic held in Views, Contexts, Nexus, the Trash, the Archive, Settings, Actions, and UIX. It grew across many sessions, so the same job is often done several ways, code lingers for file layouts no Nexus still holds, and a handful of real defects sit in the gaps. NexusOS is the one Nexus holding real property data (15 definitions over 9 types); `~/Test` is the live drives' scratch Nexus, rebuilt by `node .claude/scripts/make-benchmark-nexus.mjs test`.

#### Crash-Recovery Map

What Nathan asked to see before design (B-1): every crash-recovery file, which part of Pommora owns each, how each kind of change flows through them today, and the revision this plan builds. The evidence behind each row is cited in the tasks that change it (Phases noted in *§Process Overview*).

##### What a Crash-Recovery Note Is

Some changes rewrite many files at once: renaming a property, deleting one, renaming or deleting an option, renaming or deleting a Context or a Space. Before starting one, Pommora writes a small note in the Nexus's hidden `.nexus` folder saying what it's about to do. If the app quits halfway, or some files can't be reached, the note stays behind, and Pommora finishes the job from it the next time the Nexus opens or when you press Try Again. Once every file is done, the note is erased. Today there are exactly two of these notes, neither exists in NexusOS or `~/Test` right now, and neither travels between devices.

##### Every File Pommora Keeps in `.nexus`

Most of what lives in `.nexus` is your Nexus's own settings and data, not recovery. Only two files are crash-recovery notes. Two other things people might expect here live elsewhere: the Trash is the `.trash` folder at the top of the Nexus, and Pommora's database (its search index and file history) lives in the app's own storage on each device, outside the Nexus entirely.

| File | What It Holds | Which Part of Pommora Owns It | Kind |
|---|---|---|---|
| `nexus.json` | The Nexus's identity | Nexus | Your data |
| `settings.json` | Your settings for this Nexus | Settings | Your data |
| `state.json` | Sidebar order, pinned items, navigation | Navigation | Your data |
| `properties.json` | The property list | Properties | Your data |
| `contexts/contexts.json` | The Context list | Contexts | Your data |
| `contexts/<Context>/<Space>/` | Each Space's settings file and tiles | Contexts, Tiles | Your data |
| `interface/matrix.json` | The Matrix view's settings | Matrix | Your data |
| `interface/homepage/` | The homepage and its tiles | Tiles | Your data |
| `metadata/MM-YYYY.json` | Page icons and aliases | Nexus | Your data |
| `assets/crops.json` | Image crops | Assets | Your data |
| `assets/` (when it's the asset folder) | Your images and files | Assets | Your data |
| `archive/<Collection>/` | Archived pages and Sets | Archive | Your data |
| `assets/<id>/thumbnails/` | Sidebar thumbnails | Desktop | Rebuildable, never synced |
| `property-cascade.json` | **The property note** — one shared by every property | Properties | **Crash recovery**, never synced |
| `context-rename.json` | **The Context note** — one shared by every Context and Space | Contexts | **Crash recovery**, never synced |
| `.<name>.bad-<id>` | A damaged copy of a file, set aside when Pommora rebuilt it | Files | Left-behind damage, never synced or cleaned |
| `<name>.<number>` | A half-written copy that exists only for the moment a file is saved | Files | Momentary, never synced |
| `.trash/` (outside `.nexus`) | Trash entries; each writes its record before anything moves | Trash | A safety record of its own |
| Database (outside the Nexus) | Search index, file history, sync state | Desktop | Rebuildable per device |

##### How Each Change Flows Today

Take renaming Priority to Urgency. Pommora writes "Priority is becoming Urgency" into the property note, changes the property list, then rewrites every page. If two pages can't be reached, the note stays and you see "Couldn't update 2 Items" with Try Again. Everything else follows a variation of that, and the variations are where the trouble is.

| Change | Today |
|---|---|
| **Property Rename / Label Format** | Note, list, files. If the note is already holding another property's change, this one runs with no note at all. |
| **Property Delete** | Trash entry, note, files, Collection settings, views, then the list last. Also runs with no note if another change holds it. |
| **Option Rename / Value Format** | Refused outright if *any* property owes a change; otherwise note, list, files, views. |
| **Option Delete** | Refused if any property owes a change; otherwise note, files, views, then the option leaves the list last — and stays listed if any page was missed. |
| **Option Clear** | No note. Refused if this property owes an option change. Missed pages show an error with no Try Again. |
| **Remove From a Collection** | No note. The Collection's settings change first, then views and pages. Missed pages show an error with no Try Again, the editor stays open, and pressing Remove again does nothing. |
| **Create** | A name an owed rename used to have quietly gets a number ("Priority (2)"). A deleted property's name whose cleanup is unfinished is taken, the cleanup is abandoned, and the new property inherits the leftover values. |
| **Context Rename** | Note, folder, files, list last. If the list write fails, everything is renamed back under a second note. A second rename of the same Context overwrites the first's note, so the first's leftovers are forgotten after a restart. |
| **Space Rename** | Note, folder (a Space's folder is its list entry), files. |
| **Context or Space Delete** | No note. If any page is missed, everything is put back and the delete refuses. |
| **Restore From the Trash** | Goes through the same create step, which is the only thing stopping a later replay from deleting the restored property again. |
| **Try Again** | Four different forms: send the screen's copy of the note back, replay whatever note happens to be held (after which your own change has to be redone), re-send a Context rename with its old name, or nothing at all. |
| **On Open** | The Context note is finished first, before Pommora has read the Nexus, so it reads every page in the Nexus to find the ones to fix. The property note is finished later, once Pommora's index is ready. |

##### What the Revision Changes

One notes file, `.nexus/.owed.json`, replaces both; like them it stays on its device and never syncs, and it stays behind as an empty `{}` once nothing is owed. It holds one entry per property, Context, or Space that still owes work, so Priority's unfinished rename never touches Status. Each entry is a list of old names still owed, "these words should become whatever this thing is called now" and "these words should leave," plus, for a property, the Collections a Remove or a re-add hasn't finished. That one rule replaces four note shapes and the guesswork the replays do today, and a second change on the same item simply adds its old name to the list.

| Change | Proposed |
|---|---|
| **Property Rename / Label Format** | Its own entry, list, files. |
| **Property Delete** | Trash entry, its own entry, list, files, then each Collection's settings and views. |
| **Option Rename / Value Format** | Its own entry, list, files. Saved views name options by id, so they need no rewrite. No longer refused because some other property owes work. |
| **Option Delete** | Its own entry, the option leaves the list first, files, views. |
| **Option Clear** | Still no entry, and no longer refused because the property owes work; an old name the option still owes leaves the pages with it. Missed pages show an error with no Try Again, as today (LC-58). |
| **Remove From a Collection** | Its own entry; the editor returns to the list, and Try Again finishes stashing and stripping the pages it missed; adding the property back to that Collection cancels what's owed there. |
| **Re-Add to a Collection** | Its Collection joins the property's entry when a page can't be refilled; Try Again refills it from the stash. |
| **Create (and Rename)** | A name still owed to unfinished work is refused with "An earlier change hasn’t reached every file yet.", for properties, Contexts, and Spaces alike. Try Again finishes that work, after which the name is free. |
| **Context Rename** | Its own entry, list, folder, files. If the folder can't move, the list change is undone on the spot and nothing else happened; if the list change can't be undone either, Try Again moves the folder and finishes the files (LC-64). |
| **Space Rename** | Its own entry, folder, files. |
| **Context or Space Delete** | Trash entry, its own entry, list or folder, files. Missed pages offer Try Again instead of putting everything back. |
| **Restore From the Trash** | Restoring a property, Context, or Space turns its owed "these words should leave" back into "these words should become my name," so the pages a delete never reached come back with it. A restore onto a name another item still owes is refused the same way, and a restored property gets its set-aside values back. |
| **Try Again** | One form: finish what's owed. |
| **On Open** | One pass, once the index is ready, item by item. |

### Overview

The Properties Restructure is a full-sweep cleanup of the Properties system, wherever its logic lives. It removes the read paths for file shapes only earlier builds wrote, states each type's facts once per side of the app, and gives each job one home: one module for writing a value, one id-based reference from Collections to definitions, one undo that puts back what the file held, one `mutate` door for every property change, permanent option ids, list-first ordering with one crash-recovery notes file and one Try Again, one finder for the files holding a key, and one stash with an age. The interface follows: columns carry their resolved type, one per-kind record states filtering, sorting, grouping, and seeding, one pick model and one row menu serve every surface, one value seat replaces the table's, the cards', the panel's, and the native menu's copies, and the property settings pane takes one layout. The documents, Issues entries, drives, and test seeds read true at the end. A handful of real defects in the gaps are fixed along the way, each named in its phase's *Behavior Changes and Disclosures*.

The work is removal-first and data-first. Phases 1 through 12 rebuild the data layer underneath with almost nothing visible changing, closing with Neutral Gate 1; Phases 13 through 17 consolidate the surfaces on that layer; Phase 18 sweeps the describers. Each phase leaves a shippable head, every visible claim is proven by the Properties Drive over the Chrome DevTools Protocol, and the cumulative production delta is net-negative from Phase 1 on.

#### Concepts

Every file, folder, function, type, field, op, constant, and user-facing string the plan adds or removes entirely, grouped by the phase that lands it; anything merely modified stays out. A rename is a REMOVED row under the old name and an ADDED row under the new one; a move with its name kept is a REMOVED row at its old location. *REMOVED* is the removal's inventory.

#### Constraints

##### Who Carries These

- Nathan's approach, principles, perspectives, and constraints below are the core philosophy of the planning session and of every agent sent in planning and execution: scouts, executors, and reviewers each carry all four sections in full, word for word, in their briefs.
- The neutral verifier alone receives none of them. It's given only the baseline commit, HEAD, and a plain statement of what the work intended, and its unprimed read is the input against which the work's adherence to them is judged.

##### Approach

Nathan's, verbatim, with the overlapping entries of his two lists folded together as he ratified on 10-21-2026; Nathan's approach, principles, and perspectives govern every phase and task, and every agent brief on this topic — scouts, executors, and reviewers — carries all three sections in full.

- **Removal First:** any approach first assesses what's true *now* that could be removed, deleted, changed, consolidated, or replaced. The design isn't based on what's currently there with its course adjusted; it ensures totality-first application, removal-first scoping, and residue-eliminating frameworks that provide a clean slate rather than building changes on top of what's ultimately going to be replaced.
- **Consolidation First:** the codebase ends up more understandable, less complex, more efficient in what it does, less conflicting in defining that, and an overall cleaner foundation to work within.
- **Less Stuff:** nothing new is added unless there's evidence it's required, and nothing carries more functions, helpers, wrappers, types, layers, and call sites than necessary, with no logic stated twice. New code earns its place by removing more than it adds, fixing incorrect behavior, or delivering required behavior in its minimal form. The work ends with cumulatively less in the codebase overall — fewer ways to do similar things, less complexity, fewer paths to go through, less tech debt waiting to surface, fewer things to maintain, and fewer headaches in future work — while the line count *may* end up positive. Net-negative lines are the north star, and any net-positive gain has its rationale genuinely backed by this framework and the principles here.
- **Always Intentional:** anything within the surface area reads as always-intentional, without odd-ones-out designs, and reflects the broader codebase's resulting shape rather than remnants of, or adherence to, what's true now and is ultimately going to change. The approach reflects the outcome and isn't bound by constraints that were only relevant before. Nothing temporary, transitional, kept for compatibility, unreachable, needlessly indirect, or left over from the work remains.
- **Look Outward:** look for cross-file opportunities and shared design, avoiding hand-rolling or duplicating what's already there or can be adjusted to fit. Pommora is an established codebase, and this work doesn't start from scratch.
- **The Data Layer:** the complex data-level mechanics least reflect Nathan's intentions and mostly reflect what past session agents judged appropriate. Treat them with care and respect, without assuming they're beyond reasonable change; presenting an approach to Nathan may be all it takes to change the codebase for the betterment of everything in it and of future iterations. Zero data-level spaghetti, complexity, or additional 'stuff' should be added without reason. Rewiring things to become more understandable, more efficient, more appropriate, and more effective is preferred when the alternative is just adding more to something that's inherently unfit to suit the long-term mandate of what's actually being offered.

##### Principles

Nathan's, verbatim, folded as above.

- **Less to Understand:** A reader finds what exists, where it lives, what owns it, and what calls it with less searching and tracing than before, whether a developer reading code or Nathan reading file names and headers. A blind-eye review of the surface areas impacted by this implementation should find less confusion, less conflict about intent, and an unambiguously more approachable, maintainable ecosystem to iterate on.
- **Clearer Boundaries:** Each responsibility has one owner, and the next change of a kind has one obvious place to go, with no choice between layers, helpers, or modules — nothing that exists somewhere where it shouldn't; nothing implemented where something else already does it or adjusting it accordingly would be the more appropriate approach; nothing that increases the risk of misassumption when working here in the future.
- **One Way:** Each thing has one implementation, one pattern, and one source of truth. No part contradicts another. Anything changed or implemented should be reflected across the board — nothing that's done this way here, while something else works differently elsewhere, unless that's *genuinely* correct. Exceptions carry their reason where a reader meets them, in code or feature documentation.
- **Real Purpose:** Anything added to the codebase should have its purpose clearly stated with the perspective of its value enhancing what's already there — complexity, duplications, divergences, multiple ways to do the same thing — and anything "new" added should be assessed using that. Anything introduced should have independent justification behind its existence that isn't simply self-induced requirements. Line-count increases shouldn't translate into maintenance cost or complexity.

##### Perspectives

What this work looks out for, ratified by Nathan on 10-21-2026.

- **Responsibility Sets Scope:** The Properties system is everything whose job is properties, wherever it lives — `Core/Properties` and the property logic held in Views, Contexts, Nexus, the Trash, the Archive, Settings, Actions, and UIX. Code is inventoried where it sits and judged by where it belongs, and machinery Properties shares in kind with a sibling subsystem is assessed as one pattern across both.
- **Legacy Versus Interop:** Reading what other applications write — Obsidian's keys, YAML shapes, checkbox words, foreign frontmatter — is product behavior the Legibility decision protects. Reading what earlier Pommora builds wrote is migration residue, checked against the live Nexuses and removed once nothing holds the old shape.
- **Fix the Origin:** Every guard, refusal, special case, and review-round fix is traced to the state or decision that produces it. A fix that patched a symptom folds into the origin it patched, and a guard against a state no path produces leaves.
- **One Vocabulary:** Each concept carries one name across files, functions, types, and documents, and each name means one thing everywhere — value, raw, word, key, label, holder, member, definition. File names say what's inside them, near-identical siblings earn their difference or merge, and a module exports what other modules actually use.
- **Type Facts Once:** What varies by property type — decoding, encoding, formatting, sorting, filtering, grouping, icons, labels, cells, editors, pickers, and menu rows — is stated once per type. Adding or changing a type is one entry plus its genuinely unique pieces, and consumers ask the type's specification instead of re-deciding it.
- **One Write Path:** Every value change — from the panel, a picker, a cell, a menu, a mass assign, an undo, a restore, a sweep, or a repair — reaches the file through one pipeline, and the read path stays read-only by construction. A surface that writes values its own way folds into that pipeline.
- **Hot Paths Stay Cold:** Work done per cell, per row, per keystroke, or per render across property surfaces answers to the Hard Rule on expensive work, as does every sweep or rebuild with an incremental alternative. The Benchmark Nexuses settle it wherever scale decides.
- **Sync-Ready Shapes:** On-disk and in-memory shapes are assessed against Sync's per-section merging and the Mobile companion. While a shape is open for change, its known merge losses — such as `select_options` and `status_groups` each merging as one field — are weighed alongside it.
- **Describers Get Swept:** Tests, comments, feature documents, and Issues entries get the same deep clean as the code they describe. A test pins one intended behavior, duplicate coverage collapses, tests of removed or incidental behavior leave with it, and every claim the work makes false is rewritten in the same pass; the Issues entries citing Properties are pre-found work the sweep resolves or re-scopes.
- **Behavior Is a Decision:** Each user-visible behavior met along the way — an edge rule, a refusal, a confirmation, a cache, an auto-adoption, a repair — is classified as Nathan's intent, an earlier agent's choice, or an accident. Behavior-preserving changes proceed through the plan, while any behavior change, removal included, reaches Nathan as a decision carrying its evidence.

##### Nathan's Constraints

- **Take Along:** any trivial fixes to existing things, folds of existing duplication and divergence, or cleanup that would otherwise be risk-free, obvious, or stupid to ignore now are taken alongside this work.
- **Planning Direction (10-19-2026):** approaches may diverge from ratified decisions within reason; the "how" can alter slightly if it's genuinely best; the "what" actually gets built still gets brought to Nathan if there's conflict. Removal and consolidation come before anything truly additive, and changes to what exists come before new surface unless the new surface is foundational: never add something in one phase that a later phase's consolidation would have made unnecessary.
- **The Mandate (10-21-2026):** a self-contained, full-sweep deepclean of the Properties system, so that any future work on it happens inside a smaller, more cohesive codebase with less stuff, fewer ways of doing the same thing, and its legacy code cleaned. It finds what's spelled more than once, what lives where it shouldn't, what exists only for older systems and doesn't fit Pommora's long-term approach, what was a patch-on fix, and what wasn't integrated when it should have been.
- **Plain English (10-21-2026):** every finding, decision, and overview put to Nathan is explained in plain, non-technical English, with its technical evidence kept apart and complete. *Properties Restructure — Walkthrough* is the reference for every overview and explanation in planning.
- **Investigate Before Designing (10-21-2026):** planning re-investigates the mechanics behind every decision against the code before designing it, and presents what Nathan asked to see — the crash-recovery files, which part of Pommora owns each, how a change flows through them today, and the proposed revision — before designing it.
- **Headless Planning (10-21-2026):** from the handoff forward, the planning session runs headlessly: planning, reviews, and every call are made against the Approach, Principles, and Perspectives without stopping for Nathan. Whatever Nathan wouldn't reasonably want any other way is decided in his place. Whatever remains genuinely his call is listed in the final reconciliation report beside the plan, for his morning. The session closes with the same plain-English walkthrough given in chat at the end of the brainstorm: everything the plan changes against what's true now, what rests on his calls, and the behind-the-scenes cleanup in simple terms. Every decision the plan has to be designed around was put to Nathan before the handoff. A push notification reaches Nathan at every decision or stopping point and after each major phase of planning.
- **Sync Stays (10-21-2026):** `Core/Sync/` and its merge rules aren't changed by this work, since Sync is expected to be rebuilt; what Sync loses today is recorded as input for that rebuild.
- **Applied, Not Retyped (10-22-2026):** we should not waste tokens re-writing what's already been written.
- **Lean Execution (10-22-2026):** Lean, establish phase reviews where they matter. Give docs opus-medium instead of high; dual-agent closeout for the phase reviews please.

##### Working Rules

- **Re-Verify, Then Reuse:** *Properties Restructure — Investigation* and *Properties Restructure — Scout Reports* are leads verified at `d0595b22d`. A planning session re-verifies every claim it leans on against its own HEAD, and rides the mechanism that already does the job before designing anything new.
- **Intent Over Wording:** the decisions record intent. INFERRED and ASSUMED entries are readings the plan confirms against the code or puts to Nathan before building on them.
- **The Planning Pair:** *Properties Restructure — Investigation* and this log carry everything planning needs; the Investigation cites the decision a direction became as `[Intended as A-#]`, and this log is the one source for what was decided.
- **Cost:** nothing this work adds runs on a high-frequency trigger, and no sweep or rebuild walks the whole Nexus where an incremental or cached read does the job.
- **Gates:** `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test`, and `npm run lint` from the repo root; `.claude/Guidelines/Development-Environment.md` before driving the app; `~/Test` for live testing, rebuilt by `node .claude/scripts/make-benchmark-nexus.mjs test`.
- **Process:** decisions ran on `~/NexusOS/Studio/Athena/II. Drafts/Studio-Brainstorm-V2.md` and planning runs on `~/NexusOS/Studio/Athena/II. Drafts/Plan-Creation.md`. Their blank sections take the installed `studio-brainstorm` and `writing-plans` skills' guidance, and the processes they name without spelling out take the shape of `.claude/Planning/Completed/Archive/Archive — Plan.md`; the drafts win where they conflict.
- **Models (Nathan, 10-19-2026):** execution agents run `opus-medium`; there are no hand-checks, so every visual surface is driven over CDP. The plan's phases are designed one at a time with an advisor checkpoint before each is written.
- **Reviews:** the plan, its execution, and the landed work are reviewed as *§Review Procedure* sets out.
- **Handoffs:** every handoff on this work repeats the Approach, Principles, Perspectives, and Nathan's Constraints verbatim.
- **Names:** no personal names in anything committed outside `.claude/`, commit messages included.

##### Review Procedure

Adopted from the Archive plan (`.claude/Planning/Completed/Archive/Archive — Plan.md` *§Constraints › Models and Reviews* and *§Final Verification*, as run in `.claude/sessions/10-19-2026-Archive—Execution-&-Final-Verification.md`). Every reviewer brief carries the Approach, Principles, Perspectives, and Nathan's Constraints verbatim, except a neutral reader's, which carries none of them. Each wave closes before the next opens.

**Plan Reviews**

1. **Wave One:** two `opus-xhigh` read-only reviewers over the whole drafted plan. One leads on the frame and the data-layer phases, and the other on the interface phases. Each is briefed with the decision log as the list not to re-litigate, and with the `closeout-review` perspectives: correctness, simplification, cohesiveness, and consequences. Both read the plan's shape first and read outward, looking for:
   - sequencing faults;
   - consolidation a later phase makes possible;
   - anything a task adds that an adjacent task makes unnecessary or confusing;
   - anything additive that should have been a change to what exists;
   - machinery the behavior doesn't need, with line growth used only as a pointer;
   - anything the plan asserts about the tree that isn't true.

   Each finding is verified against the tree. One fold agent applies what holds, and what doesn't is logged with its reason.
2. **Dry Run:** in place of a second wave and the neutral read (*Lean Execution*), every task is applied in plan order in a throwaway worktree, with `tsc` and Biome run at each phase head; what it finds is execution's to fix in the code, where each phase's gates prove it.
3. **Own Read:** the orchestrator reads as the executor would, runs `plan_replay.py check` and the spec sweep (every decision maps to a task or an approved exclusion), reads for conflicts last, and checks in with the advisor.
4. **Presentation:** the plan reaches Nathan as a phase-by-phase account of what each phase builds, removes, changes, and consolidates, and why it's its own phase. With it come the ledger, with any growth justified, numbered Last Calls with recommendations, and the Open Items. Ratification is his.

Removal and consolidation come before anything additive, and changes to what exists come before new surface unless the new surface is foundational.

**Execution Reviews**

- **Phase Checkpoints:** two read-only `opus-high` reviewers to `closeout-review`'s standards at Phases 6, 8, 11B, 12, 16B, and 17, one for simplification and one adversarial, with their findings fixed before the next phase opens.
- **Mid-Plan Neutral Gate:** where a milestone completes the data layer, one `fable-high` agent is given only the baseline head, that milestone's head, and a plain statement of what the work intended, with no plan, log, document, or skill. It answers yes or no on whether the result holds, and is re-run after each fold until it answers yes.
- **Documentation Phase:** one `opus-medium` spotcheck against the Studio documentation reference before its commit.

**Post-Plan Reviews**

1. **Wave One:** two `opus-high` read-only reviewers over `BASELINE..HEAD`, briefed with the `closeout-review` perspectives.
   - **Inward:** correctness first (a defect an ordinary action reaches, data that can be lost, a cost on a frequent path, a broken invariant), then simplification within the diff.
   - **Outward:** cohesion with the rest of Core, UIX, and Desktop, odd-ones-out, and anything done one way here and another way elsewhere.

   Each reports findings ranked by severity with `file:line`, the open questions with the check that settles each, where the code drifted from the plan, and insights. One fix agent folds them as numbered fixes plus a Not Taken list, and the fold is committed.
2. **Neutral Gate:** one `fable-high` agent given only the baseline head, the final head, and the intention statement, with no plan, document, or skill. It gives a yes-or-no verdict, its corrections, and the strengths to keep, and is re-run after each fold until it answers yes on every lens.
3. **Spotcheck:** any fold made after the gate gets one `opus-high` spotcheck against the principles alone.
4. **Closeout:** the full drive on the final head and the orchestrator's own pass. Only then come the history entry, `save-session`, `save-delta`, and the report.

##### Plan Constraints

- **Gates:** `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test`, and `npm run lint`, from the repo root; each prints its own failures, and lint runs clean (`biome lint` exits 0 with warnings, so its `Found N warnings` line is read). Biome formats every TS/CSS/JSON write, so an edit failing on whitespace means it reformatted: re-read and retry. "Run the gates" in a task means these three. A VERIFY grep runs under default `git grep`, whose basic regex alternates with `\|`; `grep -r` is never used, since it reaches `Desktop/out/`. Every removal check uses `git grep -nw` for a whole symbol, or `git grep -n` with an exact, anchored pattern; `\b`, `\s`, and `\d` never appear inside `git grep -E`, where this toolchain's regex never matches them (`-w`, `[[:space:]]`, or basic regex with `\|` take their place), and no pattern also matches an unrelated name that survives. A clean state for the gates is a `git status` showing nothing outside `.claude/`. `Core/Contract/engineGraph.test.ts` and `Desktop/hostGraph.test.ts` are part of the test gate and fail the moment host-run code reaches React or a `.tsx`.
- **The Drive:** every visual or interactive claim is proven by the Properties Drive (`.claude/scripts/Properties Drive/live-drive.mjs`, on `.claude/scripts/drive-harness.mjs`, which builds the app, backs up `~/Test`, launches on its own debug port and userData, records native menus, and restores `~/Test`), created in Phase 2 with its first group and grown by one group in the last task of each phase with a visible surface. Every Review Checkpoint runs every landed group from the checkout, and the Metadata, Option Picker, and Text Property drives are re-pointed in the phase that changes what they select. A drive check is a DOM, channel-reply, or disk assertion; a screenshot is evidence beside it, never the check. Each new check is run once at its phase's base: a check claiming a change fails there before its task lands, and a check that passes there is named in its CHANGE as a regression guard. `.claude/Guidelines/Development-Environment.md` is read before anything drives the app. Nothing is left to Nathan's hand.
- **Frozen:** `Core/Sync/`, its tests included (*Sync Stays*: `mergePolicy.test.ts` keeps its cases; what Sync loses goes to *Planning Findings › §Sync Rebuild Inputs*); Project Sapphire; MarkdownPM; the property settings panes' layout and every row's wording (I-1: no row moves and no row's words change, and only Date's rows carry icons, since the rest is I-076's pass); NexusOS's files, except the four Phase 8's conversion writes after its backup.
- **Conventions:** "LC-n" and "NC-n" cite *Planning Findings › §Last Calls* and *§Nathan's Calls*; each task states the substance it leans on. A cited line is HEAD `3c6afcabb`'s, and where an earlier task moved it, the function's or test's title is the anchor. Production comments carry no planning ids. Finite states are unions plus exhaustive switches; `Core/Contract` is the one bridge, and every property change rides the `mutate` union from Phase 7 on; host-run code imports no React and no `.tsx`. User-facing copy is only what a Last Call quotes. Nothing committed outside `.claude/` carries a personal name, commit messages included.
- **Diff Notation:** each task's code lands as fenced blocks labelled with the repo path and `diff`, or `(new)` for a whole new file, each hunk opening on `@@ <anchor> @@`: the declaration, test title, or line it sits at. Space, `-`, and `+` lines are context, removal, and addition. A `…` line elides: on a `-` line it removes the lines it stands for, up to the next listed line, and elsewhere it keeps them; a `~` line is elided context. A one-line summary, `head { … }   (HEAD :a-b)`, stands for that whole block, and a `+` summary reading `(moved verbatim, HEAD path:a-b)` lands the source's lines unchanged; a block opening `~ the whole file after …` is the file entire. A block that lands on only one outcome of a measurement has `*Only on <Rule>'s <Outcome>:*` as the nearest line above it. `.claude/scripts/plan-replay/plan_replay.py` reads this notation: `check` replays the plan in order over a commit, `measure` counts it under *The Number*'s rule, and `apply` writes one task into the checkout.
- **Sequencing:** removal and consolidation precede anything additive, and changes to what exists precede new surface unless the new surface is foundational; a new type, field, op, or function lands with its first consumer, in that consumer's task. Every phase leaves a shippable head: gates green, no half-moved state, and every landed drive group green.
- **Shape:** a removal, a refactor, a migration, and a handful of fixes. The removal's inventory is *§Concepts › REMOVED*; its never-delete list is **Frozen** above. The refactor's baseline is today's behavior, kept except where a phase's *Behavior Changes and Disclosures* names a change (each tied to a decision or a Last Call) and proven by the tests each task rewrites or adds; every removal task lists its consumers and the `git grep` proving none remain. The migration is Phase 8's one-time NexusOS conversion: a backup to `~/NexusOS-Backup-<MM-DD-YYYY>/` before its first write, a transform that changes nothing on a second run, and the backup removed by its path at *§Final Verification*'s closeout. Each fix sweeps what else consumed the old behavior.
- **No New Issues:** no task files an Issues entry. I-076 and I-077 are the only deferrals; every existing entry the work touches is closed or narrowed in place with no successor (Phase 18), and anything that can't finish inside the plan is reported as a Last Call row, never filed.
- **Measurements:** each measuring task runs *Planning Findings › §Measurement Rules* as written: the Benchmark Nexus (`node .claude/scripts/make-benchmark-nexus.mjs large`), the measurement, the threshold, and both outcomes as concrete steps, so the executor runs a rule; the Benchmark Nexus and its timed sidecar are swept after.
- **The Number:** every phase's VERIFY runs `python3 ~/"The Studio/.claude/scripts/view-delta/view-delta.py" <first>^..<last> --exclude .claude --save <scratch>/phase-<N>-delta.md` over the phase's own commits, from the parent of its first commit to its last, its review's fix included, and records that file's **Actionable** column in *§Net Ledger* beside the phase's *Written* figure, removals and additions apart, the *Cumulative* column summing the rows. Other sessions commit to `active` between phases, so a range from the BASELINE head would count their work. The counting rule is `view-delta`'s Actionable rule on Biome-formatted code, stated here once and cited by every phase's *Line Total*: production lines are each code file's `+` and `-` lines, blank lines and `Core/Testing/` included, with tests (paths matching `(\.|_|/)(test|spec)s?[./]`), documents (`.md`), `.claude/`, and comment lines (`//`, `/*`, `*`) left out; a line moved between files counts on both sides, a line changed in place counts once on each side, and a file renamed whole counts only the lines it changes. Each *Written* figure is that rule applied to the phase's AFTER blocks, formatted by the repository's Biome as the executor's writes will be, task by task in plan order over HEAD, so a task's row is its own diff against what the earlier tasks leave, and an interim line counts in the task that writes it and again in the task that rewrites it. The written figures are the plan on each measurement's first outcome (F3's Pass, 02-10's Pass, O-5's Pass, and 07-17's Otherwise, the outcome its read gives at HEAD); each other outcome carries its own line in *§Net Ledger*. A phase that lands above its written figure is reported in chat before the next phase opens, with what the increase buys. The written cumulative production delta is net-negative at every phase from Phase 1 on: on the first outcomes it is thinnest at Phase 1's −136, with Phase 12's head close behind at −155 after the net-positive run of Phases 10 through 12, and on F3's Fail it is thinnest at Phase 12's head, −81. *§Final Verification* proves the measured cumulative the same way.
- **Execution:** the plan runs end to end through `c/plan-execution`, autonomously, in the main checkout on `active`: executors edit in place, each phase commits its own files with `git commit --only`, and the Properties Drive builds and launches from the checkout. If Nathan's live app runs from this checkout, the drive runs from a worktree of the phase's head built by `.claude/scripts/editor-parity/worktree.sh` and named by `POMMORA_DRIVE_REPO`. Each phase goes to one `execution-agent` carrying *§Context*, *§Overview*, this *§Constraints* whole, and its phase: `opus-low` for Phases 1 and 9, `sonnet-medium` for Phase 18, and `opus-medium` for the rest. For each task in order it first runs `python3 .claude/scripts/plan-replay/plan_replay.py apply "<this plan>" <task-id>`, adding `--outcome <Rule>=<Outcome>` once a measurement has landed on another outcome; the tool writes the task's blocks into the checkout and formats them with Biome. The executor reads its report and `git diff` against the AFTER, completes by hand only the hunks the tool refused and the CHANGE's prose steps, and runs VERIFY, retyping nothing an AFTER already holds. It reports insights, concerns, and suggestions rather than diverging, and the orchestrator checks each task's result against its AFTER and VERIFY. Reviewers sit where a phase rewrites user data, the crash-recovery path, or a surface every value passes through: the Review Checkpoints of Phases 6, 8, 11B (reading 11A with it), 12, 16B (reading 16A with it), and 17 each dispatch two read-only `opus-high` agents to the `closeout-review` skill's standards (correctness, simplification, cohesiveness, consequences; its closing procedures, write-guards, and output format don't apply), one leading on simplification and one adversarial, each carrying *§Constraints* whole and the do-not-re-raise list below, reading outward rather than in isolation, with no implementation running meanwhile, and Phase 18's checkpoint runs its `opus-medium` documentation spotcheck; every other checkpoint closes on its gates, its drive group, and its measure; the orchestrator verifies each finding against the tree, fixes what holds, and weighs the landed work against the Approach and Principles before the next phase opens. An in-flight call is weighed against *§Constraints*, disclosed in chat, and recorded under *§Deviations* where it changes an outcome. Each compaction checkpoint in *§Process Overview* runs `c/pre-compaction`, repeats the Approach, Principles, Perspectives, and Nathan's Constraints verbatim in the handoff, and stops until Nathan re-prompts; on the re-prompt the orchestrator rereads *§Constraints* and `c/plan-execution` from the files themselves before the next phase opens.
- **Neutral Gates:** two, each a `fable-high` agent that wrote and reviewed nothing, given only the BASELINE head, the head named, and the intention statement quoted in its gate, with no plan, log, principle, or document; it answers yes or no on whether the range holds, with its corrections; a "no" routes back to the orchestrator, the fix lands, and the gate runs again until it answers yes. The first closes Phase 12, where the data layer completes; the second runs inside *§Final Verification*.
- **Directive (10-22-2026):** Nathan's, verbatim, which execution and every review answer to as the plan's own reviews did: "If there's any behavior you assume ISNT my intention, that gets flagged. Ensure that the plans own reviews honestly assert its adherence to the approach and principles; concretely less of the flagged practices and perspectives: net-negative delta; zero room for two issues being replaced by one new one except the two previous issue-logged items; codebase must adhere to our standards unambiguously and be the honest better environment as a result." The two previously logged items are I-076 and I-077.
- **Rulings (Not Re-Raised):** every decision in *Properties Restructure — Decisions & Intention* and its *§Rejected* list; every call in *Planning Findings › §Planner's Calls, Settled*; and each Last Call as Nathan rules it on ratification. A reviewer's disagreement with a ruling is noted, not raised as a finding.
- **Out of Scope Everywhere:** I-076's settings-pane pass (row icons, the panes' layout and layer wording); I-077's own stash timeframe; I-042 part (1)'s Core-wide folder split; the Sync rebuild and its inputs, Approach M included; `reveal-parity`; Mobile.

### Phase 1 — Removal First

**GOAL:** Everything that reads only what earlier Pommora builds wrote leaves: the open-time migration file, the legacy type-id preprocess, the bare hidden-group keys, and their tests. The value encoder stops refusing a shape no path produces, the Context rename record loses a field nothing reads, two generic modules move to their owners, unread exports close, and comments and test titles that describe nothing true are swept. No behavior changes on NexusOS, `~/Test`, or a Benchmark Nexus. The shared test seed lands first, so every later phase rewrites its tests on one seeding path.

**State This Phase Starts From:** HEAD `7b5e294ab` (code identical to `3c6afcabb`). Every `-` line below is HEAD's text. No earlier phase exists. A live read-only check for this phase (10-22-2026) found no `"type"` of `multi_select`, `url`, or `datetime`, no `"card_banner": "image"`, and no `"icon": "table"` in any JSON under `~/NexusOS` or `~/Test`; NexusOS's only `hidden_groups` is `[]`; no `~/Benchmark-*` exists.

**Executor Notes:** A cite in a file an earlier task of this phase already edited is HEAD's line number; locate it by the quoted text, not by counting. Biome formats every TS/CSS/JSON write through the PostToolUse hook, so a literal the AFTER shows on several lines may land on one; an Edit failing on whitespace means the file was reformatted — re-read and retry. `git add` every new or moved file before its commit, since `git commit --only` skips untracked paths. Commit with `git commit --only -m "<message>" -- <paths>`.

#### Task 1-1

@@ after seedSpaceSidecar @@
+
+/** `assigned` maps a Collection folder, root-relative, to the property ids it assigns; its sidecar's id is the folder's own name. */
+export async function seedNexus(
+  root: string,
+  opts: { defs?: PropertyDefinition[]; assigned?: Record<string, string[]> } = {},
+): Promise<void> {
+  if (opts.defs)
+    await putJson(nexusConfig(root, NEXUS_CONFIG_FILES.properties), {
+      order: opts.defs.map((d) => d.id),
+      defs: Object.fromEntries(opts.defs.map((d) => [d.id, d])),
+    })
+  for (const [folder, properties] of Object.entries(opts.assigned ?? {}))
+    await putJson(sidecarPath(join(root, folder), 'collection'), {
+      id: basename(folder),
+      properties,
+    })
+}

With the legacy reads gone, the hidden-key functions take the stored key list rather than a whole view, since the grouping was read only to decide a legacy key.

**NOW:** `Core/Views/views.ts:317-323` derives a bare `<bucket>` or `sub/<bucket>` key when the view groups on the property, read by `isBucketHidden` (`:325-337`), `toggleHiddenBucket` (`:339-350`), and `editHiddenBucket` (`:359-375`); `clearHiddenBuckets` (`:377-385`) also drops a bare `sub/` key under a sub-grouping (`:382`). The Group pane's date list adds any stored key starting with a year (`Core/Views/Settings/GroupFrame.tsx:510-511`). ```UIX/Utilities/moveItem.ts diff
@@ after nextOrder @@
+
+export function resolveRowOrder<T>(
+  items: readonly T[],
+  keyOf: (item: T) => string,
+  listed: readonly string[] = [],
+): T[] {
+  const byKey = new Map(items.map((i) => [keyOf(i), i]))
+  const first = listed.flatMap((k) => {
+    const hit = byKey.get(k)
+    if (hit) byKey.delete(k)
+    return hit ? [hit] : []
+  })
+  return [...first, ...byKey.values()]
+}
```

#### Departures and Disclosures

##### Departures From the Findings

- **`seedNexus`'s Unsaid Details (1-1):** the signature is the Findings' verbatim (`opts` defaults to `{}`), since later phases call it. It writes the registry only when `defs` is given, so a test can rewrite a Collection's assignment alone, and writes each `assigned` folder's sidecar as `{ id: <the folder's own name>, properties }`, since a Collection sidecar without an id is refused by `patchSidecar` and isn't held by the tree. The defs map is built inline rather than through `registryOf` (`propertiesRegistry.ts:64`), so `hostFs.ts` stays a leaf with no engine import for the tests that mock engine modules. Identity and the Contexts registry stay per test: `restoreScrub.test.ts`'s eleven registry rewrites run mid-test inside `cycle`, and `handlers.test.ts` holds a ULID identity, so a seed that also wrote those files couldn't serve either.

##### Behavior Changes and Disclosures

- **A Try Again That Misses Files Again Can Leave No Record (1-5, LC-49):** today, a Context or Space rename's Try Again builds its record without writing it first (`contextCascade.ts:205-210`, `:257-261`), so when it skips files again the skip-list write establishes a record the next open replays. After this phase it only clears on a clean sweep. That differs only when no matching record is held at the Try Again: an earlier rename's record was displaced by a later rename of the same item (A → B skips, B → C, then a stale Try Again from A), or the open's replay already finished and cleared it. Every other settle rewrote a record already on disk, and `contextCascade.test.ts:593-598` (a retry that skips again keeps the journal) stays green. **Classification:** an earlier agent's mechanism with no stated intent; the field was never read, and the record's establishing write is a side effect of persisting it. P11 replaces the retry's construction with one note per item. **Recommended:** take it.
- **A Value Kind Past the Request Door Drops Its Key (1-4):** `encodeValue`'s default arm answers `undefined`, which a writer now lands as "no value" where it refused before. The arm is unreachable: every request is validated by zod (`mutateRequest.ts:60,90`), and TypeScript proves the switch exhaustive, which the kept `never` check still enforces for a future kind.
- **Legacy Spellings Read as Nothing (1-2, 1-3):** a registry definition typed `multi_select`, `url`, or `datetime` reads as unadmitted (A-4, Nathan's intent); a saved view's `card_banner: "image"` or `icon: "table"` stays as written; a bare hidden-group key hides nothing. The live check finds none of these in NexusOS or `~/Test`, and the Benchmark script writes camelCase.
- **The Test Collection's Id (1-1):** `restoreScrub.test.ts`'s Notes Collection is `Notes` under `seedNexus`'s rule where it was `col-notes`; no assertion reads it.

### Phase 2 — What Counts as a Property

**GOAL:** A property's type becomes one of the nine user types or Context, while Title, Creation Time, Last Modified, and Location become one Filedata table keyed by reserved id, and one record keyed by column type answers every column, Title included. One admission predicate, read by the create and by the registry read, sets aside any definition holding a Context type, a Filedata type, or a reserved id, so the UI filters that guarded against those definitions leave. Title's value reads as text, so P8's option ids can land without a title ever reading as an id. The small catalog moves (the refusals and seeds to their readers, the bucket labels to the grouping code) ride along, and the Properties Drive opens with group 1.

Builds on P1's AFTER: `typeIds` is exported and read directly by `propertyDefinitionFields.type` and `Core/Bundles/rows.ts` (the `propertyType` preprocess and `LEGACY_TYPE_IDS` gone), `TypeSpec` is module-private, `resolveRowOrder` lives in `UIX/Utilities/moveItem.ts`, `pageRow.ts` lives in `Core/Views/`, `Core/Testing/hostFs.ts` holds `seedNexus`, `Core/Testing/definitions.ts` replaces `Core/Testing/fixtures/registry.json`, and plan-round tags are gone from test titles. Every cite below is HEAD `7b5e294ab` (code identical to `3c6afcabb`); where P1 moved a line, the cite names the function or test title.

Every diff below, apart from Task 2-1's move, was applied and run on a copy of the tree carrying P1's type-id, migration, and export changes: `tsc -p Core`, `tsc -p Core/tsconfig.src.json`, `tsc -p UIX`, both Desktop configs, and `biome check Core` came back clean, `engineGraph.test.ts` and `hostGraph.test.ts` passed, and the full Core suite passed apart from the six cases P1 itself deletes or rewrites (the legacy-type pins and the `registry.json` fixture's `datetime`).

**TASK:** State "a definition the property list holds" once as `admissible` (a user type under an unreserved id), read by `validateDefinition` and `normalizeRegistry`, so a hand-written Context-typed or reserved-id definition is set aside on the way in, and the UI filters that defended against it leave.

**NOW:** `normalizeRegistry` (`Core/Properties/propertiesRegistry.ts:21-45`) admits whatever decodes and passes `validateName` (`:30-33`); after Task 2-2 a stored stamp type fails decode, but a `context` definition and a `_`-reserved id are still admitted. `validateDefinition` (`Core/Properties/validation.ts:58-74`) refuses both at create with two checks (`:64`, `:65-66`). The guards that filter them back out: `PropertyFrame.tsx:202,204` (`isReservedPropertyId`, `props` read at `:284,397,468,478`), `Core/Views/visibilityModel.ts:17` (`!isReservedPropertyId(d.id)`), `Core/Views/Settings/SortFrame.tsx:92` and `Core/Interface/Menus/propertyMenuActions.ts:69` (`PROPERTY_TYPES[d.type].origin === 'user'`). `PropertyFrame.test.tsx:174-187` pins the frame's filter with a hand-made `_title` definition. Every `PropertyDefinition[]` the renderer holds comes through `registryFrom` (`readRegistry`, `readKeptRegistry`, and `fileEvents.ts:489`'s registry event), so admission is the one gate. `PropertyPanel.tsx:209` already calls `schemaTargets(schema, () => true)`.

+export function formatBucketLabel(
+  key: string,
+  granularity: DateGranularity,
+  dateFormat: DateFormat,
+  separator: DateSeparator,
+): string {
+  const numeric = NUMERIC_FORMATS.has(dateFormat)
+  const sep = separator === 'slash' ? '/' : '-'
+  switch (granularity) {
+    case 'year':
+      return key
+    case 'week': {
+      const m = /^(\d{4})-W(\d{2})$/.exec(key)
+      if (!m) return key
+      return numeric ? `W${m[2]}${sep}${m[1]}` : `Week ${Number(m[2])}, ${m[1]}`
+    }
+    case 'month': {
+      const m = /^(\d{4})-(\d{2})$/.exec(key)
+      if (!m) return key
+      if (numeric) return `${m[2]}${sep}${m[1]}`
+      const month = dateFmt({ month: 'long' }).format(new Date(`${key}-01T00:00:00`))
+      return `${month} ${m[1]}`
+    }
+    case 'day': {
+      if (!/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(key)) return key
+      const out = formatDate(key, dateFormat, 'none')
+      return numeric && separator === 'dash' ? out.replaceAll('/', '-') : out
+    }
+  }

import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
import {
  ask, click, escapeAll, launch, mouseClick, must, NEXUS, openCollection, portalOpen, restore, results, sel,
  SETTINGS_BUTTON, settles, shot, sleep, until,
} from '../drive-harness.mjs'

const PORT = 9403
// The drive's groups in order, each landed by the plan phase that adds it.
const LANDED = ['1']
const GROUPS = new Set(process.argv.slice(2))
if (GROUPS.size === 0 || [...GROUPS].some((g) => !LANDED.includes(g))) {
  console.error(`usage: node live-drive.mjs <group…>   (groups ${LANDED.join(', ')})`)
  process.exit(2)
}

// ── Items ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

const ledger = []
/** One assertion, owned by the group that lands it and the decision it proves, printed as MATRIX.md lists it. */
function item(group, decision, name, pass, detail) {
  const mark = pass ? 'PASS' : 'FAIL'
  console.log(`${mark.padEnd(5)}  [g${group} ${decision}] ${name}${!pass && detail ? `\n       ${detail}` : ''}`)
  results.push({ name, pass: !!pass })
  ledger.push({ group: String(group), decision, name, mark })
}
const show = (v) => JSON.stringify(v)

// ── The Nexus and its surfaces ──────────────────────────────────────────────

const COLLECTION = 'Collection A'
const REGISTRY = join(NEXUS, '.nexus/properties.json')
const config = async (cdp) => (await ask(cdp, 'nexus:state')).value.tree.config
const held = async (cdp, id) => (await config(cdp)).registry.some((d) => d.id === id)

/** Each label and glyph a surface draws, read off its rows. */
const rowsOf = (cdp, css) =>
  cdp.evaluate(`[...document.querySelectorAll(${JSON.stringify(css)})].map((e) => ({
    label: e.textContent.trim(),
    glyph: [...(e.querySelector('svg')?.classList ?? [])].find((c) => c.startsWith('lucide-'))?.slice(7) ?? null,
  }))`)
const PORTAL_ROWS = '[data-picker-portal] [role=button]'
/** Opens the view settings at one of its frames. */
async function viewFrame(cdp, frame) {
  await escapeAll(cdp)
  await mouseClick(cdp, SETTINGS_BUTTON)
  await sleep(800)
  await click(cdp, `[...document.querySelectorAll('[role=button], button')].find((b) => b.textContent.trim() === ${JSON.stringify(frame)})`)
  await sleep(800)
}
async function pickerRows(cdp, ariaLabel) {
  await click(cdp, sel(`[aria-label="${ariaLabel}"]`))
  await until(`the ${ariaLabel} picker`, () => portalOpen(cdp))
  return rowsOf(cdp, PORTAL_ROWS)
}

// ── Group 1 — What Counts as a Property ─────────────────────────────────────

// Today's Filedata columns, each with the label and glyph it shows.
const FILEDATA = [
  { id: '_title', label: 'Title', glyph: 'text-align-justify' },
  { id: '_created_at', label: 'Creation Time', glyph: 'clock-plus' },
  { id: '_modified_at', label: 'Last Modified', glyph: 'repeat' },
]
const showsFiledata = (rows) => FILEDATA.every((f) => rows.some((r) => r.label === f.label && r.glyph === f.glyph))

async function group1(cdp) {
  const view = { id: 'view_01KZPROPERTIESDRIVE00TBL', name: 'Drive Filedata', type: 'table', property_order: FILEDATA.map((f) => f.id), hidden_properties: [] }
  await must('save the Drive Filedata view', ask(cdp, 'views:save', COLLECTION, 'collection', view, {}))
  await must('show the Drive Filedata view', ask(cdp, 'mutate', { op: 'setActiveView', path: COLLECTION, kind: 'collection', viewId: view.id }))
  await openCollection(cdp)
  await until('the table head', () => cdp.evaluate(`document.querySelectorAll('.table-head > *').length >= ${FILEDATA.length}`))
  const head = await rowsOf(cdp, '.table-head > *')
  item(1, 'F-2 F-3', 'the header shows Title, Creation Time, and Last Modified with their glyphs', showsFiledata(head), show(head))

  await viewFrame(cdp, 'Sort')
  const sortBy = await pickerRows(cdp, 'Sort By')
  item(1, 'F-2 F-3', 'Sort By offers Title, Creation Time, and Last Modified with their glyphs', showsFiledata(sortBy), show(sortBy))

  await viewFrame(cdp, 'Filter')
  const filterBy = await pickerRows(cdp, 'Filter property')
  item(1, 'F-2 F-3', 'the filter offers Title, Creation Time, and Last Modified with their glyphs', showsFiledata(filterBy), show(filterBy))
  await shot(cdp, 'g1-filter-targets')

  const stored = readFileSync(REGISTRY, 'utf8')
  const file = JSON.parse(stored)
  const witness = { id: 'prop_drive_witness', label: 'Drive Witness', key: 'Drive Witness', type: 'text' }
  const context = { id: 'prop_drive_context', label: 'Drive Context', key: 'Drive Context', type: 'context' }
  writeFileSync(REGISTRY, JSON.stringify({
    ...file,
    order: [...file.order, witness.id, context.id],
    defs: { ...file.defs, [witness.id]: witness, [context.id]: context },
  }, null, 2))
  const read = await settles(() => held(cdp, witness.id))
  item(1, 'F-1 LC-11', 'a Context definition written by hand is set aside when the list is read', read && !(await held(cdp, context.id)), show({ read }))

  await viewFrame(cdp, 'Properties')
  await click(cdp, `[...document.querySelectorAll('[role=button], button')].find((b) => b.textContent.trim().startsWith('All Properties'))`)
  await sleep(800)
  const pane = await cdp.evaluate('document.body.innerText')
  item(1, 'F-1 LC-11', 'the Properties pane lists the witness and never the Context definition', pane.includes(witness.label) && !pane.includes(context.label), show({ witness: pane.includes(witness.label), context: pane.includes(context.label) }))
  await shot(cdp, 'g1-properties-pane')

  await escapeAll(cdp)
  writeFileSync(REGISTRY, stored)
  await until('the registry as it was', async () => !(await held(cdp, witness.id)))
}

// ── The run ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

let cdp
try {
  cdp = (await launch(PORT, 'properties-shots')).cdp
  if (GROUPS.has('1')) await group1(cdp)
  cdp.close()
} catch (e) {
  item(0, '—', 'the run reached its end', false, String(e?.stack ?? e))
  if (cdp) await shot(cdp, 'failure').catch(() => {})
} finally {
  await restore()
}
const count = (f) => ledger.filter(f).length
console.log('\ngroup  pass  fail')
for (const g of ['0', ...LANDED].filter((g) => g === '0' || GROUPS.has(g))) {
  const of = (m) => count((r) => r.group === g && r.mark === m)
  console.log(`${g.padStart(5)} ${String(of('PASS')).padStart(5)} ${String(of('FAIL')).padStart(5)}`)
}
console.log(`${results.filter((r) => r.pass).length}/${results.length} held`)
process.exit(results.every((r) => r.pass) ? 0 : 1)
```

```.claude/scripts/Properties Drive/MATRIX.md (new)
## Properties Drive — Matrix

The drive's cases, derived from *Properties Restructure — Decisions & Intention* and written to the end-state contract of the Properties Restructure plan's AFTER blocks. Each group lands with the plan phase that adds it and drives the channels and surfaces the interface uses. Every check prints as `[g<group> <decisions>] <name>`, so a run reads against the tables below line for line. Each group seeds what it needs in `~/Test` and puts it back; the harness restores `~/Test` when the run ends.

#### Group 1 — What Counts as a Property

| Case | Seeds | Operation | Expected | Decisions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The header | the `Drive Filedata` table view showing `_title`, `_created_at`, `_modified_at` | open Collection A | `.table-head` reads Title, Creation Time, and Last Modified with `text-align-justify`, `clock-plus`, and `repeat` | F-2, F-3 |
| The sort targets | as above | view settings › Sort › Sort By | the picker offers the three with the same labels and glyphs | F-2, F-3 |
| The filter targets | as above | view settings › Filter › Filter property | the picker offers the three with the same labels and glyphs | F-2, F-3 |
| A hand-written Context definition | `prop_drive_witness` (Text) and `prop_drive_context` (`type: 'context'`) written into `.nexus/properties.json` from outside | the registry's file event | the witness reaches `tree.config.registry`; the Context definition doesn't | F-1, LC-11 |
| The Properties pane | as above | view settings › Properties › All Properties | the pane holds `Drive Witness` and never `Drive Context` | F-1, LC-11 |
```

#### Departures and Disclosures

##### Departures From the Findings

Every later task cites `validation.ts`, whose lines are HEAD's `schema.ts` lines unchanged.
- **One `admissible` Predicate in `validation.ts` (Binding Design 3):** the Findings name `isUserType` as the predicate both gates read, with `normalizeRegistry` "also" setting aside a reserved id. Reading both halves in both gates would state the reserved-id rule twice, so `admissible(def)` (`isUserType(def.type) && !isReservedPropertyId(def.id)`) is the one statement of what the property list holds; `validateDefinition`'s two refusals become one, and `isUserType` stays the type half `CREATABLE_TYPES` also reads.

### Phase 3 — Type Records and Looks

**GOAL:** Each property type's facts are stated once per side of the boundary, so consumers ask the type instead of re-deciding it: the engine record (`PROPERTY_TYPES`) answers which types hold connections, register members, and draw a blank, and owns the creatable list; one renderer record (`Core/Properties/typeDisplay.ts`) answers a type's label, icon, chip shape, chip glyph, and look-menu name; one looks record (`LOOKS`) answers which looks a column offers. The owners land first, because the records' display fields land inside them: the link-display vocabulary moves to `Core/Connections/linkValue.ts`, the pane targets to `Core/Views/paneTargets.ts`, and the renderer label tables to `Core/Properties/displayLabels.ts`, where one `pickerOptions` builder replaces the eight hand-rolled label-to-option maps. A Number column's right-click names its look "Style" (I-4). Builds on P2's AFTER: `typeIds` holds the nine user types plus `context`, `ColumnType = PropertyType | FiledataType`, `PROPERTY_TYPES: Readonly<Record<ColumnType, TypeSpec>>` with `origin: 'user' | 'context' | 'filedata'` and a `title` row, `isUserType`, and `FILEDATA` in `Core/Properties/properties.ts`; and on P1's AFTER (`TypeSpec`, `NUMBER_FAMILIES`, and `StoredColumnStyle` unexported, `propertyType` gone).

#### Task 3-1

**TASK:** Move the link-display vocabulary (`LINK_DISPLAYS`, `LinkDisplay`, `isLinkDisplay`, `DEFAULT_LINK_DISPLAY`, `LINK_DISPLAY_LABELS`) from `Core/Properties/properties.ts` into `Core/Connections/linkValue.ts`, which already owns `linkDisplayText`, `linkMarkdown`, and `linkPaste`, and re-point its fourteen importers (08-08).

```Core/Views/paneTargets.ts diff
+import { FILEDATA, type Filedata, type PropertyDefinition } from '../Properties/properties'
+import type { NexusTree } from '../Nexus/tree'
+import { contextsByIdOf } from '../Contexts/contextIdentity'
+import type { PickerOption } from '@pommora/uix/Pickers/PickerControl'
+import { propertyIcon, propertyTypeIconName } from '../Properties/Cells/PropertyTypes'
+
+export interface PaneTarget {
+  id: string
+  label: string
+  icon: string
+}
+
+// Location has no column type, so its glyph is named here.
+const filedataTarget = ({ id, label, type }: Filedata): PaneTarget => ({
+  id,
+  label,
+  icon: type ? propertyTypeIconName(type) : 'folder',
+})
+export const FILEDATA_TARGETS = {
+  title: filedataTarget(FILEDATA.title),
+  createdAt: filedataTarget(FILEDATA.createdAt),
+  modifiedAt: filedataTarget(FILEDATA.modifiedAt),
+  location: filedataTarget(FILEDATA.location),
+}
+
+export const contextPaneTargets = (tree: NexusTree | null): PaneTarget[] =>
+  [...contextsByIdOf(tree)].map(([id, c]) => ({ id, label: c.title, icon: c.icon }))
+
+export const schemaTargets = (
+  schema: PropertyDefinition[],
+  qualifies: (def: PropertyDefinition) => boolean,
+): (PaneTarget & { def: PropertyDefinition })[] =>
+  schema.filter(qualifies).map((d) => ({
+    id: d.id,
+    label: d.label,
+    icon: propertyIcon(d),
+    def: d,
+  }))
+
+export const targetOption = (t: PaneTarget): PickerOption<string> => ({
+  value: t.id,
+  label: t.label,
+  icon: t.icon,
+})
```

```Core/Nexus/governedRoot.ts diff
@@ new file @@
+// Everything that lands a value in one governed file: the world it's read against, the reconcile that repairs every governed key, the spelling a write keeps, and the one-parse writer.
+
+import { join, relative } from '../Paths/posix'
+import { listOf } from '../Contract/validators'
+import { memberKey } from '../Files/rootValues'
+import { linkEntry, readLinkText } from '../Connections/linkValue'
+import { contextTitles } from '../Contexts/contexts'
+import { type ContextWorld, contextWorldOf, groupOf } from '../Contexts/contextResolve'
+import { byKey, type PropertyDefinition } from '../Properties/properties'
+import {
+  asText,
+  checkedSpelling,
+  decodeValue,
+  encodeValue,
+  isBlankValue,
+} from '../Properties/propertyValue'
+import { spelledNumber } from '../Properties/formatValue'
+import { namesValue } from '../Properties/pageValue'
+import { assignedDefs } from '../Properties/assignment'
+import { liveTreeOf } from './liveTree'
+import { owningCollection } from './treePatch'
+import type { ContextGroup, NexusTree } from './tree'
+
+export interface GovernedWorld {
+  contexts: ContextWorld
+  defs: ReadonlyMap<string, PropertyDefinition>
+}
+
+export const governedWorld = (
+  tree: NexusTree,
+  defs: ReadonlyMap<string, PropertyDefinition>,
+): GovernedWorld => ({
+  contexts: contextWorldOf(tree.contexts),
+  defs,
+})
+
+// A Space holds any registry property, so its own values reconcile against every definition, by key.
+export const spaceWorldOf = (tree: NexusTree): GovernedWorld =>
+  governedWorld(tree, byKey(tree.config.registry))
+
+export async function pageWorldOf(root: string, absFile: string): Promise<GovernedWorld> {
+  const tree = await liveTreeOf(root)
+  const owner = owningCollection(tree, relative(root, absFile))
+  return governedWorld(tree, await assignedDefs(root, owner ? join(root, owner.path) : null))
+}
+
+/** What a frozen copy may still name: its options are the definition's own, and `holds`, when given, answers which pages still exist. */
+export interface Frozen {
+  holds?: (title: string) => boolean
+}
+
+export function gonePageEntry(raw: unknown, frozen: Frozen): string | null {
+  const entry = linkEntry(raw, 2)
+  const link = entry === null ? null : readLinkText(entry)
+  const gone =
+    link?.kind === 'page' &&
+    link.title !== '' &&
+    frozen.holds !== undefined &&
+    !frozen.holds(link.title)
+  return gone ? entry : null
+}
+
+/** `next` spelled as `raw` already spells it: … (the doc comment moves verbatim from `propertyValue.ts:231`). */
+export function writtenSpelling(next: unknown, raw: unknown): unknown {
+  if (next === true) return checkedSpelling(raw)
+  if (typeof next === 'number') return spelledNumber(next, raw)
+  if (typeof next === 'string')
+    return raw != null && typeof raw !== 'string' && asText(raw) === next ? raw : next
+  if (!Array.isArray(next)) return next
+  if (next.length === 1 && Array.isArray(raw) && linkEntry(raw, 2) === next[0]) return raw
+  const held = listOf(raw)
+  return next.map((v) => {
+    const names = namesValue(v)
+    const named = held.filter((w) => names(linkEntry(w, 2) ?? w))
+    return named.length === 1 ? named[0] : v
+  })
+}
+
+// A restore of a frozen copy keeps only the options the definition still offers and the pages its world holds, so a deleted option or page never comes back through it.
+/** `raw` read and written back through `def`, spelled as `raw` spells it; undefined when it reads as nothing or, under `frozen`, names a page gone. */
+export function reencode(def: PropertyDefinition, raw: unknown, frozen?: Frozen): unknown {
+  const value = decodeValue(def, raw)
+  const gone = frozen && value.kind === 'link' && gonePageEntry(value.value, frozen) !== null
+  return gone || isBlankValue(value) ? undefined : writtenSpelling(encodeValue(def, value), raw)
+}
+
+interface Reconciled {
+  root: Record<string, unknown>
+  changed: string[]
+}
+
+type Governor = { def: PropertyDefinition } | { group: ContextGroup }
+
+function governorOf(key: string, world: GovernedWorld): Governor | undefined {
+  const def = world.defs.get(key)
+  if (def) return { def }
+  const group = groupOf(key, world.contexts)
+  return group && { group }
+}
+
+const memberCount = (v: unknown): number => new Set(listOf(v).map(memberKey)).size
+
+export function reconcileGovernedRoot(
+  root: Record<string, unknown>,
+  world: GovernedWorld,
+  frozen?: Frozen,
+  skip?: string,
+): Reconciled {
+  const out: Record<string, unknown> = {}
+  const changed: string[] = []
+  for (const [key, raw] of Object.entries(root)) {
+    const governor = key === skip ? undefined : governorOf(key, world)
+    if (!governor) {
+      out[key] = raw
+      continue
+    }
+    let next: unknown
+    if ('def' in governor) next = reencode(governor.def, raw, frozen)
+    else {
+      const byTitle = world.contexts.spacesByTitle.get(governor.group.def.id)
+      const titles = contextTitles(raw).flatMap((title) => byTitle?.get(title)?.title ?? [])
+      if (titles.length) next = writtenSpelling([...new Set(titles)], raw)
+    }
+    // A live reconcile never shrinks or blanks a value: one holding a member it can't resolve, or reading as nothing, stays as written, for the user to settle.
+    if (!frozen && (next === undefined || memberCount(next) < memberCount(raw))) {
+      out[key] = raw
+      continue
+    }
+    if (next === undefined) {
+      changed.push(key)
+      continue
+    }
+    out[key] = next
+    if (JSON.stringify(next) !== JSON.stringify(raw)) changed.push(key)
+  }
+  return { root: out, changed }
+}
```

The reconcile now spells each value before the live guard rather than after it. The guard counts members by `memberKey`, and `writtenSpelling` maps each member of `next` to the one `raw` member named by its own title, or keeps it, so a spelled `next` holds as many distinct members as an unspelled one; `governedRoot.test.ts`'s crossing and spelling blocks pin it.

+/** A world a value is read against: a key `targets` recorded at the delete answers by whether the page it named is there under any name, any other key by the name. */
+export function frozenWorld(
+  index: PageIndex,
+  targets: ReadonlyMap<string, { id: string }> = new Map(),
+): Frozen {
+  return {
+    holds: (title) => {
+      const id = targets.get(pageKey(title))?.id
+      return id === undefined ? index.holders(title).length > 0 : index.byId.has(id)
+    },
+  }
+}

+/** `raw` with `value` under `key`, its members spelled as the root already spells them, after the reconcile repairs every other governed key. */
+export function writtenRoot(raw: Json, key: string, value: unknown, world: GovernedWorld): Json {
+  const reconciled = reconcileGovernedRoot(raw, world, undefined, key).root
+  const def = world.defs.get(key)
+  const kept = def ? keepingForeignWords(def, value, raw[key]) : value
+  return landValue(reconciled, key, writtenSpelling(kept, raw[key]))
+}
+
+/** The root a governed file holds: a page's frontmatter, or a Space sidecar's object. */
+export const governedRoot = (file: string, text: string): Json =>
+  isMarkdownFile(file) ? splitFrontmatter(text) : (parseJsonObject(text) ?? {})
+
+export const changedKeys = (raw: Json, next: Json): string[] =>
+  [...new Set([...Object.keys(raw), ...Object.keys(next)])].filter(
+    (k) => JSON.stringify(raw[k]) !== JSON.stringify(next[k]),
+  )
+
+/** A page's next text with the keys `rewrite` changes merged in; null when it changes none. A changed key the next root holds no value for is deleted. */
+export const rewriteRaw =
+  (rewrite: (raw: Json) => Json | null) =>
+  (page: SweptPage): string | null => {
+    const next = rewrite(page.raw)
+    if (next === null) return null
+    const keys = changedKeys(page.raw, next)
+    if (!keys.length) return null
+    const modeled: Json = {}
+    for (const k of keys) if (k in next) modeled[k] = next[k]
+    return page.merge(modeled, keys)
+  }
+
+/** Rewrites the page at `absFile` in one parse, writing the text `rewrite` answers for it, or nothing for null. Takes no lock: each caller holds the page's lock over a wider span, and a re-take is refused. */
+export async function rewriteRootAt(
+  absFile: string,
+  rewrite: (page: SweptPage) => string | null,
+): Promise<Result<null>> {
+  const content = await readTextOrNull(absFile)
+  if (content === null) return fail('not-found', 'Page not found.')
+  const page = sweepParse(content)
+  if (!page) return fault(UNPARSED_FRONTMATTER)
+  const next = rewrite(page)
+  if (next !== null) await atomicWriteFile(absFile, next)
+  return ok(null)
+}

+export function spelledNumber(next: number, raw: unknown): unknown {
+  const shape = numberShape(raw)
+  if (!shape) return next
+  if (shape.value === next) return raw
+  // A changed value keeps the file's currency symbol, percent sign, grouping, and decimal places; its digits are the typed value's.
+  const digits = new Intl.NumberFormat('en-US', {
+    minimumFractionDigits: Math.min(shape.places, 20),
+    maximumFractionDigits: 20,
+    useGrouping: shape.grouped,
+  }).format(Math.abs(next))
+  const spelled = `${next < 0 ? '-' : ''}${shape.lead}${digits}${shape.tail}`
+  return readNumber(spelled) === next ? spelled : next
+}

##### Departures From the Findings

- **The Decode Entry Keeps `isBlankRaw`:** the Findings' `raw == null || (typeof raw === 'string' && raw.trim() === '')` would read a Text value of `[]` as the text `[]`, which the Text arm's `isBlankRaw` reads as empty today; `isBlankRaw(typeof raw === 'string' ? raw.trim() : raw)` states the same rule and keeps that.
- **A Write That Changes Nothing Lives in `writtenRoot`:** the Findings give the Space write its own `changedKeys(raw, next).length ? next : null`; `writtenRoot` answering `null` states it once for the page value, tag, Space value, and both Space-link halves, since both writers already read `null` as "leave the file".
- **The Tidy's List Test Rides `reencode`:** the reconcile no longer holds the decoded value, so `reencode` answers `{ next, listed }`, its return type written inline since nothing else names it, and the stash refill reads `next`.

##### Behavior Changes and Disclosures

- **A Several-Word Select or Status Tidies (P-1, LC-20, LC-21; Task 4B-1):** on any value write to its page or Space (a property, a Context tag, a Space link) and on Repair On Open, it's written as the one option it shows; one naming no option stays as written. Body, title, and banner writes don't tidy. A case-variant word beside a valid one is dropped by the same rule (`Stage: [done, Active]` with option key `Done` becomes `[Active]`; T flag 5).
- **A Multi-Select's Foreign Words Dedupe and Follow Its Options (LC-22; Task 4B-1):** `[a, zeta, a]` becomes `[a, zeta]` on a sibling write, as its own pick writes it, and its options move ahead of the words no option names (`[zeta, alpha]` with only `alpha` registered becomes `[alpha, zeta]`), the order a pick writes; the never-shrink guard kept `[zeta, alpha]` whole.
- **File Dedupes (LC-23; Task 4B-2):** a File value reads each entry once and drops a spaces-only entry. A repeated entry the file quotes (Obsidian's spelling and Pommora's) also collapses on disk at the next sibling write; a repeated unquoted `[[x]]` parses as a nested list the member count counts once per occurrence, so it's kept on disk while it reads and shows once.
- **Spaces-Only Reads as Empty (J-1 for Text, LC-24 for the Rest; Task 4B-2):** for every type; a live reconcile keeps it as written (never blank), and a restore drops it.
- **A Write That Changes Nothing Writes Nothing (J-9, LC-25; Task 4B-3):** a Space value write or Space link that changes no key leaves `_space.json` and its modified time alone; a Space clear of a key it never held tidies the Space's other values, as a page clear does.
- **Repair Properties On Open Defaults On (O-3; Task 4B-4):** for every Nexus without an explicit setting; a first open still repairs nothing.

### Phase 5 — One Home per Definition

**GOAL:** Each property definition lives once, in the property list, and every Collection holds only the ids its settings file assigns, as written. One resolver in `Core/Nexus/treePatch.ts` (`schemaOf`, read by `containerSchema` and `holderSchema`) answers every holder's schema against the registry, held per id list so render paths stay cold, so a definition arriving by sync or hand edit patches the tree instead of walking the Nexus, `assignedDefs` and its disk fallback leave, and the repair sweep, the page world, and the restore scrub build their worlds from the tree through one synchronous builder. Registration at open reads the content index instead of every page file. A damaged property list opens the Nexus with no definitions and an unreadable entry naming the list, and the list's own file event restores the definitions once it's fixed. It's its own phase because it changes what the tree holds for every Collection, which P6's put-back, P7's ops, and P13's columns all read.

**Builds On:** P1's shared seed (`seedNexus`, `Core/Testing/definitions.ts`), P2's `ColumnType`/`isUserType`/`FILEDATA`, P3's `registersMembers` type fact (read at `Core/Properties/optionOps.ts:133` and `Core/Nexus/fileEvents.ts:528`), and P4's `Core/Nexus/governedRoot.ts` (`GovernedWorld`, `governedWorld`, `spaceWorldOf`, `pageWorldOf`, `reconcileGovernedRoot`, `rewriteRootAt`, and the `Frozen` world with `gonePageEntry`) and `Core/Nexus/governedSweep.ts` (moved from `Core/Properties`). P4 excluded `frozenOf`, so `frozenWorld(linkWorld(...))` stands at its two HEAD sites (`assignment.ts`, `restoreProperty.ts`), `frozenWorld` reading from `Core/Trash/holdings.ts`, and `spend.ts`' own `frozenWorld` calls stand as at HEAD; P5 touches none of them. Citations name HEAD (`7b5e294ab`, code identical to `3c6afcabb`) unless a line names the phase that moved it.

**Order:** 5-1 removes `assignedDefs` before 5-2 changes the field its tree arm reads, so no line is edited only to be deleted one task later (*§Departures From the Findings › Task Order*).
