@@ containerSchema @@
 export const containerSchema = (
   tree: NexusTree | null,
   of: string | CollectionNode | SetNode,
 ): PropertyDefinition[] => owningCollection(tree, of)?.properties ?? NO_SCHEMA
+
+const schemas = new WeakMap<
+  readonly string[],
+  { registry: PropertyDefinition[]; schema: PropertyDefinition[] }
+>()
+
+/** The definitions `ids` names, in its order, against the tree's registry; an id the registry lacks reads as nothing. One answer is held per id list and kept whole while the definitions it names stay the same, so a render keyed on a schema reruns only when its definitions change. */
+export function schemaOf(tree: NexusTree, ids: readonly string[]): PropertyDefinition[] {
+  const { registry } = tree.config
+  const held = schemas.get(ids)
+  if (held?.registry === registry) return held.schema
+  const next = ids.flatMap((id) => registry.find((d) => d.id === id) ?? [])
+  const schema = held && sameItems(next, held.schema) ? held.schema : next
+  schemas.set(ids, { registry, schema })
+  return schema
+}

For each container whose schema holds a Multi-Select it calls `readPageRecord` per page (`:136-139`), a `cachedParse` (`readNexus.ts:134-140`), one `stat` per page at least. The index holds every page's parsed front matter (`Core/Index/indexSeed.ts:42,60`) and `readPageRelations(paths)` answers it per page (`Core/Index/contentIndex.ts:85-87`), or null until the seed marks the store ready. The settle's `rels` form (`Core/Nexus/settle.ts:161-163`) passes changed pages, owed containers, and paths newly in reach; a rescope's reseed runs after that settle (`settle.ts:183-190`), so a page newly in reach isn't indexed yet when it registers. Multi-Select members are scalars (`scalarMembers`, `Core/Contract/validators.ts:11`), which the index's JSON carries unchanged. `Core/Nexus/handlers.test.ts:180-212` pins the open's registration but not its source.

**TASK:** A damaged property list opens the Nexus with no definitions and an unreadable entry naming the list (O-6): the kept registry read answers null for a file this session never saw parse, the walk lists it through the one registry-damage rule the Contexts registry already follows, the `Unreadable` registry arm names which registry it is so its two readers stay scoped to Contexts, and the list's own file event drops the entry once it reads.

**NOW:**
- `readNexusConfig` (`readNexus.ts:286-288`) reads `readKeptRegistry` (`Core/Properties/propertiesRegistry.ts:56-59`), whose `readKept` throws for a damaged file this session never saw parse (`Core/Files/atomicWrite.ts:200-205`), so the open's config gate waits on the root with that error (`handlers.ts:74-80`), and the watcher's wait re-reads the same three files (`Desktop/FileWatch/watcher.ts:146`). A file damaged after a clean read reads as its kept copy (`atomicWrite.ts:193-196`). `forgetLastReads()` runs on every genuine open (`handlers.ts:70`).
- The Contexts registry's damage arm (`readNexus.ts:315-322`): a registry that reads as nothing re-reads strictly and lists `{ path: CONTEXTS_REGISTRY_REL, kind: 'registry', reason }` unless absent.
- `Unreadable`'s registry arm (`Core/Nexus/tree.ts:109-112`) carries no name, and its two readers mean the Contexts registry: `latchBaseline` carries every prior Context and Space through when any registry entry is listed (`Core/Nexus/remintLedger.ts:55-60`), and `tileHostsOf` counts one unreachable host for an unreadable one (`Core/Tiles/tileHosts.ts:51-53`), read by `reachConfig`'s skip count (`Core/Nexus/configReach.ts:358-360`).

#### Departures and Disclosures

##### Departures From the Findings

- **Task Order:** the Findings order R4, R5, R3, O-6. `assignedDefs`' tree arm reads `node.properties`, so landing the field first would rewrite that line only for 5-1 to delete it; removing `assignedDefs` first (5-1) lets the field change (5-2) touch no code that leaves. `schemaOf` lands with 5-1 because the returning Collection needs an id-to-definition resolver before `containerSchema` reads it.
- **The Memo Keys on the Id List, Not `entityMemo`:** `entityMemo` (`tree.ts:132`) keys on `tree.collections`, which every page create, rename, or move replaces, so it would hand `useViewHost`'s `schema` memo (`useViewHost.ts:60`) a new array on every settle and rerun the view pipeline. `schemaOf` holds one answer per `propertyIds` array, checked against `config.registry`'s identity, and recycles the held array while it names the same definitions (`sameItems`, the recycle `repointRegistryInTree` performed). It resolves with `registry.find` per id rather than a memoized id map: a registry is tens of definitions, a resolve runs only when the registry or the id list changes, and a second memo would hold more than it saves.
- **The World Builder Is `governedWorld` Itself:** R5's "one synchronous builder shared with `pageWorldOf` and `scrubReturning`" is `governedWorld(tree, schema)` taking the schema array and building `byKey` once inside; the repair sweep keeps each Collection's world in a map keyed by the schema array, so a sweep over many pages builds one world per Collection, as HEAD's per-folder memo did; the repair sweep, `pageWorldOf`, and `scrubReturning` each hand it a schema, and `spaceWorldOf` hands it the registry. No separate builder is added. `spaceWorldOf` doesn't fold into a path-keyed builder: its three callers hold a Space node or a sidecar file, not a Space path.
- **Page-Only Readers Read `containerSchema`:** the Findings route `assignedDefs`' readers through `holderSchema`; each addresses pages only (`pageWorldOf` pins a Space path reading no definitions), so they read `containerSchema`, which `holderSchema` forwards to, and `holderSchema` serves the three holders that can be a Space (5-3).
- **`holderSchema(tree, holder: SpaceNode | string)`:** each of its three callers already holds the Space node, so the Space arm needs no `spaceAt` scan.
- **`assignedIds` Moves to `Core/Nexus/containerFields.ts`:** the walk now parses the `properties` list itself, and importing `assignedIds` from `Core/Properties/assignment.ts` would close a `containerFields → assignment → liveTree → readNexus → containerFields` cycle; the one parser sits where every other sidecar field is read, settling 02-11's three parsers to one.
- **`applyContainer`'s Comparison Stays:** its `containerSchema(t, next)` resolves the built node's own ids, since `owningCollection` answers a Collection node itself, so only its `registryOf` argument changes.
- **R3 Keeps the File Read for a Settle:** the Findings scope R3 to the open's call; folding the settle's `rels` form onto the index too would miss a page newly in reach, whose rescope reseed runs after the settle that registers it (`settle.ts:183-190`). An open whose index isn't ready (no store bound, as in some tests) reads the files, the same loop.
- **O-6's Damage Rule Is One Helper for Both Registries:** the Contexts block's strict re-read becomes `listDamaged(registry, path)` inside `walkNexus`, serving both lists at no line cost, so the reason (`'unparsed'` or `'unreadable'`) is read the same way for each. `readKeptRegistry` answers null rather than importing `Unreadable` into Properties, keeping the entry's construction beside the Contexts one.
- **`notifyUnreadable`, `handlers.ts`, and the Watcher Need No Change:** the notice names its entry by `titleFromPath`, so the property list's reads `'properties.json' contains invalid metadata` and the Contexts registry's `'contexts.json' …`; the open's gate and `waitUntilReadable` wait on `readNexusConfig`'s throw, which only identity and settings still raise.
- **The Recovery Prunes Through `repointUnreadable`:** the Findings' "a fixed file's own event replaces `config.registry`" leaves the walk's entry listed after the patch; `applyRegistry` prunes it with the existing `repointUnreadable(tree, path, null)`, exported, before installing the registry, so a file fixed to an empty list clears its entry too.
- **P4 as Landed:** this phase leans on no P4 shape beyond `governedRoot.ts`' world builders and `governedSweep.ts`' new home. `frozenOf` was excluded in P4, so `spend.ts`' `linkWorld`/`frozenWorld` lines are cited as they stand at HEAD; `Frozen` and `gonePageEntry` live in `governedRoot.ts`; `rewriteRootAt` (`Result<null>`) and `reencode` (`{ next, listed }`) aren't read here.
- **The Drive Reads No Notice:** the notice's 3 s dwell ends inside the harness's 3 s post-launch wait, so group 4 pins the tree's entry and `store.test.tsx` pins the notice.

##### Behavior Changes and Disclosures

- **A Damaged Property List Opens the Nexus (O-6, Nathan's Intent):** the Nexus opens with no definitions, the Properties pane empty, and the notice `'properties.json' contains invalid metadata` (or `unreadable metadata` for bytes that can't be read) with Try Again, which walks. While it's damaged, every registry write refuses (create, rename, delete, option edits), as do property value writes and a page create carrying seeded values (strict reads); body edits, titles, Context tags, and Space links work; the repair sweep reconciles Context keys only, and registration registers nothing. Each Collection keeps its assigned ids, so nothing is lost, and fixing the file restores every definition without a reopen. A list damaged after a clean read still reads as that read, as today.
- **A Definition Arriving From Outside Patches (No Visible Change):** a synced or hand-added definition a Collection already assigns shows without the whole-Nexus walk it caused.
- **The Open Registers From the Index:** an index row that missed its file's last change (the index reseeds when it misses an event, `fileEvents.ts:294-297`) registers what the index holds; the file's next settle registers from the file. Its query brings the pages' link rows along with their values (`Desktop/Store/stores.ts:133-157`), one query per Multi-Select Collection, in place of a stat and parse per page.
- **A Space Subject With No Node:** `PropertyPanel` hands `holderSchema` the empty path when its Space has left the tree, reading `NO_SCHEMA` where it read the registry; the panel draws no row in that state either way (`PropertyPanel.tsx:181`).
- **Take Along:** `SettingsFrame` stops minting a fresh `[]` per render for a Collection assigning nothing (it reads `NO_SCHEMA` or the held array), so `useActiveView`'s schema input holds still.

### Phase 6 — Undo From the File

**GOAL:** The part of Pommora that writes a value records exactly what the edited key held in its file and hands that record back with its reply, as the one request that takes the write back; undo sends it, and one put-back lands the key as the file spelled it, a bare `Status:` included, through the same page and Space writers every value write uses, leaving every other key as it now stands and writing nothing when the key already reads so. Undoing a Link value also takes back the alias its write added, through the alias edit's own reply. The renderer stops re-implementing the host's encode: a pending write lays the picked value itself over the row, so `applyValueAtRoot`, `withSeeds`' encode, and `rekeyOverrides` leave, and the F3 measurement on `~/Benchmark-Large` decides whether that last part stays. Builds on P4A's `Core/Nexus/governedRoot.ts` (`rewriteRootAt`, `rewriteRaw`, `changedKeys`, `writtenRoot`, `pageWorldOf`, `spaceWorldOf`), P4B's rule that a write changing nothing writes nothing (`writtenRoot` answering `null`), P1's `Core/Views/pageRow.ts`, and P2's Properties Drive (`.claude/scripts/Properties Drive/live-drive.mjs`).

Line cites are HEAD (`c11a312f3`). A function an earlier phase moved or rewrote is anchored by name, with the phase named; its unmarked lines in an AFTER are context and stay as that phase left them.

#### Task 6-1

**TASK:** A swept page reads one key's pair as its frontmatter spells it and lands such a pair back under a key, answering nothing to write when the key already holds that node, so a value write can record the key's node and an undo can put that node back.

**NOW:** `SweptPage` (`Core/Files/pageFile.ts:248-251`) carries `raw` and `merge`; `sweepParse` (`:254-260`) parses the block once and closes over `doc`. `merge` lands parsed values through `mergeInto` (`:166-186`), which re-creates each node with `nodeSpelledAs` (`:146-164`), so a value of `null` prints `Status: null`, the defect I-063's unfixed half names; its serialize-or-refuse tail throws P4A's `UNPARSED_FRONTMATTER`. Nothing reads or writes a key's node as the file holds it. A probe of the repo's `yaml` 2.9.0 confirms a pair cloned into a one-key document prints `Status:\n` for a bare key and `Tags: [a, "b"] # c\n` with its comment, and that `doc.set(key, parseDocument(pair).contents.items[0].value)` lands it bare, in place when the key is held and last when it isn't. The one-key document holds none of the block's anchors, so a value naming one (`B: *x` beside `A: &x foo`) throws "Unresolved alias" when printed, and prints `B: *x\n` under `verifyAliasOrder: false`; `withPair` lands it back as `B: *x`, which `writable` already admits whenever the anchor is still in the block. Re-landing the node a key already holds prints the same pair before and after, so comparing the two answers whether a landing changes anything.

+  const def = (await readRegistry(root)).defs[id]
+  if (def) return def.key
+  const group = contextWorldOf((await liveTreeOf(root)).contexts).groupById.get(id)
+  return group && contextKey(group.def.title)
+}
+
+/** Puts each entry's key back as its file held it before the write that recorded it, a page's own node so a bare key comes back bare, leaving every other key as it now stands and a file whose key already reads so unwritten; answers how many files it couldn't put back. */
+export async function putBackEntries(root: string, entries: readonly PutBack[]): Promise<number> {
+  let missed = 0
+  for (const entry of entries) if (!(await landEntry(root, entry))) missed++
+  return missed
+}
+
+// A page's key is read inside its lock, as the write read it, so a key renamed since lands under its new name.
+async function landEntry(root: string, { file, fieldId, before }: PutBack): Promise<boolean> {
+  if (!isMarkdownFile(file)) {
+    const at = await mutableTarget(root, file, ['space'])
+    const key = at.ok ? await keyNow(root, fieldId) : undefined
+    if (!at.ok || key === undefined) return false
+    const back = await writeSpaceSidecar(at.value, (raw) => {
+      const next = landValue(raw, key, before)
+      return changedKeys(raw, next).length ? next : null
+    })
+    return back.ok
+  }
+  const at = await mutableTarget(root, file, ['page'])
+  if (!at.ok || !(before === undefined || typeof before === 'string')) return false
+  return machine().lock(at.value, async () => {
+    const key = await keyNow(root, fieldId)
+    if (key === undefined) return false
+    return (await rewriteRootAt(at.value, (page) => page.withPair(key, before))).ok
+  })
+}
```

(`contextKey` and `mutableTarget` join the module's imports from those paths, and `keyNow` reads the `contextWorldOf` it already imports; `join` returns to the posix import, which P5 left without it once `pageWorldOf` stopped reading it, for `writeSpaceSidecar`; `landValue`, `changedKeys`, `isMarkdownFile`, and `liveTreeOf` are already read there.)

#### Task 6-3

**TASK:** The window's undo sends the record its write's reply carried, at the row's current path, instead of the renderer's held copy, so `held`, `restore`, `restoreValue`, and `requestedValue` leave and a Context undo stops re-sending decoded ids.

**NOW:** `assignValue` (`Core/Properties/assignValue.ts:87-120`) captures `held = target.frontmatter[def.key]` (`:98-99`), and its revert calls `restore` (`:60-72`): a property sends `restoreValue { path, propertyId, held }` patched through `landValue`, and a Context re-sends `setContext` with the decoded `prior` ids (`:67`), so a tag title naming no known Space is dropped (`contextTarget` builds the list from ids, `contextWrite.ts:42-56`). `send` (`:26-36`) and `write` (`:38-58`) split the optimistic patch from the request. The host routes `restoreValue` with `setProperty` (`Core/Nexus/mutate.ts:198-202`); `requestedValue` (`Core/Properties/setProperty.ts:40-47`) passes `held` through, and `writtenRoot` runs `keepingForeignWords` and `writtenSpelling` over it. The zod arm and its false comment sit at `mutateRequest.ts:91-92`. `Core/Session/undo.ts` (`pushUndo`, depth 100, `groupUndo`, `resetUndo`) is unchanged by this phase.

**TASK:** An alias add answers the edit that takes it back, and a Link value's undo sends that edit after its put-back, so undoing a Link value removes the alias its write added and keeps an alias the page already had.

**NOW:** `rememberedAlias` (`Core/Properties/assignValue.ts:74-85`) builds an `editAliases { op: 'add' }` for a landed Link value newly showing an alias, and `assignValue` fires it and forgets it (`:106-107` at HEAD; Task 6-3 keeps that shape). `editPageAliases` (`Core/Nexus/pageMetadata.ts:166-179`) lands it through `updatePageMetadata` and answers `done(…)`'s `{}`. `applyAliasEdit` (`Core/Connections/aliasMemory.ts:27-54`) appends a new alias, respells a fold-equal held alias in place, and returns the held list for a name `keepsAlias` refuses, so a blind `forget` on undo would delete an alias the page held before. Text values and bodies remember aliases through `linkSettle` (`Core/MarkdownPM/Links/linkSettle.ts:125-145`), outside the value write, and keep them (LC-16).

```Core/Connections/aliasMemory.ts diff
@@ after applyAliasEdit @@
+/** The edit that takes back an add of `alias`: re-adding the spelling it respelled, forgetting the alias it appended, or none when it changed nothing. */
+export function addUndo(worn: readonly string[], alias: string, title: string): AliasEdit | undefined {
+  const named = alias.trim()
+  if (!keepsAlias(named, title)) return undefined
+  const was = heldAliases(worn, title).find((a) => normalizeTitle(a) === normalizeTitle(named))
+  if (was === undefined) return { op: 'forget', alias: named }
+  return was === named ? undefined : { op: 'add', alias: was }
+}
```

#### Departures and Disclosures

##### Departures From the Findings

- **The Put-Back Lands Through the Value Writers:** the Findings' item 2 has the put-back land each key "as the file spelled it" and names no writer. A page entry lands through P4A's single-file writer, `rewriteRootAt`, whose page rewrite `withPair` answers directly, the first rewrite that isn't a root rewrite lifted through `rewriteRaw`; the value ops read `page.pair(key)` inside their own page rewrite before handing the page to `rewriteRaw`, so the writer's signature, the banner, and P4A's 43 page seeds stay as P4A left them. A Space entry lands through `writeSpaceSidecar`, which moves into `governedRoot.ts` beside the page writer, since the put-back importing it from `contextWrite.ts` would close an import cycle (`contextWrite.ts` reads `governedRoot.ts`); its color and order callers read it through the moved import. No put-back writes a file any other way.
- **`putBackEntries` Takes the Entries Alone, Beside the Sweep's Put-Back:** the Findings' item 2 gives the one put-back a `keys` scope for "a sweep's `changedKeys`". `git grep` at HEAD answers one caller of `undoSweep` (`contextCascade.ts:179`, `unlinkMembers`), which P11B removes with `undoSweep` (P11 item 10), so the value undo is the only caller that survives the plan, and `putBackEntries(root, entries)` takes the entries and the root they're relative to. The sweep's private `keysPutBack` stays as P4A left it until P11B deletes it with `undoSweep`: it puts back a text triple by key, keeping the file's times, under the lock its caller holds, where the value put-back resolves each entry's key by id and writes with a fresh time, so routing the sweep through the new landing would take a times parameter and a by-key path for code P11B deletes. P6's export takes its own name, so nothing is renamed, and the scoreboard's "put-back landings 2 → 1" closes at P11B.
- **A Put-Back That Changes Nothing Writes Nothing:** LC-25's rule, which P4B lands as `writtenRoot` answering `null`, takes the same form here: `withPair` answers `null` when the key's pair prints the same after the landing as before, a key renamed since included, and the Space arm answers `null` when `changedKeys` finds nothing, so neither writer touches the file.
- **`PutBack` Holds No `key` and No `landed`:** the record is `{ file, fieldId, before? }`, `fieldId` naming a property's or a Context's id, as `Picked` keys by field id. The key is re-read from the id inside the file's lock, as `setPagePropertyOp` reads it, so a recorded key would be read by nothing. The display patch needs no landed value: `decodeValue` drops exactly what the host's encode and reconcile keep beyond the pick (unregistered Multi-Select words, a Select's extra words, Context titles naming no Space), so a decoded landing equals the decoded pick for every type, and the values read that retires the override shows the file itself.
- **`undo` Is the Reverting Request:** `MutateOutcome.undo?: MutateRequest`, as `retry` is the retrying request, in place of `undo?: PutBack[]` plus an `aliases` field on `putBack`. A value write answers `{ op: 'putBack', entries }`; an alias add answers `{ op: 'editAliases', path, edit }`, the existing op with the inverse edit, so no `AliasPutBack` type, reply field, or second landing exists, and the revert sends each request its write answered.
- **The Alias Comes Back as an Inverse Edit:** "the aliases it replaced" reads as the add's own effect: forget the alias it appended, or re-add the spelling it respelled (`addUndo`). Restoring the whole prior list would also drop an alias added by any other surface between the commit and the undo.
- **The Put-Back Holds the Contexts Lock Always:** a put-back can reach a Context key on a page or both halves of a Space link, so the `putBack` arm runs under `underContexts` whatever it reaches, rather than splitting entries by kind.
- **`restoreValue.test.ts` Moves to `putBack.test.ts`:** its cases keep their bytes and run through the reply's record; its seed takes P1's `seedNexus`, as *P1 · The Shared Seed* asks of the phase that next rewrites a test file.
- **The F3 Run Launches a Build:** *§Measurement Rules* names `npm run dev`; the run uses `drive-harness.mjs`'s `launch`, which builds both sides the same way and accepts a baseline worktree through `POMMORA_DRIVE_REPO` (`editor-parity`'s precedent), so the comparison is like for like on the build users run.
- **Item 6 Is a Check:** the undo list's ownership is unchanged code, verified in the Review Checkpoint rather than carried as a task.
- **Take Along:** the values epoch's `oldKey`/`newKey`, read only by the re-key F3 removes, leave with it.

##### Behavior Changes and Disclosures

- **Undo Puts Back the File's Own Spelling (E-1, E-2; Nathan's Intent):** a bare `Status:` comes back bare, a key's quoting, flow style, trailing comment, and a YAML alias (`B: *x`) come back as written, and only the edited key changes; a sibling the write tidied stays tidied. I-063's unfixed half no longer occurs (its text is P18's).
- **An Undo That Changes Nothing Writes Nothing (LC-25; Nathan's Intent):** undoing a write that changed nothing, such as a re-pick of the value a page or Space already holds, leaves the file and its modified time alone, as the write itself did.
- **Unknown Context Titles Survive an Undo (Nathan's Intent):** undoing a tag change on a page whose tag names a Space Pommora can't find puts the unknown name back.
- **Undoing a Link Value Takes Back Its Alias (E-3; Nathan's Intent, LC-16):** an alias the add appended is forgotten, a respelled alias regains its old spelling, an alias the page already held stays, and a link typed in a Text value keeps the alias its save added.
- **What an Undo Reaches (an Earlier Agent's Choice Kept, Disclosed):** the edited row is reached where it now sits, as today; a far Space of a Space link and a linked page whose alias is taken back are reached at the paths they had at the edit, so one renamed or moved between the edit and the undo keeps the value or alias. A put-back that can't reach a file reports "Couldn’t update 1 Item." through the cascade notice instead of a refusal; with the row re-read by id first, only a race reaches it.
- **An Undo Waits on a Context Rename:** a value undo holds the Contexts lock, so one pressed during a Context or Space rename lands after it. No visible change beyond that ordering.
- **The Pending Display Is the Pick (F3):** while a write is in flight its cell, card, and panel row show the picked value; since the decoded pick is what the file decodes to, nothing visible differs from today's encoded patch. A pending pick now survives a property rename by its id where today's re-key renamed its key.

### Phase 7 — One Door for Property Changes

**GOAL:** Every property change reaches the host through `mutate`, answers one `MutateOutcome`, and takes the schema lock exactly once, and a confirmation counts what a change would rewrite through one typed request, so the nineteen writing property, schema, and registry channels, their seven reply adapters, the holder count's argument sniff, and the renderer's own round-trip module leave. The counting words move to `Core/Nexus/entities.ts`, which both sides already import; a delete held by nothing asks without "0 Items"; an option's Remove reads Delete; a property delete runs through the one confirmation home; and a Trash restore that took a numbered name says so. It's one phase because every one of these lands on the same eight files (`bridge.ts`, `Core/Properties/handlers.ts`, `mutateRequest.ts`, `mutate.ts`, `nexusSlice.ts`, `confirmations.ts`, `PropertyFrame.tsx`, `useOptionEdit.tsx`), and splitting them would rewrite those files twice.

**Builds On:** P1 (`typeIds` replaces `propertyType`, exported from `Core/Properties/properties.ts`; `resolveRowOrder` lives in `UIX/Utilities/moveItem.ts`; plan-round tags are gone from test titles, so every test below is cited by its title without them; `seedNexus` and `putJson` live in `Core/Testing/hostFs.ts`), P2 (`KEY_REFUSAL` and `RESERVED_NAME_PREFIX` live in `Core/Properties/validation.ts`, the two option seeds in `Core/Properties/registryProperty.ts`; `isUserType` gates `validateDefinition`; `FILEDATA` replaces `RESERVED_PROPERTY_ID`), P3 (`Core/Properties/Cells/PropertyTypes.tsx` is `Core/Properties/typeDisplay.ts`; the link-display vocabulary, `DEFAULT_LINK_DISPLAY` and `LINK_DISPLAYS` among it, lives in `Core/Connections/linkValue.ts`; `CREATABLE_TYPES` lives in `Core/Properties/properties.ts`; `lookOptions` lives in `Core/Properties/displayLabels.ts`; `optionShapeFor` left `UIX/Labels/recipes.tsx` for the renderer record), P4 (`governedSweep.ts` is `Core/Nexus/governedSweep.ts`; `Core/Nexus/governedRoot.ts` holds `reencode` and `writtenSpelling`; `Core/Properties/pageValue.ts` is gone, `editList` living in `Core/Files/rootValues.ts` and `valueEditRewrite` in `optionOps.ts`; `Frozen` and `gonePageEntry` live in `governedRoot.ts` and `frozenWorld` in `Core/Trash/holdings.ts`, read by `assignment.ts`, `restoreProperty.ts`, and `spend.ts`, with `frozenWorld(linkWorld(...))` standing at its two sites), P5 (`CollectionNode.propertyIds`; `holderSchema` and the memoized `containerSchema`; `assignedIds` lives in `Core/Nexus/containerFields.ts`, and `assignedDefs` and `assignment.ts`' `byKey` import are gone), P6 (`MutateOutcome.undo`, the `putBack` op in place of `restoreValue`; `rekeyOverrides` left `Core/Views/Host/useContainerValues.ts`, and `bumpValuesEpoch` takes no arguments). +import { type Handlers, withRoot } from '../Contract/handlers'
+import { fault } from '../Contract/result'
+import { propertyHolders } from './deleteProperty'
+import { optionHolders, valueFormatHolders } from './optionOps'
+import { countedChange } from './properties'
+import { keyFormatHolders } from './registryProperty'
+
+const NEEDS_ID_AND_VALUE = fault('A property id and value are required.')
+
+// Every property write enters through `mutate`; this read counts what a change would rewrite, by the dry run of the sweep the change runs.
+export const propertiesHandlers = {
+  'property:holders': withRoot(async (root, _ctx, propertyId: unknown, change: unknown) => {
+    const read = countedChange.safeParse(change)
+    if (typeof propertyId !== 'string' || !read.success) return NEEDS_ID_AND_VALUE
+    const counted = read.data
+    switch (counted.of) {
+      case 'property':
+        return propertyHolders(root, propertyId)
+      case 'option':
+        return optionHolders(root, propertyId, counted.label)
+      case 'format':
+        return 'key_format' in counted.change
+          ? keyFormatHolders(root, propertyId, counted.change.key_format)
+          : valueFormatHolders(root, propertyId, counted.change.value_format)
+    }
+  }),
+} satisfies Partial<Handlers>

+/** A held item asks the Trash's question and a property its own, counting what holds it. A system-trash delete mints no bundle, so it offers no Undo; `undoTo` returns a held item where the delete took it from rather than to its origin, and a property, which a restore lands only in the registry, takes none. */
+export const confirmDelete = async (
+  target: { title: string } & (
+    | { path: string; kind: HeldKind; undoTo?: RestoreDestination }
+    | { propertyId: string; undoTo?: never }
+  ),
+): Promise<boolean> => {
+  const asked =
+    'propertyId' in target
+      ? askDestroyProperty(target.propertyId, target.title)
+      : askTrashing([target])
+  if (!(await asked)) return false
+  const { mutate } = useSession.getState()
+  const done = await mutate(
+    'propertyId' in target
+      ? { op: 'deleteProperty', propertyId: target.propertyId }
+      : { op: 'delete', path: target.path, kind: target.kind },
+  )
+  if (!done) return false
+  const { bundled, cascade, retry } = done
+  offerUndo(
+    bundled ? [bundled.bundlePath] : [],
+    (undo) => notifyDeleted(target.title, undo, cascade, retry && (() => void mutate(retry))),
+    target.undoTo,
+  )
+  return true
+}

**Drive Group 6** (`group6(cdp)`; seeds through `ask(cdp, 'mutate', …)` on `~/Test`, `Collection A`; `restore()` resets `~/Test` after the run):

- [ ] `[g6 O-1] an option's menu reads Delete, and a delete nothing holds asks without a strip clause` — seed `addProperty` `{ label: 'Drive Choice', type: 'select', select_options: [{ key: 'Alpha', label: 'Alpha' }, { key: 'Beta', label: 'Beta' }] }`; open Settings → Properties → Drive Choice (the Option Picker Drive's `openEditor` path); `chooseNative(cdp, <Alpha's row>, 'Delete')` answers rows holding `Delete` and no `Remove`; the dialog asks `Delete “Alpha”?` with `The option is deleted from the property.` and a `Delete` button; pressing it leaves `Drive Choice`'s options `['Beta']` in `.nexus/properties.json`.
- [ ] `[g6 O-1] an option a page holds asks with its count` — `createPage Drive Held` in `Collection A/Set Alpha` seeded `{ [Drive Choice]: { kind: 'select', value: 'Beta' } }`; Delete on Beta asks `The option is deleted from the property and its value stripped from 1 Item.`; pressing Delete strips `Drive Choice` from `Drive Held.md`.
- [ ] `[g6 O-2] deleting a property nothing holds asks without "0 Items"` — seed `addProperty` `{ label: 'Drive Bare', type: 'text' }`; open its editor; `chooseNative(cdp, '[aria-label="Property Menu"]', 'Delete', { button: 'left' })`; the dialog asks `Delete “Drive Bare” everywhere?` with `It is removed from every collection; a restorable record lands in the nexus’s .trash folder.`; pressing Delete returns the pane to its list, `notice(cdp)` starts `Deleted “Drive Bare”`, and `bundles:list({ kind: 'trash' })` holds one property row titled `Drive Bare`.
- [ ] `[g6 O-4] a property restored after its name was taken says the name it took` — seed `addProperty` `{ label: 'Drive Bare', type: 'text' }` again; `openSettings(cdp, 'Trash')`, `chooseNative(cdp, trashRowEl('Drive Bare'), 'Restore')`; `notice(cdp)` includes `Restored “Drive Bare” as “Drive Bare (2)”`, and the registry holds `Drive Bare` and `Drive Bare (2)`.
- [ ] `[g6 —] the group leaves Collection A, the registry, and the Trash as it found them` — `deleteProperty` each seeded property through `mutate`, `deletePage` `Drive Held`, empty each bundle the group made with `permanentDelete` on, and reset `permanentDelete`; assert against start-of-group values: `Collection A`'s `properties`, `.nexus/properties.json`'s `order`, and `bundles:list({ kind: 'trash' })`'s length.

### Phase 8 — Option Identity

**GOAL:** Every Select, Multi-Select, and Status option carries a permanent id, values decode to it as Context values decode to Space ids, and every display reads the label off the option, while pages keep the word. Saved views, tiles, the Matrix filter, and the preview rules name options by id, so an option rename stops reaching configuration and rewrites only the pages holding the word; an option delete drops its id through the `gone` edit. One builder spells every property band's key, `<property>/<bucket>`, so collapsed groups are remembered per property and a grouped property's delete keeps folder collapses. Status options stop storing `group_id`, the option editor addresses options by id, and NexusOS is converted once by a throwaway script inside the checkpoint. It's a phase of its own because the value shape it changes reaches every option surface, and its head is shippable only once the conversion has run and the generator writes ids.

Builds on: P1's shared seed (`seedNexus`, `Core/Testing/definitions.ts`, which holds `STATUS_DEF` and the former `fixtures/registry.json` definitions) and its removal of the legacy hidden-group branches; P2's Title-as-text (`Core/Properties/value.ts:43` answers `{ kind: 'text' }`, `filter.ts`' title branch gone) and the seeds' move into `Core/Properties/registryProperty.ts`; P3's `typeDisplay.ts` and `displayLabels.ts`; P4's moves (`editList`/`stripList`/`Matcher` into `Core/Files/rootValues.ts`, `unregisteredMembers` and `valueEditRewrite` into `optionOps.ts`, the field-value module's rename); P5's `holderSchema` and index-read registration; P6's `putBack`; P7's ops (`editOption`, `renameOption`, `deleteOption`, `clearOption`, `replayProperty`), `askDeleteOption`, the `option:delete` action, the holders count (`countedChange` in `Core/Properties/properties.ts`, which the `property:holders` channel in `Core/Properties/handlers.ts` switches on), `useOptionEdit`'s `landed` over the slice's `mutate`, and `propertyWrite.ts`' removal; P7 leaves `optionCascade`'s label pair for this phase. Where a cite below names a HEAD line an earlier phase moved, the anchor is the function or test title and the phase that moved it.

**Task Order:** 8-1 → 8-2 → 8-3 → 8-4 → 8-5 → 8-6 → 8-7, then the Review Checkpoint with Task 8-8 (the conversion) last. This is the Findings' items 1, 2, 4, 6, 3 with 5, 8, the drive group, then 7 (*Departures From the Findings* gives why).

#### Task 8-1

**TASK:** Every option carries an `id`: a stored id reads as written, and an option stored without one answers to `opt_<its key, URI-encoded>` until the next write of its property's options stores it. The host mints `opt_<ULID>` in the seeds, at registration, and (until Task 8-5 hands it to the renderer) on an add. Status options stop carrying `group_id`, so the two option decoders become one, and the option dedupe holds each id once as it holds each label and key once: an option repeating an earlier id under its own label and key takes the id its key derives, and leaves only when that id is taken too.

**NOW:**
- **Two Decoders:** `selectOption` (`Core/Properties/properties.ts:122-132`) and `statusOption` (`:137-147`) decode the same fields, `statusOption` adding a required `group_id: statusGroupId` with no catch (`:144`), so a hand edit leaving it out sets the whole Status definition aside. `statusGroupId` (`:135`) is read by `statusGroup.id` (`:151`) and `group_id`. Both decoders end in `.transform(labelled)` (`:114-120`).
- **`group_id` Has No Reader:** `git grep -n "group_id" -- Core UIX Desktop ':!*.test.*'` answers only writers: `optionGroupsOf` stamps it on Select options (`:304`) and `withOptionGroups` strips it again (`:313`); `addOption` (`Core/Properties/optionModel.ts:35`) and `moveOption` (`:49`) write it; the two seeds (`properties.ts:317-342`, in `Core/Properties/registryProperty.ts` since P2) and `STATUS_DEF` (`Core/Testing/viewHarness.tsx:68,74`, in `Core/Testing/definitions.ts` since P1) hold it. `optionGlyph` finds an option's group by scanning `status_groups` (`Core/Properties/Cells/OptionChip.tsx:27-28`, its default glyph read from `typeDisplay.ts`' `chipOf` since P3).
- **Where an Option Gets Written:** `editStoredOptions` (`Core/Properties/optionOps.ts:59-67`) rebuilds a property's stored options through `labelled` (`:65`) and `uniqueOptionGroups` (`Core/Properties/validation.ts:76-90`); `mutateRegistry` writes an option array only when the op rebuilt it (`rebuiltOptions`, `Core/Properties/propertiesRegistry.ts:72-82`), so an untouched definition keeps its stored options byte for byte. A create writes the candidate whole (`:110`). `registerHeldOptions` adds an adopted word through `addOption(g, SELECT_GROUP, v, v)` (`optionOps.ts:154`, inside the `mutateRegistry` half P5 keeps). `withUniqueOptions` (`validation.ts:93-97`) answers the definition as it is when `validateOptionValues` passes, which compares labels and keys only.
- **Ids:** `mintPropertyId` (`Core/Nexus/ids.ts:41-43`) mints `prop_<ULID>`; `Core/Views/views.ts:5` already reaches `ids.ts` renderer-side, so the renderer can mint an option id in Task 8-5.

An option delete drops its id from every saved view, View Tile, the Matrix filter, and the preview rules through the `gone` edit, whose matcher also answers a bucket key the property scopes and whose orders now drop a gone id.

#### Task 8-4

**TASK:** `bandKey(propertyId, bucket, setId?)` in `Core/Views/views.ts` spells a property band's key once — `<property>/<bucket>`, under its Set's id when it sub-groups a Set — and the hidden keys, the pipeline's band keys, the Group pane's sub-group rows, and the `gone` matcher build through it, so collapsed groups are remembered per property as hidden groups already are. `clearBandKeys(keys, propertyId)` is the one strip of a property's band keys, so deleting the property a view groups by keeps its folder collapses; with RENAME gone since Task 8-3, the hidden and collapsed roles merge and `groupsOn` leaves.

**NOW:**
- **Two Spellings:** hidden keys are `hiddenBucketKey(level, propertyId, bucket)` → `<property>/<bucket>` or `sub/<property>/<bucket>` (`Core/Views/views.ts:307,314-315`); band keys are the bare bucket for a property band (`Core/Views/Pipeline/group.ts:250-253`, the loop variable named `key` though it holds a bucket), `subGroupKey(setId, bucket)` → `<set>/<bucket>` for a sub-band and `<set>/_ungrouped` for a Set's value-less tail (`:310-311,337,340`), the Set's id for a Set band, and `UNGROUPED` for the tail. `collapsed_groups` stores whatever band key was clicked (`Core/Views/Host/useViewHost.ts:149-155`), so a collapsed "Done" under one property collapses a "Done" under any property the view regroups by. Task 8-3's `gone` matcher spells `<property>/<id>` itself.
- **Who Builds and Who Matches:** the pipeline (`group.ts`) and the Group pane's preview (`Core/Views/Settings/GroupFrame.tsx:387,411`, keyed by option id since Task 8-2) build band keys; `useViewHost.ts:63,149-155`, `Core/Views/Bands/GroupBand.tsx:130`, `bandModel.ts:181`, and `Core/Views/Table/TableView.tsx:447` only hold and match the keys the pipeline built. Reassign and creation read a band's value (`bucketValueAt`, `Core/Views/Bands/bandRouter.ts:159-162`; `useViewInteractions.tsx:112,265`; `useViewCreation.ts:241`), never its key.
- **The Property Clear:** `CLEAR.hiddenKeys` strips through `clearHiddenBuckets(held, propertyId)` (`views.ts:377-385`, which P1 left taking the stored key list, its bare-`sub/` clause gone, leaving its two prefix tests); `CLEAR.bandKeys` (`Core/Nexus/configReach.ts:212-217`) empties every collapsed key when the view groups by the property — Set ids from an earlier structural grouping included — and drops every slash-holding key when it sub-groups by it, `groupsOn`'s last reader. `CLEAR.bandKeys` is the last handler to read `Handler`'s `view` argument (P1 dropped `hiddenKeys`' read of it); `GONE` already treats both roles alike.
- **The Test Helper:** `viewOn` (`Core/Testing/configSurfaces.ts:25-37`) seeds `hidden_groups` with a hand-spelled `` `${propertyId}/${value}` `` and `collapsed_groups: [value]`, the bare key.

- [ ] The listed tests pass; `OptionEditor.test.tsx`' kept menu, draft, heading, and drag cases pass on ids; `UIX/Menus/useListEdit`'s callers' tests (`AliasList`, `ExcludedDirectoriesRow`) pass unchanged.

- [ ] `npm run test -- engineGraph hostGraph` passes (`useOptionEdit.tsx` reaches `Nexus/ids.ts` renderer-side, as `views.ts` does).
- [ ] Run the gates.
- [ ] Check for unnecessary code or mistakes.

**Lines:** −11 production (+142 / −153). Tests about −160 for the popup's re-keying and −32 for the label race, about +25 written.

---
#### Task 8-6

**TASK:** The Benchmark generator writes option ids and no `group_id`, and the drives that already exist name options the way the app now does: every option op, holders count, value, filter operand, and option-carrying view they send names the option's id, every `add` carries a minted id, and the pins Task 8-3 and Task 8-5 make false are rewritten to what holds now.

**NOW:**
- **The Generator:** `definition(p)` (`.claude/scripts/make-benchmark-nexus.mjs:162-173`) writes Select options `{ key, label }` and Status options `{ key, label, color, group_id }`; its ids come from the seeded `plainId()` (`:90-104`), so a build stays reproducible. The `test` preset writes no option property (`:155`, `TEST ? [] : TYPES`).
- **The Metadata Drive** (`.claude/scripts/Metadata Drive/live-drive.mjs`, re-pointed to P7's ops): `statusGroups` stamps `group_id` (`:178-181`) and a Status create writes one by hand (`:876`); option values are built from words (`set('select', 'Doing')` and its kin at `:446-447,590-612,1019-1020`; `spaceValue`/`setValue` at `:506,843,845`); filter operands, saved views, and the Matrix filter name options by word (`:679-680,696-704,909-912,1062-1065`); option ops and counts name labels (`:684-685,733,788-789,848,921-938,953-963,979,1150-1159,1218`); pins assert the rename reach and the record's label pair: "an option rename rewrites the saved view, the View Tile, and the Matrix filter by label" (`:924-925`), "… and the view follows the label" (`:927-929`, `:1160-1162`), "an option removal strips the page and the view naming it" (`:932-934`), "an option rename record carries its key pairs and its label pair" (`:950-952`), and the casing pins "Select Is with another casing matches nothing" and its two kin (`:697,701,703`), which compare word operands. Its `optionsOf` helper (`:146`) reads stored options.
- **The Option Picker Drive** (`.claude/scripts/Option Picker Drive/live-drive.mjs`): its seed's `add`s carry no id (`:39`), its pages are seeded and set by word (`:44-45,164,214`), and its host-refusal case adds without an id (`:286`).
- **Other Drives:** `git grep -nE "kind: '(select|multiSelect)'|group_id|renameOption|clearOption|deleteOption|editOption" -- .claude/scripts` names two more: the Alias Drive adds its two options without an id (`Alias Drive/live-drive.mjs:80`, through P7's `editOption`), which Task 8-5's `add` refuses (`id: z.string().min(1)`), and the Archive Drive renames its Draft option by label (`Archive Drive/live-drive.mjs:391`, through P7's `renameOption { from, to }`), which Task 8-5's `{ optionId, label }` refuses.

**CHANGE**

- [ ] `make-benchmark-nexus.mjs`: one `option(value, extra)` builder writes `id: opt_<plainId()>`; Status options drop `group_id`.
- [ ] `drive-harness.mjs` exports one `optionId(def, label)`, answering an option's stored id or the id its key derives (`opt_<encodeURIComponent(key)>`, the app's rule for an option written without one), and one `mintOptionId()` (`opt_<ulid()>`, beside `mintPageId`); each drive hands `optionId` the definition it reads at the moment a value or op is sent (the Metadata Drive's `defOf(id)`, the Option Picker Drive's `defNamed(name)`), so every option value, operand, op, and count above resolves its words through the one helper, and every `add` sends `id: mintOptionId()`. +// Converts NexusOS's options and the saved views naming them to option ids, once. A second run writes nothing.
+import { copyFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, renameSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
+import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
+import { homedir } from 'node:os'
+import { basename, dirname, join } from 'node:path'
+
+const HOME = homedir()
+const NEXUS = join(HOME, 'NexusOS')
+const { monotonicFactory } = createRequire(join(HOME, 'The Studio/Projects/Project Pommora/package.json'))('ulidx')
+const nextUlid = monotonicFactory()
+
+const REGISTRY = '.nexus/properties.json'
+const IDEAS = 'Ideas/_pagecollection.json'
+const HOMEPAGE = '.nexus/interface/homepage/_tiles.json'
+const POMMORA = '.nexus/contexts/Projects/Pommora/_tiles.json'
+const FILES = [REGISTRY, IDEAS, HOMEPAGE, POMMORA]
+const STATUS = 'prop_01KWG2FPV0VP0D2W6BR5EK485P'
+const SET = '01KXQ7HKBZNGKT00VDF1F7X5ER'
+const DROPPED = new Set(['open', 'closed'])
+const OPTION_TYPES = new Set(['select', 'multiSelect', 'status'])
+const TEXT_OPS = new Set(['contains', 'does_not_contain', 'starts_with'])
+const COUNTS = { Status: 8, Tags: 3, Brand: 20, Concern: 5, Scale: 5, Color: 12, Version: 6 }
+const MINTED = /^opt_[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$/
+
+const fail = (why) => {
+  console.error(`STOP  ${why}`)
+  process.exit(1)
+}
+const sortKeys = (v) =>
+  Array.isArray(v) ? v.map(sortKeys)
+  : v && typeof v === 'object' ? Object.fromEntries(Object.keys(v).sort().map((k) => [k, sortKeys(v[k])]))
+  : v
+const stable = (v) => `${JSON.stringify(sortKeys(v), null, 2)}\n`
+const readAt = (dir, rel) => JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(dir, rel), 'utf8'))
+const optionsIn = (def) => (def.type === 'status' ? def.status_groups.flatMap((g) => g.options) : (def.select_options ?? []))
+
+// 1. The backup, first: each file copied once, so a later run keeps the copy of what NexusOS held before the first.
+const pad = (n) => String(n).padStart(2, '0')
+const d = new Date()
+const backups = readdirSync(HOME).filter((n) => /^NexusOS-Backup-\d{2}-\d{2}-\d{4}$/.test(n))
+if (backups.length > 1) fail(`more than one backup folder: ${backups.join(', ')}`)
+const BACKUP = join(HOME, backups[0] ?? `NexusOS-Backup-${pad(d.getMonth() + 1)}-${pad(d.getDate())}-${d.getFullYear()}`)
+for (const rel of FILES) {
+  const to = join(BACKUP, rel)
+  if (existsSync(to)) continue
+  mkdirSync(dirname(to), { recursive: true })
+  copyFileSync(join(NEXUS, rel), to)
+}
+const backup = Object.fromEntries(FILES.map((rel) => [rel, readAt(BACKUP, rel)]))
+for (const rel of FILES)
+  if (readFileSync(join(BACKUP, rel), 'utf8') !== stable(backup[rel])) fail(`${rel} isn't in Pommora's stable form, so a rewrite would change more than the conversion`)
+
+// 2. The ids: an option keeps a stored id and the rest are minted; Status's options lose group_id.
+const registry = readAt(NEXUS, REGISTRY)
+const ids = new Map()
+for (const [pid, def] of Object.entries(registry.defs)) {
+  if (!OPTION_TYPES.has(def.type)) continue
+  const byLabel = new Map()
+  for (const o of optionsIn(def)) {
+    if (!o.id) o.id = `opt_${nextUlid()}`
+    delete o.group_id
+    byLabel.set(o.label ?? o.key, o.id)
+  }
+  ids.set(pid, byLabel)
+}
+const status = ids.get(STATUS)
+
+// 3. The views: whole-value operands, sort and group orders, and Status's leftover collapses name option ids.
+const idOf = (pid, word, where) => {
+  const byLabel = ids.get(pid)
+  if ([...byLabel.values()].includes(word)) return word
+  return byLabel.get(word) ?? fail(`${where}: "${word}" names no option of ${pid}`)
+}
+const ordered = (holder, where) => {
+  if (holder && ids.has(holder.property_id) && Array.isArray(holder.order))
+    holder.order = holder.order.map((w) => idOf(holder.property_id, w, where))
+}
+const ruled = (node, where) => {
+  if (!node || typeof node !== 'object') return
+  if (Array.isArray(node.rules)) return node.rules.forEach((r) => ruled(r, where))
+  const def = registry.defs[node.property_id]
+  if (!ids.has(node.property_id) || (def.type !== 'multiSelect' && TEXT_OPS.has(node.op))) return
+  if (typeof node.value === 'string') node.value = idOf(node.property_id, node.value, where)
+  if (Array.isArray(node.values)) node.values = node.values.map((w) => idOf(node.property_id, w, where))
+}
+const collapsed = (keys) =>
+  keys.flatMap((k) => (DROPPED.has(k) ? [] : status.has(k) ? [`${STATUS}/${status.get(k)}`] : [k]))
+const viewsIn = (doc) =>
+  [...(doc.views ?? []), ...(doc.tiles ?? []).flatMap((t) => (t.views ?? []).map((v) => v?.config))].filter((v) => v && typeof v === 'object')
+
+const next = { [REGISTRY]: registry }
+for (const rel of [IDEAS, HOMEPAGE, POMMORA]) {
+  const doc = readAt(NEXUS, rel)
+  for (const v of viewsIn(doc)) {
+    const where = `${rel} "${v.name}"`
+    for (const c of v.sort ?? []) ordered(c, where)
+    ordered(v.group, where)
+    ordered(v.sub_group, where)
+    ruled(v.filter, where)
+    if (Array.isArray(v.collapsed_groups)) v.collapsed_groups = collapsed(v.collapsed_groups)
+  }
+  next[rel] = doc
+}
+
+// 4. The expectations, Walkthrough §Your Data written out against the backup: each converted file equals its backup with exactly these changes.
+const want = structuredClone(backup[REGISTRY])
+const seen = new Set()
+let total = 0
+for (const [pid, def] of Object.entries(want.defs)) {
+  if (!OPTION_TYPES.has(def.type)) continue
+  const theirs = optionsIn(next[REGISTRY].defs[pid])
+  if (COUNTS[def.label] !== theirs.length) fail(`${def.label} holds ${theirs.length} options, expected ${COUNTS[def.label]}`)
+  if (def.label === 'Status' && optionsIn(def).filter((o) => 'group_id' in o).length !== 8) fail('Status held other than eight group_ids')
+  optionsIn(def).forEach((o, i) => {
+    const id = theirs[i].id
+    if (o.id ? id !== o.id : !MINTED.test(id)) fail(`${def.label} "${o.label}" landed under ${id}`)
+    if (seen.has(id)) fail(`the id ${id} repeats`)
+    seen.add(id)
+    delete o.group_id
+    o.id = id
+    total++
+  })
+}
+if (total !== 59 || ids.size !== 7) fail(`${total} options across ${ids.size} properties, expected 59 across 7`)
+
+const S = (...labels) => labels.map((l) => status.get(l))
+const scoped = (...labels) => S(...labels).map((id) => `${STATUS}/${id}`)
+const viewAt = (doc, path, name) => {
+  const v = path.reduce((x, k) => x?.[k], doc)
+  return v?.name === name ? v : fail(`${path.join('.')} is "${v?.name}", expected "${name}"`)
+}
+const statusSort = (v) => v.sort.find((c) => c.property_id === STATUS)
+const ORDER = S('Active', 'Open', 'Paused', 'Awaiting', 'Complete', 'Closed', 'Archived', 'Revisit')
+const HOME_ORDER = S('Active', 'Open', 'Paused', 'Awaiting', 'Revisit', 'Complete', 'Closed', 'Archived')
+
+const ideas = structuredClone(backup[IDEAS])
+const table = viewAt(ideas, ['views', 0], 'Table')
+table.group.order = S('Active', 'Open', 'Awaiting', 'Revisit', 'Complete', 'Closed', 'Archived')
+statusSort(table).order = ORDER
+table.collapsed_groups = [SET, ...scoped('Archived', 'Paused', 'Closed', 'Complete')]
+const untitled = viewAt(ideas, ['views', 1], 'Untitled View')
+untitled.group.order = S('Active', 'Open', 'Paused', 'Archived', 'Awaiting', 'Closed', 'Revisit', 'Complete')
+untitled.collapsed_groups = scoped('Paused', 'Revisit', 'Closed')
+
+const homepage = structuredClone(backup[HOMEPAGE])
+for (const [i, name, op] of [[0, 'Active', 'is_not'], [1, 'Archive', 'is']]) {
+  const v = viewAt(homepage, ['tiles', 0, 'views', i, 'config'], name)
+  statusSort(v).order = HOME_ORDER
+  const rule = v.filter.rules.find((r) => r.property_id === STATUS)
+  if (rule?.op !== op) fail(`the homepage's "${name}" Status rule is ${rule?.op}, expected ${op}`)
+  rule.values = S('Complete', 'Closed', 'Archived', 'Revisit')
+}
+
+const pommora = structuredClone(backup[POMMORA])
+const ideasTile = viewAt(pommora, ['tiles', 2, 'views', 0, 'config'], 'Ideas')
+statusSort(ideasTile).order = ORDER
+ideasTile.collapsed_groups = [...scoped('Paused', 'Closed', 'Complete', 'Archived'), SET]
+
+for (const [rel, expected] of [[REGISTRY, want], [IDEAS, ideas], [HOMEPAGE, homepage], [POMMORA, pommora]])
+  if (stable(expected) !== stable(next[rel])) fail(`${rel} differs from Walkthrough §Your Data`)
+if (stable(next[REGISTRY]).includes('group_id')) fail('a group_id survived')
+
+// 5. The writes: only a file whose text changes, through a hidden temp file the watcher never reads.
+let written = 0
+for (const rel of FILES) {
+  const abs = join(NEXUS, rel)
+  const text = stable(next[rel])
+  if (readFileSync(abs, 'utf8') === text) continue
+  const tmp = join(dirname(abs), `.${basename(abs)}.conversion`)
+  writeFileSync(tmp, text)
+  renameSync(tmp, abs)
+  written++
+}
+
+// 6. Nothing in NexusOS names an option by its word any more.
+const VIEW_FILES = new Set(['_pagecollection.json', '_pageset.json', '_tiles.json'])
+const offenders = []
+const optionWord = (pid, w) => ids.has(pid) && typeof w === 'string' && !w.startsWith('opt_')
+const scan = (dir) => {
+  for (const e of readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
+    if (e.name === '.obsidian' || e.name === '.git') continue
+    const abs = join(dir, e.name)
+    if (e.isDirectory()) scan(abs)
+    else if (VIEW_FILES.has(e.name)) {
+      for (const v of viewsIn(JSON.parse(readFileSync(abs, 'utf8')))) {
+        const words = [
+          ...(v.sort ?? []).flatMap((c) => (c.order ?? []).filter((w) => optionWord(c.property_id, w))),
+          ...[v.group, v.sub_group].flatMap((g) => (g?.order ?? []).filter((w) => optionWord(g.property_id, w))),
+          ...[...(v.collapsed_groups ?? []), ...(v.hidden_groups ?? [])].filter((k) => [...ids.values()].some((m) => m.has(k))),
+        ]
+        const walk = (n) => {
+          if (!n || typeof n !== 'object') return
+          if (Array.isArray(n.rules)) return n.rules.forEach(walk)
+          if (!TEXT_OPS.has(n.op) || registry.defs[n.property_id]?.type === 'multiSelect')
+            words.push(...[n.value, ...(n.values ?? [])].filter((w) => optionWord(n.property_id, w)))
+        }
+        walk(v.filter)
+        if (words.length) offenders.push(`${abs.slice(NEXUS.length + 1)} "${v.name}": ${words.join(', ')}`)
+      }
+    }
+  }
+}
+scan(NEXUS)
+if (offenders.length) fail(`option words remain:\n  ${offenders.join('\n  ')}`)
+
+console.log(`backup ${BACKUP}\nwritten ${written}\n59 options, 8 group_ids stripped, the three view files verified, no option word left in NexusOS`)
```

#### Departures and Disclosures

##### Departures From the Findings

- **The Task Order Is 1, 2, 4, 6, 3 With 5, 8, the Drive, Then 7 (Order Line):** Findings item 3 (ops take ids) and item 5 (the popup's re-keying leaves) land in one task, Task 8-5, because the op's request shape and `useOptionEdit`'s calls compile together: an op taking an id while the editor still keys by label would need a label-to-id lookup inside the editor that the next task deletes. Item 4 (the rename reach) lands before item 6 (`bandKey`) because the rename block's tests and `CLEAR.bandKeys` read the bare collapsed keys `bandKey` retires; with RENAME gone first, Task 8-4 rewrites the keys, merges the two roles, and retires `groupsOn` in one place, and Task 8-3's `gone` matcher spells `<property>/<id>` inline for one task before reading it through `bandKey`. The remaining interim is Task 8-2's `labelledOption` (three calls) and `EditableOptionRows`' four `o.label` handles, which Task 8-5 rewrites; the line rule counts them once, in their final form.
- **`optionLabels` Becomes `optionIds` (Item 2):** the Findings had `optionLabels`' readers (`group.ts:199,219`, `sort.ts:87`) "read labels off options". They order buckets and rank values, which are ids now, so they list option ids; labels are read where something is shown (`optionLabel`). `optionLabels` keeps its last reader, the replay's label check, until Task 8-3 removes both.
- **The Option-Rename Record Loses `labels` (Item 4's `optionCascade`'s labels leave):** the record carried the label pair for two readers, the configuration reach and `rekeyOptions`' relabel by label. With the reach gone, keeping the pair would leave an id-addressed rename relabelling its option by label, so `rekeyOptions` takes the relabel as an argument (`{ optionId, label }` or `{ value_format }`) and the record keeps its key pairs alone. A record already on disk holding `labels` decodes without them; no Nexus holds one (*§Verified at HEAD › Crash Recovery*). The Metadata Drive's record pin follows (Task 8-6).
- **`optionCascade`'s Label Pair Becomes the Deleted Option's Id (Item 4):** the pair's `null` second half carried two facts, "this is a delete" and "stop at a skipped file", and its labels fed the reach. With the reach gone a cascade needs only whether it deletes and what, so `removed?: string` (the option's id) states both once; P7 left the pair for this phase on the same reasoning (its *Departures*, "`OptionChange` Is Excluded").
- **`bandKey(propertyId, bucket, setId?)` in Place of a Union Argument (Item 6):** the Findings' signature also took `{ kind: 'set' }` and `{ kind: 'tail' }` arms, which would answer their own argument (a Set band's key is its id) or a constant (`UNGROUPED`). The function spells only what varies, the property band, and Set and tail bands keep the keys they have. A Set's value-less sub-tail is `bandKey(property, UNGROUPED, set)`, which retires `subGroupKey`.
- **`clearHiddenBuckets` Becomes `clearBandKeys(keys, propertyId)` (Item 6):** it strips collapsed keys as well as hidden ones now, both of them band keys `bandKey` spells, so its name follows; P1 already gave it the key list. The hidden and collapsed roles then merge into the one `bandKeys` role in Task 8-4, since CLEAR and GONE treat them alike once RENAME leaves, and "bucket key" keeps its one meaning, `group.ts`' `bucketKey` for a row's bucket.
- **The Gone Edit Strips Orders (Item 4):** GONE kept `sort[].order` and the groupings' `order`, while today's option delete stripped them through RENAME. Leaving a deleted option's id in an order would keep a dead id in the view's JSON (inert, since `group.ts`' live-bucket rule and `OptionOrderList`' row filter skip it), so `goneOrder` (RENAME's `scopedOrder`, re-aimed) strips it for any gone id on the order's property. Spaces and Sets never sit in an order (Context sorts and groups by nothing, `sort.ts:106-108`), so only options meet it.
- **The Gone Matcher Is Property-Scoped for Bucket Keys:** two properties' options written without ids derive the same id from the same key (`opt_Done` under Status and under another Select), and a bucket key names its property, so the matcher answers a key ending in `/<property>/<id>` or equal to `<property>/<id>`, not any key holding the id. The head-or-whole rule (`isAtOrUnder`) stays for Set ids and operands.
- **Duplicate Option Ids Are Dropped as Duplicate Labels Are (Item 1, Left Open):** an option block copied by hand or by an agent keeps its id, and two options under one id would decode as one and write each other's key on a pick. `uniqueOptionGroups` already keeps the first of any repeated label or key; it now keeps the first of any repeated id too, and `withUniqueOptions`' fast path checks ids (+4 lines).

A word no option holds draws the default, as before. An accident fixed. **Recommended:** take it.

#### Task 9-1

**TASK:** Move the open's Context replay from before the seed walk into the genuine-open block, after `seedContentIndex`, `oweSeen`, and `sweepFileHistory`, ahead of the property replay, under a catch that logs, so a throwing replay leaves the walk, the seed, and the settle done.

**NOW:** `openNexusSequence` (`Core/Nexus/handlers.ts:57-118`) calls `await replayPendingRename(root)` at `:86`, on every open and re-point, after `ctx.openStores` (`:85`) and before `readNexus` (`:89`) and `seedContentIndex` (`:108`), with no catch: `relocate` can throw (`Core/Contexts/contextCascade.ts:312-313,348`), and a throw there skips the walk, the seed, the property replay, and the settle after `openStores` already ran. Its sweep reads `queryMembers(…) ?? nexusCorpus(root)` (`contextCascade.ts:72`), so before the seed it walks the corpus. `replaySchemaCascade(root)` runs at `:111` inside `if (root !== priorRoot)` (`:87`), after the seed, and catches inside itself (`Core/Properties/replaySchemaCascade.ts:24-35`), since it also answers P7's `replayProperty` op with a fault.

**Every Way a Root Becomes the Open Nexus** (re-verified at HEAD; the orchestrator's item 5):

| Path | Entry | `priorRoot` | Genuine Block |
|---|---|---|---|
| Launch restore | `Desktop/main.ts:387` → `openNexusSequence(…, true)` | `null` (no session yet) | Runs |
| Choose / Open Recent | `nexus:choose` (`handlers.ts:140-145`), `nexus:openPath` (`:148-156`), `openNexusPath` (`Desktop/main.ts:180-187`) → `adoptNexus` | Another root, or `null` | Runs |

| Nexus rename | `nexus:rename` (`handlers.ts:159-170`) → `adoptNexus(ctx, newRoot, false)` | The old root | Runs (`latchRecord` gates only `runOpenLedger`, `:101`) |

The block is skipped only for a same-root re-adopt. That root's session was opened by an earlier `openNexusSequence` in this process that passed its config read, and the first such open of the root ran the block (its `priorRoot` was null or another root), so any note present at the re-adopt was written by this process's own ops after that replay, whose replies already carry their Try Again (`renamed`, `Core/Nexus/mutate.ts:68-77`; P7's `retry` for property records). ##### Behavior Changes and Disclosures

- **A Context Rename Refused at Its Title Commit Moves Nothing:** today the folder moves, the files cascade, and the reversal sweeps them back, appending "Couldn’t update N Items." when the reversal misses files; now nothing moves and the refusal reads alone. A folder that can't move refuses with nothing renamed, as today. If its title can't go back either, the Context shows its new title with no Spaces until the next open moves the folder (H-8's double failure, which needs a damaged Contexts list mid-op).
- **Re-Adopting the Open Nexus No Longer Retries an Owed Context Rename (LC-50):** choosing the Nexus already open re-ran the Context replay; it now runs only on a genuine open, as the property replay already did. The rename's own notice keeps its Try Again (`renamed`). One rule for both replays.
- **An Open Whose Context Replay Throws Completes (LC-48):** the walk, seed, property replay, settle, repair sweep, and sync start run. An accident fixed.
- **The Open's Ledger Reads the Tree Before the Context Replay:** in the crash window between a title commit and the folder move, the open's seed walk lists the Context without its Spaces, `runOpenLedger` latches that tree, and the settle's walk restores them before the window shows the Nexus. The ledger's next open sees those Spaces' ids as present again; nothing re-mints, since no id is duplicated.
- **The Context Replay Sweeps Through the Index:** after the seed, `queryMembers` answers, so the replay opens only the pages holding the key instead of every page in the corpus. No visible change.

### Phase 10 — One Finder

**GOAL:** Every rename, delete, count, and strip finds its pages from the content index and its Spaces from the tree through one finder, `findHolders` in `Core/Index/keyHolders.ts`, whose doc comment states the one rule: a property reaches the pages of Collections and the Archive, a Context tag reaches any page, and both reach every Space that holds them. Every sweep writes pages and Space sidecars alike through `sweepGovernedRoots(files, plan)`, which dispatches each file by its basename, so the sidecar arm's disk scan, `spaceArm`, `sweepMembers`, `governedReach`, `confirmedKeyHolders`, `keyedHolders`, the delete snapshot's Space loop, and the restore routines' hand-rolled Space loops leave. A finder read answers which keys each holder holds and its values in the same pass that confirms it, and the restore routines report the files they couldn't update as a warning instead of ignoring them.

**Builds On:** P4's `Core/Nexus/governedSweep.ts` (moved from `Core/Properties`, beside `governedRoot.ts`, which took `governedRoot`, `changedKeys`, and `rewriteRaw` from it); P7's `Core/Properties/unassignProperty.ts` (from `removeProperty.ts`), `Core/Trash/trashedCopies.ts` (from `holdings.ts`), `unsweptLine` in `Core/Nexus/entities.ts`, and `refillValues` beside `sweepRootsById`; P8's option ops addressed by option id; P9's list-first Context rename (note → `commitTitle` → `relocate` → cascade, with the in-op revert) and its one post-seed replay. Every HEAD cite below is at `c11a312f3`; a line an earlier phase moved is anchored by its function and that phase.

**Task Order:** 10-1 (Findings item 2), 10-2 (items 1, 3's candidate half, and 4's engine), 10-3 (item 1's `read: 'values'` and 3's holder half), 10-4 (items 4's restore loops and 5), 10-5 (the drive). The Findings' order puts the leaves (3) before the one writer (4); the sweep can take a Space path only once it dispatches by basename, and no plan can drop its `sidecars` arm until the finder hands it Space paths, so the finder and the writer land in one task and the `sidecars` arm leaves in one stroke (*§Departures From the Findings*).

+export type Reach = 'governed' | { collection: string } | 'anywhere'
+
+/** A folder an op moved ahead of its sweep, root-relative. */
+export type Moved = { from: string; to: string }
+
+export type HolderQuery = {
+  keys: readonly string[]
+  reach: Reach
+  title?: string
+  id?: string
+  moved?: Moved
+}
+
+/** A holder a finder read: the id `byId` addresses it by, the query keys it holds, and their values as written, or null when it couldn't be read. */
+export type Held = { file: string; id: string | null; keys: string[]; values: Json | null }
+
+export type Holders = { pages: string[]; spaces: string[]; held: Held[] }
+
+/** The pages among `rels`, or among the whole corpus before the index is ready, that `reach` holds, as absolute paths. */
+export async function pagesInReach(
+  root: string,
+  tree: NexusTree,
+  rels: readonly string[] | null,
+  reach: Reach,
+): Promise<string[]> {
+  const files = (rels ?? (await nexusCorpus(root))).map((rel) => join(root, rel))
+  if (reach === 'anywhere') return files
+  const only = reach === 'governed' ? undefined : reach.collection
+  const archive = archiveReach(tree, only && relative(root, only))
+  const folders = [
+    ...(only === undefined ? collectionFolders(root, tree) : [only]),
+    ...(archive === null ? [] : [join(root, archive)]),
+  ]
+  return files.filter((abs) => folders.some((folder) => abs.startsWith(`${folder}/`)))
+}
+
+const sidecarAt = (root: string, rel: string, moved?: Moved): string =>
+  join(
+    root,
+    moved && isAtOrUnder(rel, moved.from) ? `${moved.to}${rel.slice(moved.from.length)}` : rel,
+    SPACE_SIDECAR,
+  )
+
+/** The sidecar of each Space the tree holds that `holds` answers for, at the folder `moved` sent it to when the tree still lists the one it left. */
+export const spaceFiles = (
+  root: string,
+  tree: NexusTree,
+  holds: (space: SpaceNode) => boolean,
+  moved?: Moved,
+): string[] =>
+  tree.contexts.flatMap((g) => g.spaces.filter(holds).map((s) => sidecarAt(root, s.path, moved)))
+
+/**
+ * The pages and Spaces holding `keys[0]`: pages from the content index (the corpus before it's ready), Spaces from the tree. A property's key means something only where a schema governs it, so `governed` reaches the pages of Collections and the Archive, and `{ collection }` one Collection's and its Archive's; a Context tag means something on any page, so `anywhere` reaches every one. Both of those reach every Space holding the key, every Space whose row order lists `id`, and every Space the tree couldn't read, which may hold anything. `title` narrows a Context key's pages to those naming that Space, and `moved` points a Space under a folder the op moved ahead of the tree.
+ *
+ * With `read`, each file is read once: `held` lists each one holding a key or that couldn't be read, with the keys the index last read it holding, and `pages` and `spaces` leave out a holder no id addresses, which a strip passes over since no restore could put its value back.
+ */
+export async function findHolders(
+  root: string,
+  q: HolderQuery,
+  read?: 'values',
+): Promise<Holders> {
+  const tree = await liveTreeOf(root)
+  const title = q.title === undefined ? undefined : exactTitle(q.title)
+  const rels = q.keys.map((key) => queryMembers(key, title))
+  const pages = await pagesInReach(root, tree, rels[0], q.reach)
+  const [key] = q.keys
+  const store = parseContextKey(key) === null ? 'values' : 'contextKeys'
+  const holds = (s: SpaceNode): boolean =>
+    Object.hasOwn(s[store] ?? {}, key) || (q.id !== undefined && !!s.rowOrder?.includes(q.id))
+  const spaces =
+    typeof q.reach === 'string'
+      ? [
+          ...spaceFiles(root, tree, holds, q.moved),
+          ...(tree.unreadable ?? []).flatMap((u) =>
+            u.kind === 'space' ? [sidecarAt(root, u.path, q.moved)] : [],
+          ),
+        ]
+      : []
+  if (!read) return { pages, spaces, held: [] }
+  const listed = rels.map((r) => r && new Set(r))
+  const { byId } = await nexusPages(root, tree)
+  const held: Held[] = []
+  const heldOut = new Set<string>()
+  for (const file of [...pages, ...spaces]) {
+    const text = await readTextOrNull(file)
+    const raw =
+      text === null ? null : isMarkdownFile(file) ? splitFrontmatter(text) : parseJsonObject(text)
+    const rel = relative(root, file)
+    const keys = q.keys.filter((k, i) => (raw ? Object.hasOwn(raw, k) : !!listed[i]?.has(rel)))
+    if (raw && !keys.length) continue
+    const id = raw ? rootId(file, raw) : undefined
+    const addressed = addressable(byId, id) ? id : null
+    if (raw && addressed === null) heldOut.add(file)
+    held.push({ file, id: addressed, keys, values: raw && Object.fromEntries(keys.map((k) => [k, raw[k]])) })
+  }
+  const kept = (file: string): boolean => !heldOut.has(file)
+  return { pages: pages.filter(kept), spaces: spaces.filter(kept), held }
+}

#### Departures and Disclosures

##### Departures From the Findings

- **Task Order (Findings Order 2, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6):** the sweep can't take a Space sidecar path until it dispatches by basename, and no plan can drop `sidecars` until the finder hands it Space paths, so the finder and the writer land together in 10-2 and the `sidecars` arm leaves in one stroke; `keyedHolders`, existing code, survives one task into 10-3 rather than a loosened `SweepPlan` being written for one task.
- **`Holders` Carries a `held` List, Not a Map by Id:** the Findings' `values?: ReadonlyMap<string, Record<string, unknown>>` keyed by id can't serve the rename clash, which counts files outside the Archive, ID-less pages among them (`keyHolders.ts:18-22`), and an unreadable page the index lists under both keys (`keyHolders.test.ts:124-139`). Each `Held` names its file, the id `byId` addresses it by, the query keys it holds (the index's when it can't be read), and its values; the first key names the candidates and the rest are read along, so the clash reads the old key's holders only. `heldValues` states the by-id value filing once for the delete and Remove, and P11's capture fills an unreadable holder's `values` from the index into the same field.
- **`HolderQuery` Gains `id`:** `withoutOrderId` drops a deleted property's or Context's id from every Space's `$order` (`spaceSidecar.ts:84-89`, read at `deleteProperty.ts:144` and `contextCascade.ts:141`), which HEAD's full scan reached; a key-only Space rule would leave the id in the order of a Space that orders but doesn't hold it. `id` adds the Spaces whose `rowOrder` lists it, which also keeps the delete's count equal to HEAD's.
- **Unreadable Spaces Are Candidates:** HEAD's scan filed a permission-denied sidecar as skipped on every property and Context sweep, so the op owed it; the tree omits that Space and lists it in `tree.unreadable`. `findHolders` includes every Space the tree lists unreadable, so a Space that held the key during the change still makes it owed. The connection cascades, which HEAD read only when another Space answered their rewrite, take tree Spaces alone.
- **The Connection Cascades Take the Finder's Halves, Not `findHolders`:** the Findings name `cascade.ts:129` as a finder consumer, but `deleteCascade` and `renameCascade` find pages by mention (`queryMentions`), not by key. They read `pagesInReach` (the one page reach and corpus fallback) and `spaceFiles` (the one Space half) with their own rewrite as the test, in place of `governedReach` and `spaceArm`; `findHolders` composes the same two.
- **A Rename Finds Before Its List Step:** Context and Space renames run outside the settle's turn (`mutate.ts:241,247`), and a Context-list title change can fall to a walk (`fileEvents.ts:476-486`); a walk between P9's `commitTitle` and `relocate` would read the Context's new title over its old folder and drop its Spaces from the tree. `titleHolders` runs before the note and the list step, while the tree lists the Spaces at their old folder, and `moved` points them at the new one; a finder that throws then leaves no note written for nothing.
- **The Replay Commits Before It Moves, and Re-Reads the Tree Instead of Using `moved`:** the Findings have the replay arm rebase through `moved`. After a crash between P9's `commitTitle` and `relocate`, the open's tree reads the Context's Spaces from the folder its new title names (`readNexus.ts:254-255`), which doesn't exist yet, so it holds none of them and there's nothing to rebase; and P9's replay moves the folder before it commits, so a crash between the note and the commit would re-read the tree under the old title's folder, already moved. The Context arm commits an uncommitted title first, as the live op does, and follows its folder move with `await refreshTree(root)`, which installs because `openSession` set the root (`handlers.ts:65-67`), before it finds; P11A's `finishContext` re-reads the tree at the same point.
- **`sweepGovernedRoots` Drops `root`:** its only reader was the sidecar arm's `spaceSidecars(root)`; every call loses its first argument.
- **`SweepPlan` Is `{ raw; text? }`:** every text plan that reaches a Space already had a Space rewrite beside it (the property rename's `rekeyHeld`, the Context rename's `rekeyContext` or `retitleSpace`, the re-spell's and `repairLanded`'s `spaceMoved`, the scrub's sidecar reconcile), so one optional field replaces the union and the `sidecars` arm.
- **`spaceSidecars`' Comment States the Asset Migration's Reason:** the Findings rewrite it "to the finder's rule and its move rebase", but after 10-3 its one caller is the asset migration (`assetMigrate.ts:117`), which reports sidecars it can't read; the finder's rule lives at `findHolders`.
- **Take Along: The Trashed-Copy Refill Lands Through the Live Refill's Reconcile:** the orchestrator relayed P12's finding that `refillTrashed` landed recorded Link values unreconciled while `refillValues` reconciles them; folding the trashed-copy loop into the sweep is where the two meet, so `refillValues`' rewrite becomes `refillOf(def, frozen)` and both refills land through it. P12's Trash parking builds on `refillTrashed(root, links, defs, frozen)` as this phase leaves it.
- **`SpaceNode.contextKeys` Is Optional:** absent when the sidecar holds no Context key, as `values` is.
- **`seedSpaceSidecar` Registers Its Context:** "sweep tests seed Spaces through the tree" reads as the one test seed registering the Context when the list doesn't name it, since the tree reads only registered Contexts' Spaces.

LC-48 carries it beside the Space files: **Recommended:** take it, since a restore otherwise refuses over one page while every Space file it misses only warns.
- **A Restore Counts Refused Files Too:** an Unknown page or a sidecar that won't parse is left byte-identical by every sweep; a property sweep leaves it silent since a retry reads it no better, while a restore, which nothing retries, now reports it through `unwritten`. `repairLanded` already counted a corrupt sidecar; the scrub's and the refill's refused files, and `repairLanded`'s refused pages, now warn too.
- **A Trashed Copy Takes a Refilled Link Value as a Live Page Would:** a value naming a page that's gone since stays out of the trashed copy, and one the definition spells differently lands in its written spelling, where both landed as recorded; an accident of the two refills diverging, fixed with the fold.
- **A Context Rename Reaches a Loose Page and a Property Rename Doesn't, by Stated Rule (G-2, Nathan's Reading):** unchanged in effect; it's now one rule in one doc comment.
- **One Hold-Out for Every Strip:** `deleteCascade`'s Space arm and the property delete's Space strip hold out a Space no id addresses (none, or one two files claim), as their page arms and `sweepRootsById` already did; only a hand copy inside `.nexus/contexts`, or a sidecar whose id was removed by hand, makes one.
- **A Space's Blank Value Isn't Filed in a Delete's Trash Entry:** pages never filed one (`keyHolders.ts:59`); Spaces did (`deleteProperty.ts:83`). A restore has nothing to put back for a blank value either way.
- **A Space Under a Context Folder the Context List Doesn't Name Is No Longer Swept:** HEAD's folder scan reached every folder under `.nexus/contexts`; the tree holds only registered Contexts' Spaces, and nothing displays an unregistered one.
- **A Re-Spell or Link Strip No Longer Reads an Unreadable Space Sidecar When Another Space Answered:** HEAD's all-or-nothing arm read every sidecar once any tree Space answered, counting an unreadable one into the warning; the cascades now read the Spaces that answer.
- **I-035's Event Order (Findings Item 6):** the Context rename's order is now note → find → list → folder → files; P18 rewrites I-035's event-order sentence to it, and its defect (pages already tagged with the new name stay unlinked until re-read) stays open (LC-35).
- **Risk Kept From the Findings:** an outside Space edit not yet settled is missed until it settles, as an outside page edit already is through the index.
