### Phase 11A — One Note per Item: The Notes and the Renames

**GOAL:** Every property, Context, and Space keeps its own entry in one device-local notes file, `.nexus/.owed.json`, and every rename, format change, property delete, and option change runs through one runner, `runNoted`: it refuses a name another item still owes, writes its note, takes its list step, and sweeps, refusing with nothing changed when the note or the list step can't land, so unfinished work on one item never blocks or unprotects another. A name still owed is refused at every property, Context, and Space create and rename through one check, and one argument-less Try Again runs the same finishing pass the open runs. The property delete and the option delete take their list step right after the note (B-2), landed here with the notes rather than on the slot they replace. The two one-slot journals, their shared slot, both replays, and the four Try Again forms leave. Phase 11B moves the Context and Space deletes and Remove onto the notes. Builds on P6 (`putBackEntries` as the one put-back), P7 (every property change is a `mutate` op answering `MutateReply`; the interim `replayProperty` op and `retry` transport; `addProperty` as one schema-lock hold; `confirmDelete` as the one delete flow, the property delete's included; the counting module in `Core/Nexus/entities.ts`), P8 (option ids; option ops take `optionId`; `resolveOption` answering `{ def, option }`; `rekeyOptions` taking a `Rekey` change), P9 (the Context rename's list-first order with H-8's in-op revert; both replays in the genuine-open block after the seed, each under its own catch), and P10 (`findHolders(root, q, 'values')` in `Core/Index/keyHolders.ts` answering `{ pages, spaces, held }` with one `Held` `{ file, id, keys, values }` per holder, `heldValues`, `rootId`, `deletePlan` answering `{ holders, plan }`, its `moved` rebase, `SpaceNode.contextKeys`, `titleHolders` finding a rename's files before its note, and every arm writing through `sweepGovernedRoots(files, { raw, text? })` with no `root`).

**Anchors:** HEAD is `c11a312f3` (code identical to `3c6afcabb`). A `path:line` cite is HEAD's; where P1–P10 moved or reshaped a line, the anchor is the function or test title and the phase that reshaped it. Where an AFTER names a P7–P10 symbol (an op's request fields, `findHolders`' answer, `optionCascade`'s post-P8 parameters), the landed spelling governs and the AFTER's intent is what lands; the executor reads each such site before editing it.

+// The notes file: one entry per property, Context, or Space that still owes work, keyed by its id, each holding the old names files may still carry. A change writes its entry before anything else and refuses when it can't; the entry clears once nothing is owed.
+
+import { fail, ok, type Result } from '../Contract/result'
+import { readAppFile, updateNexusFile } from '../Files/atomicWrite'
+import { memberKey } from '../Files/rootValues'
+import { same } from '../Files/stableJson'
+import { normalizeTitle } from '../Paths/caseFold'
+import { OWED_REL } from '../Paths/nexusPaths'
+import { join } from '../Paths/posix'
+import type { CascadeReport } from './cascade'
+import { type ConfigReach, reachReport } from './configReach'
+
+/** Each name in `rename` becomes the current name wherever a file still holds it; each in `strip` leaves. */
+export type Owed = { rename?: string[]; strip?: string[] }
+export type PropertyEntry = Owed & {
+  kind: 'property'
+  options?: Record<string, Owed>
+  unassigned?: string[]
+}
+export type ContextEntry = Owed & { kind: 'context'; bundle?: string }
+export type SpaceEntry = Owed & { kind: 'space'; contextId: string; bundle?: string }
+export type Entry = PropertyEntry | ContextEntry | SpaceEntry
+export type Notes = Record<string, Entry>
+
+/** Where a name lives: a property's keys, a Context's titles, a Space's titles inside its Context, or one property's option words. */
+export type Owner =
+  | { kind: 'property' }
+  | { kind: 'context' }
+  | { kind: 'space'; contextId: string }
+  | { kind: 'option'; propertyId: string }
+/** A name a create or rename lands on, and the item landing there, whose own owed names never refuse it. */
+export type Landing = { owner: Owner; name: string; except?: string }
+
+export const OWED = fail('owed', 'An earlier change hasn’t reached every file yet.')
+
+const notesFile = (root: string): string => join(root, OWED_REL)
+
+// Only this module writes the file and it never syncs, so it reads as written; a corrupt one is set aside by `updateNexusFile`.
+export const readNotes = async (root: string): Promise<Notes> =>
+  ((await readAppFile(notesFile(root))) as Notes | null) ?? {}
+
+/** Every name in `parts` once, or nothing when there are none, as an entry stores a part. */
+export const distinct = (...parts: (readonly string[] | undefined)[]): string[] | undefined => {
+  const all = parts.flatMap((p) => p ?? [])
+  return all.length ? [...new Set(all)] : undefined
+}
+
+const owes = (o: Owed | undefined): boolean => !!(o?.rename?.length || o?.strip?.length)
+
+const owesAnything = (e: Entry): boolean =>
+  owes(e) ||
+  (e.kind === 'property' &&
+    (!!e.unassigned?.length || Object.values(e.options ?? {}).some(owes)))
+
+/** Whether `e` still owes a rename. Pages under its old name weren't candidates for any sweep since, so an option part, a Remove's Collection, or a Space under it settles only once the rename lands (H-1). */
+export const owesRename = (e: Entry | undefined): boolean => !!e?.rename?.length
+
+/** Edits `id`'s entry under the file's own lock, dropping one that owes nothing; answers the entry as it stood, or the refusal naming the file. */
+export async function editNote(
+  root: string,
+  id: string,
+  edit: (e: Entry | undefined) => Entry | undefined,
+): Promise<Result<Entry | undefined>> {
+  let prior: Entry | undefined
+  const written = await updateNexusFile(
+    notesFile(root),
+    (cur) => {
+      const { [id]: held, ...rest } = cur as Notes
+      prior = held
+      const next = edit(held)
+      if (same(next ?? null, held ?? null)) return null
+      return next && owesAnything(next) ? { ...rest, [id]: next } : rest
+    },
+    true,
+  )
+  return written.ok ? ok(prior) : written
+}
+
+export const propertyNote = (e: Entry | undefined): PropertyEntry =>
+  e?.kind === 'property' ? e : { kind: 'property' }
+
+export const owedRename = (o: Owed, from: string, to: string): Owed => ({
+  rename: distinct([...(o.rename ?? []), from].filter((n) => n !== to)),
+  strip: o.strip,
+})
+/** Every owed name and, for a delete, the current one move into `strip`; Clear passes no current name, since its own word is never owed (H-2, H-3). */
+export const owedDelete = (o: Owed, current?: string): Owed => ({
+  rename: undefined,
+  strip: distinct(o.strip, o.rename, current === undefined ? [] : [current]),
+})
+export const owedRestore = (o: Owed): Owed => ({
+  rename: distinct(o.rename, o.strip),
+  strip: undefined,
+})
+/** `o` once a sweep that missed nothing has reached `swept`. */
+export const owedSwept = (o: Owed, swept: readonly string[]): Owed => ({
+  rename: distinct(o.rename?.filter((n) => !swept.includes(n))),
+  strip: distinct(o.strip?.filter((n) => !swept.includes(n))),
+})
+
+export function withOption(
+  e: PropertyEntry,
+  optionId: string,
+  edit: (o: Owed) => Owed,
+): PropertyEntry {
+  const { [optionId]: part, ...rest } = e.options ?? {}
+  const next = edit(part ?? {})
+  const options = owes(next) ? { ...rest, [optionId]: next } : rest
+  return { ...e, options: Object.keys(options).length ? options : undefined }
+}
+
+/** Whether an item other than `except` still owes `name` within its owner, so no create or rename may land on it: the work still due would land there too. Option words compare as written; every other name folds case. */
+export function owedName(notes: Notes, { owner, name, except }: Landing): boolean {
+  const fold = owner.kind === 'option' ? memberKey : normalizeTitle
+  const scope: [string, Owed][] =
+    owner.kind === 'option'
+      ? Object.entries(propertyNote(notes[owner.propertyId]).options ?? {})
+      : Object.entries(notes).filter(
+          ([, e]) =>
+            e.kind === owner.kind &&
+            (e.kind !== 'space' || (owner.kind === 'space' && e.contextId === owner.contextId)),
+        )
+  return scope.some(
+    ([id, o]) => id !== except && [...(o.rename ?? []), ...(o.strip ?? [])].some((n) => fold(n) === fold(name)),
+  )
+}
+
+/** A restore turns what its delete never reached back into renames to the restored name, so those files keep their values (H-4); an item that owes no strip writes nothing. */
+export async function restoreNote(root: string, id: string): Promise<Result<unknown>> {
+  if (!(await readNotes(root))[id]?.strip) return ok(undefined)
+  return editNote(root, id, (e) => e && { ...e, ...owedRestore(e) })
+}
+
+/** A many-file change's report, marked owed while it left files for Try Again. */
+export const owedReport = (reach: ConfigReach): CascadeReport => ({
+  ...reachReport(reach),
+  ...(reach.skipped ? { owed: true as const } : {}),
+})
+
+/** A many-file change on `id`, in its one order: refused while another item owes a name it lands on, then its note, its list step, and its sweep. A refused note or list step changes nothing, the entry put back as it stood; a sweep that missed nothing settles the entry, unless the entry `under` names still owes a rename. */
+export async function runNoted<T>(
+  root: string,
+  id: string,
+  change: {
+    lands?: readonly Landing[]
+    note: (e: Entry | undefined) => Entry
+    list: () => Promise<Result<T>>
+    sweep: (listed: T, prior: Entry | undefined) => Promise<ConfigReach>
+    settle: (e: Entry, listed: T) => Entry | undefined
+    under?: string
+  },
+): Promise<Result<{ listed: T; cascade: CascadeReport }>> {
+  const notes = await readNotes(root)
+  if (change.lands?.some((l) => owedName(notes, l))) return OWED
+  const prior = await editNote(root, id, change.note)
+  if (!prior.ok) return prior
+  const listed = await change.list()
+  if (!listed.ok) {
+    await editNote(root, id, () => prior.value)
+    return listed
+  }
+  const reach = await change.sweep(listed.value, prior.value)
+  const held = change.under === undefined ? undefined : notes[change.under]
+  if (!reach.skipped && !owesRename(held)) await editNote(root, id, (e) => e && change.settle(e, listed.value))
+  return ok({ listed: listed.value, cascade: owedReport(reach) })
+}

A page an owed rename never reached reaches the Trash with the value it holds under its old key (LC-10's reach, which Task 11B-1 extends to unreadable pages), and each holder is read once per key it holds, which for a delete owing no rename is once.

+// The one finishing pass, at the open and on Try Again: Context entries under the Contexts lock, then Space entries, then property entries under the schema lock, the notes file's own lock innermost and never nested; each entry under a catch that logs, so one that throws costs only itself. Every arm re-derives from the lists as they read now: a name a live entity holds now is skipped and dropped, and an entity gone takes its owed renames with it.
+
+import { errText } from '../Contract/result'
+import { readRegistry, serializeSchemaOp } from '../Properties/propertiesRegistry'
+import { removeFromRegistry, renameSweep } from '../Properties/registryProperty'
+import { deletePlan, stripProperty } from '../Properties/deleteProperty'
+import { dropOptionFromDef, optionCascade } from '../Properties/optionOps'
+import { collectionFolders } from './governedSweep'
+import { optionsOf, type PropertyDefinition } from '../Properties/properties'
+import { findOption } from '../Properties/propertyValue'
+import { memberKey } from '../Files/rootValues'
+import type { TrashDeps } from '../Trash/discard'
+import type { CascadeReport } from './cascade'
+import type { ConfigReach } from './configReach'
+import { liveTreeOf } from './liveTree'
+import {
+  editNote,
+  type Entry,
+  type Notes,
+  type Owed,
+  owedReport,
+  owesRename,
+  type PropertyEntry,
+  readNotes,
+} from './owed'
+
+type Finished<E extends Entry> = { left: E; reach: ConfigReach }
+
+/** An arm whose list file can't be read or written leaves its entry as it stood, counting that file as missed. */
+const stuck = <E extends Entry>(e: E): Finished<E> => ({ left: e, reach: { skipped: 1, hosts: [] } })
+
+/** Counts `r` into `reach`, answering whether it missed a file. */
+const add = (reach: ConfigReach, r: ConfigReach): boolean => {
+  reach.skipped += r.skipped
+  reach.hosts.push(...r.hosts)
+  return r.skipped > 0
+}
+
+export async function finishOwed(root: string, deps: TrashDeps): Promise<CascadeReport> {
+  const total: ConfigReach = { skipped: 0, hosts: [] }
+  const each = async (kind: Entry['kind']): Promise<void> => {
+    for (const [id, e] of Object.entries(await readNotes(root))) {
+      if (e.kind !== kind) continue
+      try {
+        add(total, await finishEntry(root, id, deps))
+      } catch (err) {
+        console.error('owed work could not finish:', errText(err))
+      }
+    }
+  }
+  await serializeSchemaOp(root, () => each('property'))
+  return owedReport(total)
+}
+
+/** Finishes one entry inside a caller already holding its kind's lock (the pass, or a Context or Space delete), writing back what it still owes. */
+export async function finishEntry(root: string, id: string, deps: TrashDeps): Promise<ConfigReach> {
+  const notes = await readNotes(root)
+  const e = notes[id]
+  if (!e) return { skipped: 0, hosts: [] }
+  const done = await finishArm(root, id, e, notes, deps)
+  await editNote(root, id, () => done.left)
+  return done.reach
+}
+
+function finishArm(root: string, id: string, e: Entry, notes: Notes, deps: TrashDeps): Promise<Finished<Entry>> {
+  switch (e.kind) {
+    case 'property':
+      return finishProperty(root, id, e)
+    case 'context':
+    case 'space':
+      return Promise.resolve({ left: e, reach: { skipped: 0, hosts: [] } })
+  }
+}
+
+/** Sweeps each of `names` that `skip` passes over, answering those a sweep missed; `reach` counts the files. */
+async function sweepEach(
+  names: readonly string[] | undefined,
+  skip: (name: string) => boolean,
+  sweep: (name: string) => Promise<number>,
+  reach: ConfigReach,
+): Promise<string[] | undefined> {
+  const left: string[] = []
+  for (const name of names ?? []) {
+    if (skip(name)) continue
+    const missed = await sweep(name)
+    reach.skipped += missed
+    if (missed) left.push(name)
+  }
+  return left.length ? left : undefined
+}
+
+async function finishProperty(root: string, id: string, e: PropertyEntry): Promise<Finished<PropertyEntry>> {
+  const reach: ConfigReach = { skipped: 0, hosts: [] }
+  let defs = (await readRegistry(root)).defs
+  // The current key sitting in `strip` is a delete whose list step hadn't landed.
+  if (defs[id] && e.strip?.includes(defs[id].key)) {
+    if (!(await removeFromRegistry(root, id)).ok) return stuck(e)
+    defs = (await readRegistry(root)).defs
+  }
+  const def = defs[id]
+  const held = (key: string): boolean => Object.values(defs).some((d) => d.id !== id && d.key === key)
+  if (!def) {
+    const strip = (e.strip ?? []).filter((key) => !held(key))
+    const folders = collectionFolders(root, await liveTreeOf(root))
+    const missed = strip.length > 0 && add(reach, await stripProperty(root, id, folders, await deletePlan(root, id, strip)))
+    return { left: { kind: 'property', strip: missed ? strip : undefined }, reach }
+  }
+  const rename = await sweepEach(e.rename, (key) => key === def.key || held(key), (key) => renameSweep(root, key, def.key), reach)
+  const options = await finishOptions(root, def, e.options ?? {}, reach)
+  // A live definition holding a strip part only arrives by sync; its Collections aren't this entry's to purge, so the part leaves.
+  const left: PropertyEntry = { kind: 'property', rename, options }
+  return { left: owesRename(left) ? { ...e, rename } : left, reach }
+}
+
+async function finishOptions(
+  root: string,
+  def: PropertyDefinition,
+  options: Record<string, Owed>,
+  reach: ConfigReach,
+): Promise<Record<string, Owed> | undefined> {
+  const left: Record<string, Owed> = {}
+  for (const [optionId, o] of Object.entries(options)) {
+    let option = findOption(def, optionId)
+    if (option && o.strip?.includes(option.key)) {
+      if (!(await dropOptionFromDef(root, def.id, option.key)).ok) {
+        left[optionId] = o
+        continue
+      }
+      option = undefined
+    }
+    const held = (word: string): boolean =>
+      optionsOf(def).some((x) => x.id !== optionId && memberKey(x.key) === memberKey(word))
+    const to = option?.key
+    const rename = to === undefined ? [] : (o.rename ?? []).filter((w) => w !== to && !held(w))
+    const strip = (o.strip ?? []).filter((w) => !held(w))
+    const renamed =
+      to !== undefined && rename.length > 0 && add(reach, await optionCascade(root, def, new Map(rename.map((w) => [w, to]))))
+    const stripped =
+      strip.length > 0 && add(reach, await optionCascade(root, def, new Map(strip.map((w) => [w, null])), optionId))
+    if (renamed || stripped) left[optionId] = { rename: renamed ? rename : undefined, strip: stripped ? strip : undefined }
+  }
+  return Object.keys(left).length ? left : undefined
+}
```

`deps` is read from Task 11B-2 on, by the Context and Space delete arms, and `finishArm`'s two pass-through cases are Task 11A-3's arms; Task 11A-2 lands the signature and the union's `switch` once. Every arm answers a `Finished`, so `finishEntry` writes back and reports whatever the arm left, and an arm that can't reach its list file reports it through `stuck`. The option parts sweep whether or not the property's rename is still owed, since the pages already under the current key are theirs to reach now; the entry keeps them whole until the rename lands (H-1), the same rule the runner applies to a live option change.

+async function finishContext(root: string, id: string, e: ContextEntry): Promise<Finished<ContextEntry>> {
+  const reg = await readRegistryStrict(root)
+  if (!reg.ok && reg.error.code !== 'not-found') return stuck(e)
+  const contexts = reg.ok ? reg.value.contexts : []
+  const title = contexts.find((c) => c.id === id)?.title
+  const reach: ConfigReach = { skipped: 0, hosts: [] }
+  const rename =
+    title === undefined
+      ? undefined
+      : await sweepEach(
+          e.rename,
+          (old) => old === title || contexts.some(rivalTitled(old, id)),
+          async (old) => {
+            const from = join(contextsDir(root), old)
+            const to = join(contextsDir(root), title)
+            // A crash between the list step and the folder move left the folder under the old title, and the open's tree read none of the Context's Spaces from the folder the list names, so the tree is read again once the folder is there.
+            if ((await heldName(from)) === old && !(await targetTaken(from, to))) {
+              await relocate(from, to)
+              await refreshTree(root)
+            }
+            return cascadeTitle(title, old, title, false, await titleHolders(root, title, old, false))
+          },
+          reach,
+        )
+  return { left: { ...e, rename }, reach }
+}
+
+async function finishSpace(root: string, id: string, e: SpaceEntry, notes: Notes): Promise<Finished<SpaceEntry>> {
+  const parent = notes[e.contextId]
+  const { groupById, spaceById } = contextWorldOf((await liveTreeOf(root)).contexts)
+  const group = groupById.get(e.contextId)
+  const reach: ConfigReach = { skipped: 0, hosts: [] }
+  // A Context gone or owed a delete takes its key, and every Space name in it, with it.
+  if (!group || parent?.strip?.length) return { left: { kind: 'space', contextId: e.contextId }, reach }
+  const title = spaceById.get(id)?.title
+  const rename =
+    title === undefined
+      ? undefined
+      : await sweepEach(
+          e.rename,
+          (old) => old === title || group.spaces.some(rivalTitled(old, id)),
+          async (old) =>
+            cascadeTitle(group.def.title, old, title, true, await titleHolders(root, group.def.title, old, true)),
+          reach,
+        )
+  return { left: owesRename(parent) ? e : { ...e, rename }, reach }
+}
```

A Space entry sweeps the holders already under its Context's current title on every finish, and stays whole while the Context's rename is owed, since the pages under the Context's old title weren't candidates (H-1); the pass runs Context entries first, so a Try Again that finishes the Context's rename lets the Space entry settle in the same pass.

- **Each Item Owes Its Own Work (B-1, LC-45):** one property's unfinished rename never blocks or unprotects another's; option renames, Value Format, option deletes, and Clear stop being refused because some property owes work. Nathan's intent.
- **Owed Names Are Refused (B-4; LC-7, LC-8, LC-9):** property create, rename, and Label Format, option create and rename, Context and Space create and rename, and every Trash restore refuse a name another item still owes with "An earlier change hasn’t reached every file yet." and Try Again.
- **A Note That Can't Be Written Refuses (LC-12):** every many-file change refuses with nothing changed; a Label Format change or option relabel that moves no key writes no note, so it lands as today.
- **One Try Again Finishes Everything (LC-6):** the open runs the same pass, once the index is seeded.

- **A Second Rename of One Context Keeps the First's Leftovers:** HEAD's slot let a second rename overwrite the first's record, forgetting its unreached pages after a restart; both old titles stay owed. B-1's intent applied to Contexts.
- **A Live Op Sweeps Its Own Old Name:** an older name still owed to the same item waits for Try Again rather than being swept by a later rename; a delete strips every owed name.
- **A Context Rename Whose Folder Can't Move or Go Back Offers Try Again (LC-64):** P9's order answered the relocate's error and left the note for the next open. The runner reads a title that couldn't go back as a list step that landed, so the reply reads "Couldn’t update 1 Item." with Try Again, which moves the folder and rekeys the files. The reason: the registry already names the new title, so the rename has landed in the list and only its folder and files are owed; Try Again finishes it now instead of at the next open. Recommendation: keep.
- **A Change Waiting on an Owed Rename Reads as Done (LC-63):** while a property's rename is owed, an option rename, option delete, or Remove reaches every page already under the new key and reads as done; while a Context's rename is owed, a Space rename or delete reaches every holder already under the Context's new title and reads as done. The pages under the old name keep the old value until the rename's own Try Again or the next open, which finishes the rename and then the change, in that order (H-1). For a Space delete this departs from B-3's letter, a delete that can't reach every page offering Try Again for the rest. The reason: those pages are the ones the rename's own notice counted and offered Try Again for, and counting which of them hold the change's word or Space would read files the rename couldn't read; offering Try Again here would need either a per-kind count of those pages (about 15 lines across the runner and the arms) or a count of one that misstates the number. Recommendation: keep; the alternative is the per-kind count.

  - "a Context's record leaves out its own Spaces": two Spaces under the deleted Context linking each other; the record's `membership` names neither, as HEAD's sweep capture didn't.

  - "a Context delete's own Spaces aren't owed": the Spaces under the deleted folder, which the tree still lists at their old paths, aren't counted as missed.
  - "a Space deleted while its Context owes a rename strips the holders under the Context's new title and stays owed": the Space entry stands with `strip: ['Gym']`, and once the Context's page reads, one `finishOwed` rekeys it and strips `Gym` from it (H-1).

+/** A Context's or Space's delete note: every title it still owed and the current one leave, with the bundle a finish moves the folder into. */
+const noteDelete = (
+  root: string,
+  id: string,
+  kind: { kind: 'context' } | { kind: 'space'; contextId: string },
+  title: string,
+  bundle: string | null,
+) =>

```

A Context or Space target resolves through the tree (`mutableTarget`), which lists only registry-held Contexts and their Spaces, so `entry` and `space` answer for every target that reaches the branch; the `entry ?` ternaries guarded a state no path produces, and one `not-found` line each narrows the type in their place. The capture is the finder's one read with `'values'`, made only when a bundle takes the record; the strip finds again after the move, inside the arm, since the arm is what the finish runs too. `finishEntry` runs inside `deleteOp`'s Contexts lock, which it doesn't take; it finds the list step landed and the folder moved, so it strips each owed title with the moved folder's files left out, reaches the views, and settles the entry. With `goneEdit`'s two cases gone, `edit` is `null` for a Context or Space, so `deleteOp`'s own configuration pass runs only for pages and containers. The Context and Space deletes keep their note and list step in `deleteOp`'s per-kind branch rather than `runNoted`: their sweep is the finish's arm, which runs after the folder move `deleteOp` shares with every kind.

#### Departures and Disclosures

##### Departures From the Findings

- **One Arm per Kind, Shared by the Finish and the Context and Space Deletes:** `finishEntry` runs one entry under a lock its caller holds; the pass calls it per entry, and `deleteOp` calls it once the folder has moved, so the live strip and the finishing strip are one routine. The deletes' note and list step sit in `deleteOp`'s per-kind branch rather than `runNoted`, since their sweep runs after the folder move `deleteOp` shares with every kind; Remove and every other many-file change run through the runner. The property ops sweep through their own modules' routines, which the arms import, since an arm in a property module the ops call would be an import cycle.
- **A Context's and a Space's Views Are Reached by Their Arm:** `deleteOp`'s configuration pass reached them through `goneEdit`; the arm now reaches them by id on every finish while the delete is owed, so a delete a crash cut short drops the views' columns too, and `goneEdit` loses its two cases.
- **The Capture Leaves Out the Deleted Folder's Own Files:** HEAD's sweep capture skipped the deleted Context's own folder (`skipUnder`); the up-front capture leaves out the same files, so a Context's record holds the same membership it did.
- **Remove's Stash Lands in Its Own Write:** item 12's "one sidecar write" held the assignment and the stash together. The live Remove and the finish now share `stashAndStrip` (read → stash → strip, F-7), so the stash lands in a second locked write after the assignment's; a crash between them leaves the Collection noted for the same routine.
- **Item 3's Remove and Delete Notes Land With Items 12 and 10:** each flow is rewritten in one task, Remove in 11B-3 and the Context and Space deletes in 11B-2; item 7's restore conversion lands per kind in the task that first produces that kind's delete entry (properties in 11A-2, Contexts and Spaces in 11B-2), through the one `restoreNote`, and item 8's refusals with the kind's notes (11A-2, 11A-3).
- **The Context and Space Delete Branches Require Their Target:** `mutableTarget` resolves a Context or Space through the tree, which lists only registry-held Contexts and their Spaces, so the `entry ?` ternaries guarded a state no path produces; they leave with a `not-found` line each.
- **A Restore Converts After It Lands:** converting before the landing would need the note put back on each of the landing's refusals; H-4's crash reading already covers a conversion that can't land (the next finish deletes again into the same bundle, and the restore can be repeated), as the property restore converts after its create.

##### Behavior Changes and Disclosures

- **Deletes Finish (B-3):** a Context or Space delete that misses pages, or a view settings file, finishes and offers Try Again, where it put everything back and refused. Nathan's intent.
- **A Partial Delete's Trash Entry Holds What It Missed (LC-10):** every delete captures its holders' values up front, an unreadable page's from the index.
- **Re-Adding Cancels an Owed Remove (LC-18); a Remove Reports What It Can't Clean Up (LC-19, C-2):** a Remove that missed pages returns to the list with Try Again.
- **The Refused-Holder Reading (Item 12):** Remove's entry stays owed, and is reported on every Try Again, for as long as a holder stays refused (front matter Pommora can't rewrite safely). That is how every arm already treats a page that stays unreadable (`chmod 000`): the entry stands until the file can be reached, and the warning says so. Dropping a holder the index no longer lists doesn't apply, since the index keeps a refused page's rows; and dropping refused holders would leave the value on a page the Collection no longer governs with nothing on record, the silent case LC-19 ends. An ID-less or duplicate-ID holder is transient: adoption stamps an ID at the page's next read and the remint ledger settles a duplicate, after which Try Again stashes and strips it. Under LC-6 a stuck refused page re-reports its one count with every Try Again until it's fixed by hand; the page's own "contains invalid metadata" notice names it.
- **A Space Deleted Under an Owed Context Rename:** the delete strips every holder already under the Context's current title and reads as done, against B-3's letter; the pages under the Context's old title keep the Space's tag until the Context's rename finishes, then lose it in the same pass. *Phase 11A*'s LC-63 carries the reading for every kind.
- **For Nathan — Refused Pages Under Rename and Delete:** LC-19 counts a refused page for Remove only. Property rename and delete, option changes, and Context and Space sweeps still count only files they couldn't read (`renameSweep` reads `skipped.length`; `sweepGovernedRoots`' `refused` reaches only Remove and, through the capture's `partial`, the Trash record), so after a rename or delete a page Pommora can't rewrite keeps the old key with nothing owed, as at HEAD. Widening the count to every arm is a behavior change this plan doesn't make; it's Nathan's call, NC-3.
- **The System Trash Mode's Context and Space Deletes (NC-1):** a finish in System Trash mode sends the folder to the system Trash and strips the tags with no record anywhere, as the live delete does; unchanged, Nathan's call.
- **The Orphan Trash Entry (H-5 Residual):** a crash between a delete's bundle mint and its note leaves a Trash entry for a live item, as at HEAD; its restore refuses `'exists'`, and it can be emptied.

##### Found False at HEAD

- **`deleteOp`'s Absent-Entry Branches:** the `entry ?` guards (`Core/Trash/delete.ts:121,125,133,136`) guard a Context target `mutableTarget` never resolves.

### Phase 12 — The Stash and Trash Records

**GOAL:** The stash keeps its home in the Collection's settings file, takes one name on disk and in code, records when each property's values were removed, and ages them out after the History Timeframe on that timeframe's two existing triggers. Re-adding a property refills the pages still in the Collection and the Trash copies of pages trashed from it, drops entries for pages that left, and surfaces any page it couldn't write with Try Again; a restored property gets its stash back in the right order and with its original removal time. A partly recorded Trash entry shows its mark and its restore says so, and a restore that reports in its own notice keeps the Try Again its reply owes. This phase is separate because it closes the data layer: every stash writer, the Trash record, and both restores move together, and the Mid-Plan Neutral Gate reads the range it ends.

**Builds On:** P1 (`seedNexus` in `Core/Testing/hostFs.ts`, the shared fixture module `Core/Testing/definitions.ts`); P4 (`Core/Nexus/governedSweep.ts`; `reencode`, `Frozen`, and `gonePageEntry` in `Core/Nexus/governedRoot.ts`; `frozenWorld` in `Core/Trash/holdings.ts`, which P7 renames `trashedCopies.ts`); P5 (`CollectionNode.propertyIds`, `resolveAssignedSchema` gone); P7 (the `mutate` ops `addProperty`, `assignProperty`, `unassignProperty`, `deleteProperty`; `Core/Properties/removeProperty.ts` → `unassignProperty.ts`; `Core/Trash/holdings.ts` → `Core/Trash/trashedCopies.ts`; `refillValues` beside `sweepRootsById` in `Core/Nexus/governedSweep.ts`; `createProperty` answering the landed definition; the counting module `Core/Nexus/entities.ts` holding `unsweptLine`; `openSettings`, `closeSettings`, and `trashRowEl` moved into `drive-harness.mjs`; the `mutate` arm `assignProperty` replying through `done`); P8 (option ids); P9 (list-first orders; replays after the seed); P10 (`findHolders` in `Core/Index/keyHolders.ts`; `sweepGovernedRoots(files, plan)` with no `root`; `sweepRootsById` reading each Space's path from `byId`; `unwritten` and `rootId` in `governedSweep.ts`; `refillOf(def, frozen)`, the one refill rewrite `refillValues` and `refillTrashed(root, links, defs, frozen)` both land through; `spaceArm` gone; G-3's `unswept`); P11 (`Core/Nexus/owed.ts` with `PropertyEntry`, `owesAnything`, `editNote`, `propertyNote`, `owedReport`, `owedDelete`; `Core/Nexus/finishOwed.ts` with `finishProperty` and `sweepEach`; `CascadeReport.owed?: true`, which `joinCascades` carries; the slice's `finishOwed` action, its one Try Again; Remove's note, `stashAndStrip`, and its `unassigned` arm; H-18's counted purge; restores as create → `owedRestore` → spend). +/** Drops every block a Remove last stamped before the History Timeframe, in the Collections the held tree lists as stashing one; with none listed, it reads nothing. */
+export async function sweepStashes(root: string): Promise<void> {
+  const collections = heldTreeOf(root)?.collections ?? []
+  const ids = new Set(collections.flatMap((c) => c.stashed ?? []))
+  if (!ids.size) return
+  const cutoff = Date.now() - (await readFileHistoryConfig(root)).keepMs
+  await editStashes(root, collections, ids, (_values, _id, removedAt) =>
+    Date.parse(removedAt) < cutoff ? {} : null,
+  )
+}

  > This range rebuilds how the Pommora app stores, writes, and recovers property data underneath, with almost nothing a person sees changing. It intended these outcomes:
  > - Code that only existed to read file layouts from older builds of the app is gone, and nothing still holding those layouts needed to keep working.
  > - The list of property types holds only the types a person can create, plus Context; Title, Created Time, Last Modified, and Location are a separate small table, and a hand-written definition that isn't a real type is set aside when the property list is read.
  > - Each type's facts are written once per side of the app, so code asks the type instead of deciding it again.
  > - Writing a value to a page or a Space goes through one module that reads the file once. When a value is written, the page's other properties are tidied by one rule: a value is never blanked, a list never loses an item it can't read, and a Select or Status holding several words becomes the one option it shows. Text holding only spaces reads as empty. A write that changes nothing leaves the file alone.
  > - Collections refer to property definitions by id, so an incoming definition doesn't force re-reading every page; a damaged property list opens the workspace with properties marked unreadable instead of refusing to open.
  > - Undo puts back exactly what the file held for the one property that was edited, and undoing a link value also removes the alias it added.
  > - Every property change goes through the app's one change channel with one reply shape, and confirmations count affected items correctly, zero included.
  > - Every option has a permanent id; saved views, tiles, and filters refer to options by id, so renaming an option no longer rewrites them. Collapsed groups are remembered per property.
  > - Changes that rewrite many files update the list first and the files second, and every property, Context, and Space keeps its own crash-recovery record in one file. A change that can't reach every file finishes what it can and offers one Try Again that finishes everything owed; a name still owed to unfinished work can't be reused until that work finishes.
  > - Finding which files hold a property or a tag uses one shared lookup: properties reach pages in Collections and the archive, tags reach any page.
  > - A removed property's set-aside values record when they were removed and are cleaned out after the page-history timeframe; re-adding the property refills pages still in the Collection, pages in the trash, and reports any it couldn't refill.
  > - The production code is smaller than at the baseline, with fewer ways of doing the same thing, and the tests pin each intended behavior once.
  >
  > Does the range hold these outcomes, with no data lost on an ordinary action, no expensive work added to a frequent path, and nothing left half-moved? Answer yes or no, with the corrections that would make it yes.

#### Departures and Disclosures

##### Departures From the Findings

- **The Refill's Note Is Written in `assignInner`, Not `assignProperty` (item 6, *One Write Path*):** the Findings have `assignProperty` reply owed and write `refill`. `restoreInner` re-assigns through the same `assignInner`, so its skips would stay silent, the loss LC-5 exists to stop; every re-add (the op, the restore, and `addProperty`, whose new property has no stash) passes through `assignInner`, so the note and the owed report live there and `assignProperty` forwards them, answering the reply itself in place of `done`'s empty one.
- **`refillStash` Takes the Collection's Id (item 5):** the notes entry holds Collection ids (folders move between a crash and a retry), and `finishProperty` has nothing else; `refillStash(root, propertyId, collectionId)` resolves the Collection from the tree it already reads, so both callers pass an id. Whether the Collection still assigns the property is its callers' to know: `assignInner` has just appended it, and the finish reads it off the tree with the same skip rule its `unassigned` part reads. `assignInner` reads the id off the sidecar `patchSidecar` answers, which it writes only when the sidecar carries one.
- **`refillValues` Answers `{ taken, skipped }`, `sweepRootsById`'s Shape (item 6):** the Findings name the refill's answer `{ spent; skipped }`. `refillValues` returns `sweepRootsById`'s reply unchanged, and `taken` is already the restore's word for it (`restoreProperty.ts:71`, `spend.ts:237`), so one shape carries one name. `skipped` counts the sweep's skipped and refused files, the reading P11's Remove takes for refused pages (LC-19).
- **`addressable` Widens With `sweepRootsById`'s Roots (item 5):** the Findings narrow `sweepRootsById`'s `roots`; `sweepRootsById` reads `addressable(roots, id)`, which reads only `get(id) !== null`, so its parameter widens to `ReadonlyMap<string, unknown>` in the same task. `RootsById` is exported once from `governedSweep.ts` because `refillStash` builds one.
- **The Stash Sweeps When the History Timeframe Is Written, Not the Archive's (item 4, LC-26):** the Findings run the sweep inside the `historyDays || archiveHistoryDays` branch. The stash follows the History Timeframe alone (LC-26), so an Archive History Timeframe write moves no cutoff the stash reads; only a `historyDays` write runs it, one line beside the file-history trigger.
- **The Sweep Has No Catch of Its Own (item 4):** the Findings say it logs and swallows errors as `sweepFileHistory` does. With no Collection listed as stashing, which includes no tree held, the sweep returns before reading anything; otherwise `readFileHistoryConfig` reads the held tree's config and `editStashes` swallows each sidecar's failure. No throw path is left for a catch to guard (*Fix the Origin*).
- **The Partial Line's Builder Sits Beside `partial` (item 9):** the Findings put `recordedPartly` in `spend.ts`. The property restore's reply is built in `restoreInner`, the one place that knows the label its definition landed under (the record's `def` decodes loose), so the builder lives in `record.ts` beside the field it reads, and each restore joins it where it builds its reply.
- **The Glyph Joins the Curated Roster (item 9):** the curated registry has no warning glyph, and `Icon` would render `'triangle-alert'` through `LazyGlyph`, loading the whole Lucide set into the Settings window for one row. `TriangleAlert` joins the registry, which its own comment names as the way to add an icon.

The slice's notices and the Restored notice share the one shown notification, so the Restored notice replaces them in the same turn and the lines show once, inside it (*§Found False at HEAD*); dropping them would hide them. The task passes the reply's Try Again instead, which the replacement otherwise loses.

Its `MATRIX.md` rows are Task 18-6's, which rewrites them once for the landed system.

##### Behavior Changes and Disclosures

- **Each Is a Ruled or Recommended Behavior:** stash entries age out after the History Timeframe at the open and when the History Timeframe is written (C-3, Nathan's intent; LC-26, LC-27); re-adding drops entries for pages that left and parks a trashed page's value in its Trash copy, only for a page trashed from this Collection (C-2, Nathan's intent; LC-36); a re-add or a property restore that couldn't refill a page says "Couldn’t update N Items." with Try Again, and the entry keeps the refill owed until a finish reaches it (LC-5); a restored property's stash keeps its Remove's stamp (LC-26) and is written back before the re-assign, so leftovers refill and a page in both takes its delete-time value (C-2); a partly recorded Trash entry shows its mark and its restore says so (N-1, LC-37); a restore that reports in its own notice keeps the Try Again its reply owes (B-3); Collections in the Trash stay untouched by a global delete, and a restored Collection's inert id stays (LC-2, LC-4, pinned in Task 12-4).
- **A Page That Left Loses Its Stashed Value at the Next Re-Add (C-2):** a page deleted, moved to another Collection, or claimed by two files at the re-add leaves the block, where today it waits forever; `unassignProperty.test.ts`' HEAD case pinning the opposite is rewritten. A page unreadable at that moment is absent from `byId` and drops with them (S's accepted edge, since `tree.unreadable` lists paths, not ids). A member already holding its own value isn't taken, so its entry waits for the timeframe, as does a stashed Link refilled into a Trash copy naming a gone page, since `gonePageEntry` runs over members only; both are bounded and earn no arm.
- **A Failed Spend Write Counts as a Skip:** `refillStash` answers one more skip when its final sidecar write fails, where HEAD's `assignInner` answered that failure as the re-add's refusal after the assignment and the refill had already landed. The re-add now reports it with Try Again, which re-runs the spend.
- **The Note Is Written After the Refill:** the refill can't know it skipped until it runs, so `refill` is written on a skip, after the pages. When the notes file can't be written, the warning still shows and `owed` is left off, so no Try Again is offered for an entry that doesn't exist; the values stay in the stash until the timeframe.
- **A Restore Into Several Collections Joins Their Lines:** a property restore whose re-assign skipped in two Collections shows "Couldn’t update 1 Item. Couldn’t update 2 Items." through `joinCascades`, the way a batch restore lists each bundle's warning. Two Collections skipping in one restore needs two unwritable pages in two Collections at once.
- **A Batch Restore Shows a Missed Refill Without Try Again:** `restoreBatch` runs `mutate` quiet and posts its own lines, so a property among several restored at once reports a refill it missed with no Try Again, as every batch line does today; its entry stays owed, and the next open's finish refills it.
- **The Sweep and Try Again Run Side by Side at the Open:** `void sweepStashes(root)` runs while `await finishOwed(…)` does; both write sidecars through `patchSidecar`'s per-file lock, a `refill` part re-run against a block the sweep just dropped answers 0 skipped and drops out of the entry, and the sweep's tree lists Collections from the walk, whose paths no property arm moves.
- **A Block That Expires Mid-Session Can Still Refill Until the Next Trigger:** expired file history stays viewable the same way, since neither reader filters by age.
- **A Block Without a Stamp Is Read as No Block:** every block the app writes carries its stamp from the commit that names the store, and Sync carries a Collection's settings file whole (`Core/Sync/Arrival/mergePolicy.ts:38`), so only a hand edit can leave one; `stashedBlock` reads it as absent, so it neither refills nor ages. No Nexus holds a stash today (LC-3).
- **The Sweep Is a New Writer of Synced Sidecars:** recorded in *§Sync Rebuild Inputs* (*The Stash Sweep as a New Writer*); nothing under `Core/Sync/` changes.
- **The History Timeframe's Hint Stays:** "Stores recoverable snapshots of device-local file history." (`Core/Settings/frames.ts:650`) now undersells a setting that also ages a synced store; its wording waits for I-076's pass and I-077 (LC-27).
- **The Restore's Link Parking and the Stash's Trash Parking Share One Rewrite:** `refillTrashed` puts `record.links`' recorded Link values back into Trash copies at a restore, and the stash's parking re-adds a value into a Trash copy through the definition as it reads now. P10 lands `refillTrashed` through `refillOf(def, frozen)`, the rewrite `refillValues` passes to `sweepRootsById`, so both parkings reconcile, encode, and blank-check a value the way a live refill does (an option or page deleted since doesn't come back), find copies through the one `trashedHolders`, and write through `sweepGovernedRoots`. This phase adds only `trashedHolders`' `from` filter and its second caller.

### Phase 13 — Columns Carry Their Answer

**GOAL:** A view classifies each column once, into one `ResolvedColumn` carrying its type and definition, and every cell, filter rule, sort criterion, grouping, width, alignment, look, and header reads that answer instead of looking the id up again: the per-cell schema scans, `declaredType`'s 23 calls, `columnType`, the five hand-built columns, and the optional Context-id defaults leave. +const TITLE: ResolvedColumn = { id: FILEDATA.title.id, kind: 'title', type: 'title' }
+
+export const propertyColumn = (def: PropertyDefinition): ResolvedColumn => ({
+  id: def.id,
+  kind: 'property',
+  type: def.type,
+  def,
+})
+
+export const contextColumn = (id: string): ResolvedColumn => ({ id, kind: 'context', type: 'context' })
+
+/** The one classification of a column id, done once per view pass; nothing for Location, which is never a column, or for an id neither the schema nor the registry holds. */
+export function resolveColumn(
+  id: string,
+  schema: PropertyDefinition[],
+  contextIds: readonly string[],
+): ResolvedColumn | undefined {
+  if (id === TITLE.id) return TITLE
+  const stamp = FILEDATA_BY_ID.get(id)?.type
+  if (stamp) return { id, kind: 'stamp', type: stamp }
+  if (contextIds.includes(id)) return contextColumn(id)
+  const def = schema.find((d) => d.id === id)
+  return def && propertyColumn(def)
+}
 
 /** Context columns are default-OFF — they render only when the view's property_order explicitly reveals them. */
 export function resolveColumns(
   view: SavedView,

-  contextIds: readonly string[] = [],

-  return result
+  const hidden = new Set(view.hidden_properties)
+  const columns = new Map<string, ResolvedColumn>()
+  for (const id of view.property_order) {
+    if (hidden.has(id) || columns.has(id)) continue
+    const column = resolveColumn(id, schema, contextIds)
+    if (column) columns.set(id, column)
+  }
+  return columns.has(TITLE.id) ? [...columns.values()] : [TITLE, ...columns.values()]
 }

+/** A value a pending write picked stands in until a read retires it. Title, the stamps, and a Context read the row, not the front matter the memo is keyed on; a Context's ids resolve at walk assembly onto the row's own `contextValues`. */
+export function resolveFieldValue(row: ViewRow, column: ResolvedColumn): PropertyValue {
+  const picked = row.picked?.[column.id]
+  if (picked) return picked
+  switch (column.kind) {
+    case 'title':
+      return { kind: 'text', value: row.title }
+    case 'stamp':
+      return stampValue(column.type === 'createdTime' ? row.createdAt : row.modifiedAt)
+    case 'context': {
+      const ids = row.contextValues?.[column.id]
+      return ids?.length ? { kind: 'context', value: ids } : NULL_VALUE
+    }
+    case 'property': {
+      const { def } = column
+      if (!def) return NULL_VALUE
+      let m = resolvedByFm.get(row.frontmatter)
+      if (!m) {
+        m = new WeakMap()
+        resolvedByFm.set(row.frontmatter, m)
+      }
+      let v = m.get(def)
+      if (!v) {
+        v = decodeValue(def, (row.frontmatter as Record<string, unknown>)[def.key])
+        m.set(def, v)
+      }
+      return v
+    }
+  }
+}

#### Task 13-3

**TASK:** A column's style resolves from the column itself, and the view host owns the one memoized style map: `styleFor(column, view, nexus)` and `columnStylePatch(view, column, nexus, patch)` read `column.type` and `column.def`, the host computes `styleById` once per pass and its `styleOf` and `setStylePatch` take a column, and `useColumnStyleMap` and `useStyleFor` leave. The Settings panes outside the host (`FilterFrame`, `GroupFrame`, `PropertyFrame`) call the pure `styleFor` with `useNexusForms()`, as `GroupFrame` already does, and the band face takes its grouping's date format rather than a style callback. `FilterFrame` resolves each rule's column once, which also retires its two `declaredType` calls and its private `defById`.

**NOW:**
- Four accessors resolve one column's style (07-09): `styleFor(columnId, schema, view, nexus)` (`Core/Views/Host/useColumnStyles.ts:35-46`, through `columnDefaults`' `declaredType` and `schema.find`, `:23-33`); `useStyleFor()` (`:83-90`), read by `FilterFrame.tsx:234` (used at `:353,410`) and `PropertyFrame.tsx:188` (used at `:406`); `useColumnStyleMap(host)` (`:92-102`), memoized, read by `useColumns.ts:186` and `CardsView.tsx:208`; and the host's unmemoized `styleOf(columnId)` (`useViewHost.ts:210`), read by `pickTarget` (`:214`) and handed to `runPropertyAction` (`useViewInteractions.tsx:412`). `useBandHeads.ts:29` builds its own closure for `headContextOf`, which reads only the grouping's `date_format` from it (`bandModel.ts:67`); `GroupFrame.tsx:210,519` call `styleFor` with `useNexusForms()`.
- `setStylePatch(colId, key, value)` (`useViewHost.ts:156-157`) and `columnStylePatch(view, schema, nexus, columnId, patch)` (`useColumnStyles.ts:59-75`) re-derive the column's defaults by id; `setStylePatch`'s callers are `useColumns.ts`' `runStyleAction` (`:300-303`, from the header menu `:329` and `TableView.tsx:308`'s cell menu), `CardsView.tsx:291`'s `setStyle` (`CardValue.tsx:130`'s `onStyle(column.id, …)`), and `pickTarget`'s style control (`useViewHost.ts:230`). `PropertyFrame.tsx:260-262`'s `saveColumnStyle(propId, patch)` takes an id its five callers hold the definition for (`:334,357,364,372,421`).
- `FilterFrame`'s rule row classifies its rule twice (`:380` Context, `:408` Checkbox, both `declaredType`), reads its definition through a private `defById` map (`:265`, read at `:327,409`), and resolves its style twice (`:353,410`).
- `useColumnStyles.test.ts` drives `styleFor` and `pickedStyle` by id (`:31-115`), with `'prop_gone'` (`:63`) pinning a stale id's defaults.

Behavior is unchanged: every column a surface lays out has a type, so the width and alignment fallbacks for a type-less column leave as unreachable.

#### Task 13-7

**TASK:** The table header's hide writes through `hideShown`, the one hide rule the host and the Visibility pane already use. On F3's Fail outcome only, a value write's optimistic patch and a created page's two seed patches also share one split, `patchedValues`, which lays each value by its column: a Context's ids on `contexts`, a property's value in the row's front matter. On its Pass outcome P6 has already removed every copy of that split, so the half has nothing to fold and doesn't land. Behavior is unchanged.

**NOW:**
- `useColumns`' `commitHide` writes `[...view.hidden_properties, collapsing]` itself (`useColumns.ts:291-296`), without the dedupe `hideShown` (`Core/Views/visibilityModel.ts:37-43`) applies for `useViewHost.ts:166-169` and `VisibilityFrame`; the header hides only a rendered column, which `resolveColumns` has already excluded from `hidden_properties`, so the missing dedupe is unreachable and the second path is the only difference (07-16).
- `withSeeds(schema, frontmatter, seeds)` (`Core/Views/Host/useViewCreation.ts:45-58`) re-implements the value write's optimistic split for a created page, with two readers: `impliedSeeds` (`:110`) builds the blank row the view's filter judges, and `patchSeedValues` (`:135`) builds the created page's override. +export function patchedValues(
+  frontmatter: Record<string, unknown>,
+  values: Record<string, PropertyValue | null>,
+  columnOf: (id: string) => ResolvedColumn | undefined,
+): { frontmatter: PageFrontmatter; contexts?: Record<string, string[]> } {

### Phase 14 — The Per-Kind View Record

**GOAL:** One renderer-free record keyed by value kind, `VALUE_KINDS` in `Core/Views/valueKinds.ts`, states what each kind does in a view: the operators the filter pane offers, how a rule tests a value with its operands read once, what Is Empty means, the key a sort compares, the words the Sort pane names a direction with, the band a grouping files a value under, and the value a new page takes from a filter rule, a band, or a sort neighbor. It replaces the filter's six evaluators and their dispatcher, the sort's five key extractors and its kind switch, the bucket switch, `KIND_OPS`, `FROM_GROUP_KEY`, `SEEDS_FROM_SORT`, the seed switch, and the Sort pane's direction switch, and one `shownText` replaces the two text projections. An unreadable filter value and an operator its kind doesn't answer are ignored, a Checkbox's "is not empty" works, and an empty value sorts last for every type in both directions. The view pipeline's per-edit cost and the Matrix filter's cost are measured on `~/Benchmark-Large` and settle Approach K and 07-10 by rule, and the Properties Drive gains group 12.

**Builds On:** P2's AFTER (`ColumnType`, `PROPERTY_TYPES: Readonly<Record<ColumnType, TypeSpec>>` with Title's `{ kind: 'text' }` row, `FILEDATA`, Title's value `{ kind: 'text' }`, `formatBucketLabel` in `group.ts`), P3's (`Core/Views/paneTargets.ts`), P4A's (`readNumber` in `Core/Properties/propertyValue.ts`, `fileName` in `Core/Connections/linkValue.ts`, `Core/Properties/fieldValue.ts`, `formatValue.ts` outside the engine graph), P8's (option ids; `optionIds(def)` in `properties.ts`; `optionLabel(def, id)` in `propertyValue.ts`; `prepareRule` hands the evaluators the rule's definition; Task 8-4 deletes `configReach.ts`' `wholeValues` and `filterRules.ts`' `SUBSTRING_OPS`), and P13's (`resolveColumn(id, schema, contextIds)` in `Core/Views/Pipeline/columns.ts`; `ResolvedColumn = { id; kind; type: ColumnType; def? }`; `resolveFieldValue(row, column)`; `prepareRule` resolving its column once; `buildCriterion(c, schema, contextIds)`, `makeSorter(sort, schema, contextIds, manualOrder)`, `resolvedSortCount(sort, schema, contextIds)`; `bucketKey(row, column, granularity)`; `Grouping = { config; column }`; `TypeSpec.groups?: true` kept, whether a type groups at all; `declaredType` gone). Every cite is HEAD `6890f015d` (code identical to `3c6afcabb`); where an earlier phase rewrote a line, the cite names the function and that phase, and the `-` lines show that phase's text.

+/** A value as the text its cell shows, which the filter's text operators search and the sort orders: an option's label, a text with its connections as they read, a link's display text, a list's members joined; null for a value that shows no text of its own. */
+export function shownText(value: PropertyValue, def?: PropertyDefinition): string | null {
+  switch (value.kind) {
+    case 'text':
+      return shownProse(value.value)
+    case 'link':
+      return linkDisplayText(value.value)
+    case 'select':
+      return optionLabel(def, value.value)
+    case 'multiSelect':
+      return value.value.map((id) => optionLabel(def, id)).join(',')

+      // The filenames, not the raw `[[…]]` references, which would all share the leading bracket.
+      return value.value.map(fileName).join(',')
+    case 'number':
+    case 'checkbox':
+    case 'dateTime':
+    case 'context':
+    case 'null':
+      return null
+  }
+}

```Core/Views/valueKinds.ts (new, as this task creates it)
// What each value kind does in a view: the operators the filter pane offers, how a rule tests a value, the key a sort compares, the band a grouping files a value under, and the value a new page takes from a rule, a band, or a sort neighbor.

import { foldKey } from '../Paths/caseFold'
import type { PropertyDefinition } from '../Properties/properties'
import {
  checkboxWord,
  isBlankValue,
  type PropertyValue,
  readNumber,
  selectedValues,
  type ValueKind,
} from '../Properties/propertyValue'
import { dayMs, type LocalDate, readDate, shownText } from '../Properties/formatValue'
import { FILTER_OPS } from './filterRules'

type ValueSlot = 'none' | 'text' | 'number' | 'date' | 'chips' | 'set'

export interface OperatorChoice {
  op: string
  label: string
  slot: ValueSlot
  impliedValue?: string
  /** A typed folder name is an operand as well as a picked folder. */
  names?: true
}

export type ValueTest = (v: PropertyValue) => boolean

export type ValueKindSpec = Readonly<{
  /** The operators the filter pane offers, in its menu's order; a hand-written rule may hold others the kind still answers. */
  ops: readonly OperatorChoice[]
  /** Is Empty matches a value this reads as unfilled, and Isn't Empty one it reads as filled. */
  filled: ValueTest
  /** A rule's test, its operands read once; undefined, so the rule abstains, for an op the kind doesn't answer or an operand that doesn't read. */
  prepare(op: string, want: readonly string[], def?: PropertyDefinition): ValueTest | undefined
}>

const EMPTIES: OperatorChoice[] = [
  { op: FILTER_OPS.isEmpty, label: 'Is Empty', slot: 'none' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.isNotEmpty, label: "Isn't Empty", slot: 'none' },
]

const TEXT_OPS: OperatorChoice[] = [
  { op: FILTER_OPS.is, label: 'Is', slot: 'text' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.isNot, label: "Isn't", slot: 'text' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.startsWith, label: 'Starts With', slot: 'text' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.contains, label: 'Contains', slot: 'text' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.doesNotContain, label: "Doesn't Contain", slot: 'text' },
  ...EMPTIES,
]

/** The Starts and Ends ops are inclusive — the strict variants stay registered for hand-authored files, but the frame doesn't offer a second near-identical set. */
const DATE_OPS: OperatorChoice[] = [
  { op: FILTER_OPS.is, label: 'Is', slot: 'date' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.onOrBefore, label: 'Starts Before', slot: 'date' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.onOrAfter, label: 'Starts After', slot: 'date' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.endsOnOrBefore, label: 'Ends Before', slot: 'date' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.endsOnOrAfter, label: 'Ends After', slot: 'date' },
  ...EMPTIES,
]

const SET_OPS: OperatorChoice[] = [
  { op: FILTER_OPS.containsAny, label: 'Is Any', slot: 'chips' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.containsAll, label: 'Is All', slot: 'chips' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.doesNotContain, label: "Isn't", slot: 'chips' },
  ...EMPTIES,
]

const NUMBER_OPS: OperatorChoice[] = [
  { op: FILTER_OPS.is, label: 'Is', slot: 'number' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.isNot, label: "Isn't", slot: 'number' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.greaterThan, label: 'Greater Than', slot: 'number' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.greaterOrEqual, label: 'At Least', slot: 'number' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.lessThan, label: 'Less Than', slot: 'number' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.lessOrEqual, label: 'At Most', slot: 'number' },
  ...EMPTIES,
]

/** Is/Isn't are chip pickers whose multi-chips mean any-of/none-of — never Is All, which is unsatisfiable on a one-value property. */
const OPTION_OPS: OperatorChoice[] = [
  { op: FILTER_OPS.is, label: 'Is', slot: 'chips' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.isNot, label: "Isn't", slot: 'chips' },
  ...EMPTIES,
]

const CHECKBOX_OPS: OperatorChoice[] = [
  { op: FILTER_OPS.is, label: 'Is Checked', slot: 'none', impliedValue: 'true' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.is, label: "Isn't Checked", slot: 'none', impliedValue: 'false' },
]

const notBlank: ValueTest = (v) => !isBlankValue(v)
const showsText: ValueTest = (v) => !!shownText(v)

/** Is and Isn't compare a value's whole shown text, and the others search within it, folded on both sides. */
function prepareText(
  op: string,
  want: readonly string[],
  def?: PropertyDefinition,
): ValueTest | undefined {
  const w = want.map(foldKey)
  const shown = (v: PropertyValue): string | null => {
    const s = shownText(v, def)
    return s === null ? null : foldKey(s)
  }
  const is: ValueTest = (v) => {
    const f = shown(v)
    return f !== null && w.includes(f)
  }
  const contains: ValueTest = (v) => shown(v)?.includes(w[0]) ?? false
  switch (op) {
    case FILTER_OPS.is:
      return is
    case FILTER_OPS.isNot:
      return (v) => !is(v)
    case FILTER_OPS.contains:
      return contains
    case FILTER_OPS.doesNotContain:
      return (v) => !contains(v)
    case FILTER_OPS.startsWith:
      return (v) => shown(v)?.startsWith(w[0]) ?? false
    default:
      return undefined
  }
}

/** Is and the containing ops match a value holding any operand, Is All one holding every operand, and the two negations a value holding none. */
function prepareMembers(op: string, want: readonly string[]): ValueTest | undefined {
  const any: ValueTest = (v) => selectedValues(v).some((x) => want.includes(x))
  switch (op) {
    case FILTER_OPS.containsAll:
      return (v) => {
        const xs = selectedValues(v)
        return want.every((w) => xs.includes(w))
      }
    case FILTER_OPS.is:
    case FILTER_OPS.contains:
    case FILTER_OPS.containsAny:
      return any
    case FILTER_OPS.isNot:
    case FILTER_OPS.doesNotContain:
      return (v) => !any(v)
    default:
      return undefined
  }
}

function prepareNumber(op: string, want: readonly string[]): ValueTest | undefined {
  const e = readNumber(want[0])
  if (e === undefined) return undefined
  const holds =
    (test: (n: number) => boolean): ValueTest =>
    (v) =>
      v.kind === 'number' && test(v.value)
  const is = holds((n) => n === e)
  switch (op) {
    case FILTER_OPS.is:
      return is
    case FILTER_OPS.isNot:
      return (v) => !is(v)
    case FILTER_OPS.greaterThan:
      return holds((n) => n > e)
    case FILTER_OPS.lessThan:
      return holds((n) => n < e)
    case FILTER_OPS.greaterOrEqual:
      return holds((n) => n >= e)
    case FILTER_OPS.lessOrEqual:
      return holds((n) => n <= e)
    default:
      return undefined
  }
}

/** Days are the local days the cells show. `is` matches a day the value spans; a bare-day operand orders by day, and one carrying a time orders by instant. The Starts ops and the strict pair read a span's start, the Ends ops its end. */
function prepareDate(op: string, want: readonly string[]): ValueTest | undefined {
  const target = readDate(want[0])
  if (target === null) return undefined
  const ms = (x: Date): number => (target.timed ? x.getTime() : dayMs(x))
  const e = ms(target.at)
  const day = dayMs(target.at)
  // A clockless end holds its whole day, so a timed operand meets it at the day's last instant.
  const endMs = (d: LocalDate): number => {
    const last = d.end ?? d.at
    return d.timed || !target.timed
      ? ms(last)
      : new Date(last.getFullYear(), last.getMonth(), last.getDate() + 1).getTime() - 1
  }
  const dated =
    (test: (d: LocalDate) => boolean): ValueTest =>
    (v) => {
      const d = v.kind === 'dateTime' ? readDate(v.value) : null
      return d !== null && test(d)
    }
  switch (op) {
    case FILTER_OPS.is:
      return dated((d) => dayMs(d.at) <= day && day <= dayMs(d.end ?? d.at))
    case FILTER_OPS.isBefore:
      return dated((d) => ms(d.at) < e)
    case FILTER_OPS.isAfter:
      return dated((d) => ms(d.at) > e)
    case FILTER_OPS.onOrAfter:
      return dated((d) => ms(d.at) >= e)
    case FILTER_OPS.onOrBefore:
      return dated((d) => ms(d.at) <= e)
    case FILTER_OPS.endsOnOrAfter:
      return dated((d) => endMs(d) >= e)
    case FILTER_OPS.endsOnOrBefore:
      return dated((d) => endMs(d) <= e)
    default:
      return undefined
  }
}

function prepareCheckbox(op: string, want: readonly string[]): ValueTest | undefined {
  const checked = checkboxWord(want[0])
  if (checked === null) return undefined
  const is: ValueTest = (v) => (v.kind === 'checkbox') === checked
  switch (op) {
    case FILTER_OPS.is:
      return is
    case FILTER_OPS.isNot:
      return (v) => !is(v)
    default:
      return undefined
  }
}

const PROSE: ValueKindSpec = { ops: TEXT_OPS, filled: showsText, prepare: prepareText }

export const VALUE_KINDS: Readonly<Record<ValueKind, ValueKindSpec>> = {
  text: PROSE,
  link: PROSE,
  number: { ops: NUMBER_OPS, filled: notBlank, prepare: prepareNumber },
  dateTime: {
    ops: DATE_OPS,
    filled: (v) => v.kind === 'dateTime' && readDate(v.value) !== null,
    prepare: prepareDate,
  },
  checkbox: { ops: CHECKBOX_OPS, filled: notBlank, prepare: prepareCheckbox },
  // Is and Isn't name whole options; the text ops a hand-written rule may hold search the option's label.
  select: {
    ops: OPTION_OPS,
    filled: notBlank,
    prepare: (op, want, def) =>
      op === FILTER_OPS.is || op === FILTER_OPS.isNot
        ? prepareMembers(op, want)
        : prepareText(op, want, def),
  },
  multiSelect: { ops: SET_OPS, filled: notBlank, prepare: prepareMembers },
  context: { ops: SET_OPS, filled: notBlank, prepare: prepareMembers },
  file: { ops: EMPTIES, filled: notBlank, prepare: () => undefined },
}

```Core/Views/Pipeline/sort.ts (as this task leaves it, in full)
// `sort[]` is honored in array order (priority = index), each criterion compared until one breaks the tie, then stable input order; a value with no key sorts last in either direction.

import type { SortCriterion } from '../views'
import type { ViewRow } from '../viewRow'
import { compareTitles } from '../../Paths/caseFold'
import { PROPERTY_TYPES, type PropertyDefinition } from '../../Properties/properties'
import { resolveFieldValue } from '../../Properties/fieldValue'
import { resolveColumn } from './columns'
import { VALUE_KINDS } from '../valueKinds'

type SortKey = string | number | null

interface ResolvedCriterion {
  key: (row: ViewRow) => SortKey
  ascending: boolean
}

/** A kind's keys are all numbers or all strings; strings compare as titles do. */
const compareKeys = (a: string | number, b: string | number): number =>
  typeof a === 'number' ? a - (b as number) : compareTitles(a, b as string)

function buildCriterion(
  c: SortCriterion,
  schema: PropertyDefinition[],
  contextIds: readonly string[],
): ResolvedCriterion | null {
  const column = resolveColumn(c.property_id, schema, contextIds)
  const sortKey = column && VALUE_KINDS[PROPERTY_TYPES[column.type].kind].sortKey
  if (!column || !sortKey) return null
  const key = sortKey(column.def, c.order)
  return {
    key: (row) => key(resolveFieldValue(row, column)),
    // A Custom order always reads ascending.
    ascending: c.order?.length ? true : c.direction !== 'descending',
  }
}

/** TableView's drag/manual-order gates read this, never the raw array length, so a dead criterion can't retire row reorder. */
export function resolvedSortCount(
  sort: SortCriterion[] | undefined,
  schema: PropertyDefinition[],
  contextIds: readonly string[],
): number {
  return (sort ?? []).filter((c) => buildCriterion(c, schema, contextIds) !== null).length
}

export function makeSorter(
  sort: SortCriterion[] | undefined,
  schema: PropertyDefinition[],
  contextIds: readonly string[],
  manualOrder?: string[],
): ((rows: ViewRow[]) => ViewRow[]) | null {
  const resolved = (sort ?? [])
    .map((c) => buildCriterion(c, schema, contextIds))
    .filter((rc): rc is ResolvedCriterion => rc !== null)
  // The manual order is the LOWEST-priority tiebreaker: it reorders only rows already equal on every real sort key, and is the sole comparator when a view is grouped but unsorted.
  const manualIndex = manualOrder?.length
    ? new Map(manualOrder.map((id, i) => [id, i] as const))
    : null
  if (resolved.length === 0 && !manualIndex) return null

  return (rows) => {
    const decorated = rows.map((row, offset) => ({
      offset,
      row,
      keys: resolved.map((rc) => rc.key(row)),
      manual: manualIndex ? (manualIndex.get(row.id) ?? Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) : 0,
    }))
    decorated.sort((a, b) => {
      for (let i = 0; i < resolved.length; i++) {
        const ka = a.keys[i]
        const kb = b.keys[i]
        if (ka === null || kb === null) {
          if (ka !== kb) return ka === null ? 1 : -1
          continue
        }
        const order = compareKeys(ka, kb)
        if (order !== 0) return resolved[i].ascending ? order : -order
      }
      if (a.manual !== b.manual) return a.manual - b.manual
      return a.offset - b.offset
    })
    return decorated.map((d) => d.row)
  }
}
```
