```Core/Views/valueKinds.ts (final)
// What each value kind does in a view: the operators the filter pane offers, how a rule tests a value, the key a sort compares, the band a grouping files a value under, and the value a new page takes from a rule, a band, or a sort neighbor.

import { localDayKey, pad } from '@pommora/uix/Utilities/pad'
import { foldKey } from '../Paths/caseFold'
import { optionIds, type PropertyDefinition } from '../Properties/properties'
import {
  checkboxValue,
  checkboxWord,
  isBlankValue,
  type PropertyValue,
  readNumber,
  selectedValues,
  type ValueKind,
} from '../Properties/propertyValue'
import { dayMs, type LocalDate, readDate, shownText } from '../Properties/formatValue'
import { FILTER_OPS } from './filterRules'
import type { DateGranularity } from './views'

type ValueSlot = 'none' | 'text' | 'number' | 'date' | 'chips' | 'set'

export interface OperatorChoice {
  op: string
  label: string
  slot: ValueSlot
  impliedValue?: string
  /** A typed folder name is an operand as well as a picked folder. */
  names?: true
}

export type ValueTest = (v: PropertyValue) => boolean
export type SortDirections = 'option' | 'text' | 'value'

export type ValueKindSpec = Readonly<{
  /** The operators the filter pane offers, in its menu's order; a hand-written rule may hold others the kind still answers. */
  ops: readonly OperatorChoice[]
  /** Is Empty matches a value this reads as unfilled, and Isn't Empty one it reads as filled. */
  filled: ValueTest
  /** A rule's test, its operands read once; undefined, so the rule abstains, for an op the kind doesn't answer or an operand that doesn't read. */
  prepare(op: string, want: readonly string[], def?: PropertyDefinition): ValueTest | undefined
  /** A criterion's key reader, built once per sort; a null key sorts last in either direction, and a kind with no reader doesn't sort. */
  sortKey?(
    def?: PropertyDefinition,
    order?: readonly string[],
  ): (v: PropertyValue) => string | number | null
  /** Which pair of words the Sort pane names a direction with. */
  directions: SortDirections
  /** The band a grouping files a value under; null files it with the value-less rows. */
  bucket?(v: PropertyValue, granularity: DateGranularity): string | null
  /** The value a new page takes from a rule naming one operand, null when the rule's op names none; a band's key seeds the value an Is rule naming it would. */
  seed?(op: string, operand: string): PropertyValue | null
  /** A page created beside another under a sort on this kind takes the other's value. */
  sortSeeds?: true
}>

const EMPTIES: OperatorChoice[] = [
  { op: FILTER_OPS.isEmpty, label: 'Is Empty', slot: 'none' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.isNotEmpty, label: "Isn't Empty", slot: 'none' },
]

const TEXT_OPS: OperatorChoice[] = [
  { op: FILTER_OPS.is, label: 'Is', slot: 'text' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.isNot, label: "Isn't", slot: 'text' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.startsWith, label: 'Starts With', slot: 'text' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.contains, label: 'Contains', slot: 'text' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.doesNotContain, label: "Doesn't Contain", slot: 'text' },
  ...EMPTIES,
]

/** The Starts and Ends ops are inclusive — the strict variants stay registered for hand-authored files, but the frame doesn't offer a second near-identical set. */
const DATE_OPS: OperatorChoice[] = [
  { op: FILTER_OPS.is, label: 'Is', slot: 'date' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.onOrBefore, label: 'Starts Before', slot: 'date' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.onOrAfter, label: 'Starts After', slot: 'date' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.endsOnOrBefore, label: 'Ends Before', slot: 'date' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.endsOnOrAfter, label: 'Ends After', slot: 'date' },
  ...EMPTIES,
]

const SET_OPS: OperatorChoice[] = [
  { op: FILTER_OPS.containsAny, label: 'Is Any', slot: 'chips' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.containsAll, label: 'Is All', slot: 'chips' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.doesNotContain, label: "Isn't", slot: 'chips' },
  ...EMPTIES,
]

const NUMBER_OPS: OperatorChoice[] = [
  { op: FILTER_OPS.is, label: 'Is', slot: 'number' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.isNot, label: "Isn't", slot: 'number' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.greaterThan, label: 'Greater Than', slot: 'number' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.greaterOrEqual, label: 'At Least', slot: 'number' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.lessThan, label: 'Less Than', slot: 'number' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.lessOrEqual, label: 'At Most', slot: 'number' },
  ...EMPTIES,
]

/** Is/Isn't are chip pickers whose multi-chips mean any-of/none-of — never Is All, which is unsatisfiable on a one-value property. */
const OPTION_OPS: OperatorChoice[] = [
  { op: FILTER_OPS.is, label: 'Is', slot: 'chips' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.isNot, label: "Isn't", slot: 'chips' },
  ...EMPTIES,
]

const CHECKBOX_OPS: OperatorChoice[] = [
  { op: FILTER_OPS.is, label: 'Is Checked', slot: 'none', impliedValue: 'true' },
  { op: FILTER_OPS.is, label: "Isn't Checked", slot: 'none', impliedValue: 'false' },
]

const LIST_OPS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([FILTER_OPS.containsAny, FILTER_OPS.containsAll])

const notBlank: ValueTest = (v) => !isBlankValue(v)
const showsText: ValueTest = (v) => !!shownText(v)

/** Is and Isn't compare a value's whole shown text, and the others search within it, folded on both sides. */
function prepareText(
  op: string,
  want: readonly string[],
  def?: PropertyDefinition,
): ValueTest | undefined {
  const w = want.map(foldKey)
  const shown = (v: PropertyValue): string | null => {
    const s = shownText(v, def)
    return s === null ? null : foldKey(s)
  }
  const is: ValueTest = (v) => {
    const f = shown(v)
    return f !== null && w.includes(f)
  }
  const contains: ValueTest = (v) => shown(v)?.includes(w[0]) ?? false
  switch (op) {
    case FILTER_OPS.is:
      return is
    case FILTER_OPS.isNot:
      return (v) => !is(v)
    case FILTER_OPS.contains:
      return contains
    case FILTER_OPS.doesNotContain:
      return (v) => !contains(v)
    case FILTER_OPS.startsWith:
      return (v) => shown(v)?.startsWith(w[0]) ?? false
    default:
      return undefined
  }
}

/** Is and the containing ops match a value holding any operand, Is All one holding every operand, and the two negations a value holding none. */
function prepareMembers(op: string, want: readonly string[]): ValueTest | undefined {
  const any: ValueTest = (v) => selectedValues(v).some((x) => want.includes(x))
  switch (op) {
    case FILTER_OPS.containsAll:
      return (v) => {
        const xs = selectedValues(v)
        return want.every((w) => xs.includes(w))
      }
    case FILTER_OPS.is:
    case FILTER_OPS.contains:
    case FILTER_OPS.containsAny:
      return any
    case FILTER_OPS.isNot:
    case FILTER_OPS.doesNotContain:
      return (v) => !any(v)
    default:
      return undefined
  }
}

function prepareNumber(op: string, want: readonly string[]): ValueTest | undefined {
  const e = readNumber(want[0])
  if (e === undefined) return undefined
  const holds =
    (test: (n: number) => boolean): ValueTest =>
    (v) =>
      v.kind === 'number' && test(v.value)
  const is = holds((n) => n === e)
  switch (op) {
    case FILTER_OPS.is:
      return is
    case FILTER_OPS.isNot:
      return (v) => !is(v)
    case FILTER_OPS.greaterThan:
      return holds((n) => n > e)
    case FILTER_OPS.lessThan:
      return holds((n) => n < e)
    case FILTER_OPS.greaterOrEqual:
      return holds((n) => n >= e)
    case FILTER_OPS.lessOrEqual:
      return holds((n) => n <= e)
    default:
      return undefined
  }
}

/** Days are the local days the cells show. `is` matches a day the value spans; a bare-day operand orders by day, and one carrying a time orders by instant. The Starts ops and the strict pair read a span's start, the Ends ops its end. */
function prepareDate(op: string, want: readonly string[]): ValueTest | undefined {
  const target = readDate(want[0])
  if (target === null) return undefined
  const ms = (x: Date): number => (target.timed ? x.getTime() : dayMs(x))
  const e = ms(target.at)
  const day = dayMs(target.at)
  // A clockless end holds its whole day, so a timed operand meets it at the day's last instant.
  const endMs = (d: LocalDate): number => {
    const last = d.end ?? d.at
    return d.timed || !target.timed
      ? ms(last)
      : new Date(last.getFullYear(), last.getMonth(), last.getDate() + 1).getTime() - 1
  }
  const dated =
    (test: (d: LocalDate) => boolean): ValueTest =>
    (v) => {
      const d = v.kind === 'dateTime' ? readDate(v.value) : null
      return d !== null && test(d)
    }
  switch (op) {
    case FILTER_OPS.is:
      return dated((d) => dayMs(d.at) <= day && day <= dayMs(d.end ?? d.at))
    case FILTER_OPS.isBefore:
      return dated((d) => ms(d.at) < e)
    case FILTER_OPS.isAfter:
      return dated((d) => ms(d.at) > e)
    case FILTER_OPS.onOrAfter:
      return dated((d) => ms(d.at) >= e)
    case FILTER_OPS.onOrBefore:
      return dated((d) => ms(d.at) <= e)
    case FILTER_OPS.endsOnOrAfter:
      return dated((d) => endMs(d) >= e)
    case FILTER_OPS.endsOnOrBefore:
      return dated((d) => endMs(d) <= e)
    default:
      return undefined
  }
}

function prepareCheckbox(op: string, want: readonly string[]): ValueTest | undefined {
  const checked = checkboxWord(want[0])
  if (checked === null) return undefined
  const is: ValueTest = (v) => (v.kind === 'checkbox') === checked
  switch (op) {
    case FILTER_OPS.is:
      return is
    case FILTER_OPS.isNot:
      return (v) => !is(v)
    default:
      return undefined
  }
}

const textKey =
  (def?: PropertyDefinition) =>
  (v: PropertyValue): string | null =>
    shownText(v, def) || null

/** A Custom order leads with its saved options and appends the ones it predates; a value no option holds sorts with the value-less rows. */
function optionKey(def?: PropertyDefinition, order: readonly string[] = []) {
  const listed = new Set(order)
  const ids = [...order, ...(def ? optionIds(def) : []).filter((id) => !listed.has(id))]
  const rank = new Map(ids.map((id, i) => [id, i]))
  return (v: PropertyValue): number | null => (v.kind === 'select' ? (rank.get(v.value) ?? null) : null)
}

/** UTC arithmetic, so adding days never crosses a DST boundary. A week belongs to the year of its Thursday; weeks start Monday. */
function isoWeek(year: number, month: number, day: number): [year: number, week: number] {
  const d = new Date(Date.UTC(year, month, day))
  d.setUTCDate(d.getUTCDate() + 4 - (d.getUTCDay() || 7))
  const yearStart = Date.UTC(d.getUTCFullYear(), 0, 1)
  const week = Math.ceil(((d.getTime() - yearStart) / 86400000 + 1) / 7)
  return [d.getUTCFullYear(), week]
}

/** Zero-padded so lexicographic order IS chronological. Buckets by the local day the cell shows, so a date-only value keeps the day the user picked. */
function dateBucketKey(iso: string, granularity: DateGranularity): string | null {
  const d = readDate(iso)?.at
  if (!d) return null
  const year = d.getFullYear()
  const month = d.getMonth()
  const day = d.getDate()
  switch (granularity) {
    case 'year':
      return pad(year, 4)
    case 'month':
      return `${pad(year, 4)}-${pad(month + 1, 2)}`
    case 'day':
      return localDayKey(d)
    case 'week': {
      const [wy, w] = isoWeek(year, month, day)
      return `${pad(wy, 4)}-W${pad(w, 2)}`
    }
  }
}

const PROSE: ValueKindSpec = {
  ops: TEXT_OPS,
  filled: showsText,
  prepare: prepareText,
  sortKey: textKey,
  directions: 'text',
}

export const VALUE_KINDS: Readonly<Record<ValueKind, ValueKindSpec>> = {
  text: PROSE,
  link: PROSE,
  number: {
    ops: NUMBER_OPS,
    filled: notBlank,
    prepare: prepareNumber,
    sortKey: () => (v) => (v.kind === 'number' ? v.value : null),
    directions: 'value',
    sortSeeds: true,
  },
  dateTime: {
    ops: DATE_OPS,
    filled: (v) => v.kind === 'dateTime' && readDate(v.value) !== null,
    prepare: prepareDate,
    sortKey: () => (v) =>
      v.kind === 'dateTime' ? (readDate(v.value)?.at.getTime() ?? null) : null,
    directions: 'value',
    bucket: (v, granularity) =>
      v.kind === 'dateTime' ? dateBucketKey(v.value, granularity) : null,
    sortSeeds: true,
  },
  // An unchecked box draws as one: Is Empty still matches it, as the filter always has, while the sort keeps it in the run its direction orders rather than with the value-less tail.
  checkbox: {
    ops: CHECKBOX_OPS,
    filled: notBlank,
    prepare: prepareCheckbox,
    sortKey: () => (v) => (v.kind === 'checkbox' ? 1 : 0),
    directions: 'value',
    bucket: (v) => (v.kind === 'checkbox' ? 'true' : null),
    seed: (op, operand) =>
      op === FILTER_OPS.is ? checkboxValue(checkboxWord(operand) === true) : null,
    sortSeeds: true,
  },
  // Is and Isn't name whole options; the text ops a hand-written rule may hold search the option's label.
  select: {
    ops: OPTION_OPS,
    filled: notBlank,
    prepare: (op, want, def) =>
      op === FILTER_OPS.is || op === FILTER_OPS.isNot
        ? prepareMembers(op, want)
        : prepareText(op, want, def),
    sortKey: optionKey,
    directions: 'option',
    bucket: (v) => (v.kind === 'select' ? v.value : null),
    seed: (op, operand) => (op === FILTER_OPS.is ? { kind: 'select', value: operand } : null),
    sortSeeds: true,
  },
  multiSelect: {
    ops: SET_OPS,
    filled: notBlank,
    prepare: prepareMembers,
    sortKey: textKey,
    directions: 'text',
    seed: (op, operand) => (LIST_OPS.has(op) ? { kind: 'multiSelect', value: [operand] } : null),
  },
  context: {
    ops: SET_OPS,
    filled: notBlank,
    prepare: prepareMembers,
    directions: 'value',

A signature cache would compile once per distinct prune.
- `MatrixRuntime.sync` (`Core/Matrix/matrixRuntime.ts:122-151`) reruns `matrixVisible` when the filter changes, only while the Matrix shows (`:130-133`). `matrix:write` (`Core/Contract/bridge.ts:232`) takes `{ filter: { rules, enabled } }`, as the Metadata Drive writes it (`.claude/scripts/Metadata Drive/live-drive.mjs:212`). A Context rule is one every Space answers (`answers`' `'context'` arm), and the loop adds each Space to its own Context's ids before filtering (`matrixInput.ts:119-128`), so every Space compiles and evaluates the whole rule: the case a signature cache would collapse into one compile.

##### Behavior Changes and Disclosures

- **An Unreadable Filter Value Is Ignored (K-1, Nathan's Intent):** a rule whose value doesn't read (letters in a Number filter, a word that isn't a date, a Checkbox word that isn't one) no longer matches every page: it sits out, so inside an Any group the other rules decide, and a new page created in that view inherits from the rule that does decide.
- **An Operator a Kind Doesn't Answer Is Ignored (an Accident Fixed; LC-48):** a hand-written rule whose operator its kind doesn't answer (`greater_than` on a Checkbox, `contains_any` on a Select, `is_not` on a Date) sits out where it matched every page. The pane never writes one. K-1 rules on values that don't read, not on operators, so this rides LC-48's accidents fixed along the way. **Recommended:** take it; a rule that can't test a value shouldn't decide an Any group.
- **Checkbox "Is Not Empty" Works (K-1):** it shows checked pages only, which only a hand-written rule holds, since the pane offers a Checkbox only Is Checked and Isn't Checked (`CHECKBOX_OPS`, HEAD `Core/Views/filterModel.ts:94-97`).
- **Empty Values Sort Last for Every Type, Both Directions (K-2, a Reading Nathan Didn't Object To):** Number, Date, Creation Time, Last Modified, Select, Status, Text, Link, Multi-Select, and File put the pages holding no value at the bottom whichever way the sort runs. Today empty Numbers, Dates, and texts led an ascending sort and empty Selects led a descending one. Dragging a row into another value's run in a single-sorted view keeps reassigning, the empty run included.
- **Checkbox Keeps Both Its Readings (LC-53):** an unchecked box reads as no value on disk. The filter keeps today's reading, so Is Empty matches an unchecked box and Isn't Empty a checked one (K-1's fix). The sort keeps today's order: applying K-2 literally would put every unchecked page last in both directions and make the Checkbox sort's direction do nothing, so the record treats an unchecked box as a value there, as it draws (P3's `blankDraws`): ascending puts unchecked first, descending checked first. The one entry states both, with the reason beside it. **Recommended:** keep both; a Checkbox has no empty state on screen, and "empty sorts last" was written about values that can be missing. Nathan's call if he reads K-2 otherwise.
- **A Custom Order Reads Ascending for Any Kind:** `buildCriterion` forces ascending whenever a criterion carries an `order`, where only the Select arm did. Only a Select criterion is written with one (the Sort pane's Custom, `SortFrame.tsx:188`), so nothing changes for a criterion any path writes.
- **Hidden Changes:** none beyond the above. The record is read only by the renderer; nothing on disk changes shape.

```Core/Properties/Pickers/pickModel.ts (new)
import {
  groupOptions,
  optionGroupsOf,
  type OptionPickKind,
  pickKindOf,
  type PickOption,
  type PropertyDefinition,
} from '../properties'
import { type PropertyValue, selectedValues } from '../propertyValue'

export type PickGroup = { id: string; options: PickOption[] }
export type PickCommit = { index: number; next: PropertyValue | null }

export const pickGroups = (def: PropertyDefinition, contextOptions?: PickOption[]): PickGroup[] =>
  contextOptions
    ? [{ id: def.id, options: contextOptions }]
    : optionGroupsOf(def)
        .map((g) => ({ id: g.id, options: groupOptions(g).map((o) => ({ ...o, value: o.id })) }))
        .filter((g) => g.options.length > 0)

export const toggleValue = (selected: string[], value: string): string[] =>
  selected.includes(value) ? selected.filter((v) => v !== value) : [...selected, value]

const pickKind = (def: PropertyDefinition): OptionPickKind => pickKindOf(def.type) ?? 'select'

// A value every row holds leaves them all; otherwise it lands on each row lacking it, a Select replacing what the row held and a list joining it.
function pickCommits(kind: OptionPickKind, rows: string[][], value: string): PickCommit[] {
  const all = rows.every((own) => own.includes(value))
  return rows.flatMap((own, index) => {
    if (own.includes(value) !== all) return []
    if (kind !== 'select') return [{ index, next: { kind, value: toggleValue(own, value) } }]
    return [{ index, next: all ? null : { kind, value } }]
  })
}

/** One pick over one row or many: what every row holds reads as picked, and a Select's picker closes once picked, since a Select holds one value. */
export function pickOver(
  def: PropertyDefinition,
  currents: readonly (PropertyValue | null)[],
  onCommit: (commits: PickCommit[]) => void,
  onClose: () => void,
): { selected: string[]; pick: (value: string) => void } {
  const kind = pickKind(def)
  const rows = currents.map(selectedValues)
  return {
    selected: rows[0].filter((v) => rows.every((own) => own.includes(v))),
    pick: (value) => {
      onCommit(pickCommits(kind, rows, value))
      if (kind === 'select') onClose()
    },
  }
}

export const pickedValue = (
  def: PropertyDefinition,
  current: PropertyValue | null,
  value: string,
): PropertyValue | null => pickCommits(pickKind(def), [selectedValues(current)], value)[0].next
```

import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest'
import type { PropertyDefinition } from '../properties'
import type { PropertyValue } from '../propertyValue'
import { type PickCommit, pickGroups, pickOver } from './pickModel'

const def = (type: 'select' | 'multiSelect' | 'context'): PropertyDefinition =>
  type === 'context'
    ? { id: 'ctx_areas', label: '', key: '', type }
    : {
        id: 'prop_p',
        label: 'P',
        key: 'P',
        type,
        select_options: [
          { id: 'opt_a', key: 'a', label: 'a' },
          { id: 'opt_b', key: 'b', label: 'b' },
          { id: 'opt_c', key: 'c', label: 'c' },
        ],
      }
const select = (value: string): PropertyValue => ({ kind: 'select', value })
const multi = (...value: string[]): PropertyValue => ({ kind: 'multiSelect', value })
const spaces = (...value: string[]): PropertyValue => ({ kind: 'context', value })

/** The commits one pick of `value` makes over `currents`, and whether it closed the picker. */
function pickOf(d: PropertyDefinition, currents: (PropertyValue | null)[], value: string) {
  const onCommit = vi.fn<(commits: PickCommit[]) => void>()
  const onClose = vi.fn()
  pickOver(d, currents, onCommit, onClose).pick(value)
  return { commits: onCommit.mock.calls[0][0], closed: onClose.mock.calls.length > 0 }
}

describe('pickGroups', () => {
  it('offers an option under its id and names it by its label, never by its key', () => {
    const named = { ...def('select'), select_options: [{ id: 'opt_new', key: 'new', label: 'New' }] }
    const offered = pickGroups(named).flatMap((g) => g.options)
    expect(offered.map((o) => [o.value, o.label])).toEqual([['opt_new', 'New']])
  })
})

describe('pickOver', () => {
  it('marks as picked only what every row holds', () => {
    const rows = [multi('opt_a', 'opt_b'), multi('opt_a'), multi('opt_a', 'opt_c')]
    expect(pickOver(def('multiSelect'), rows, vi.fn(), vi.fn()).selected).toEqual(['opt_a'])
    expect(pickOver(def('select'), [select('opt_a'), select('opt_b')], vi.fn(), vi.fn()).selected).toEqual([])
  })

  it('a list value joins every row lacking it, keeps what each holds, and leaves the picker open', () => {
    const { commits, closed } = pickOf(def('multiSelect'), [multi('opt_a'), multi('opt_b', 'opt_c'), null], 'opt_b')
    expect(commits).toEqual([
      { index: 0, next: multi('opt_a', 'opt_b') },
      { index: 2, next: multi('opt_b') },
    ])
    expect(closed).toBe(false)
  })

  it('a list value every row holds leaves each of them', () => {
    expect(pickOf(def('context'), [spaces('a', 'b'), spaces('b', 'c')], 'b').commits).toEqual([
      { index: 0, next: spaces('a') },
      { index: 1, next: spaces('c') },
    ])
  })

  it('a Select lands on every row not already holding it, and closes the picker', () => {

+// Rebuilt after every render, so an undo reads the surface's newest rows, and emptied on unmount, so an undo after it reverts nothing.
+export function useValueWriter(
+  host: Pick<ValueWriter, 'rowOf'> & { setOverride: SetOverrides },
+): RefObject<ValueWriter | null> {
+  const writer = useRef<ValueWriter | null>(null)
+  useEffect(() => {
+    writer.current = {

+    return () => {

+    }
+  })
+  return writer

+/** A writer for one row no surface shows, as the native menu's pick writes it; the row it keeps takes each pick, so its undo reads what was written. */
+export function oneShotWriter(opened: ViewRow): RefObject<ValueWriter> {
+  let row = opened
+  return {
+    current: {
+      rowOf: (id) => (id === row.id ? row : undefined),
+      apply: (_, picked) => {
+        row = { ...row, picked: { ...row.picked, ...picked } }
+      },
+    },
+  }
+}

#### Task 15-4

**TASK:** One row-menu vocabulary: `hideable` names what Remove takes a value out of, a view's columns or the Properties panel's rows, and a column with no look in hand is a bare value, so the value seat's one row menu (Task 16A-1's `menu`, the panel's in Task 16B-2) asks `cellMenuContextFor` for every surface (06-06, B-06-01).

**NOW:**
- **A Boolean That Means Two Things:** `CellMenuContext.hideable` is a boolean (`Core/Actions/cellMenu.ts:27,41,47-51`), and `cellMenuModel`'s closing label is `'Remove from View'` for every hideable `file` context (`:94`). That's true of cards, whose Remove hides the column from the view (`CardValue.tsx:93` → `onHide`), and false of the panel, whose Remove clears the value and un-reveals the row (`emptyRow(id, false)`, `PropertyPanel.tsx:314-318`).

The panel holds no column look and offers Clear for every filled value, so the seat, whose host answers `style` as `ColumnStyle | null` (Task 16A-1), needs `cellMenuContextFor` to answer a bare value when the style is `null`.

```Core/Views/Settings/useMultiValue.ts (after; moved from valueField.tsx)
import { useState } from 'react'
import { sameItems } from '@pommora/uix/Utilities/same'
import { toggleValue } from '../../Properties/Pickers/pickModel'

export function useMultiValue(
  values: string[],
  onCommit: (next: string[]) => void,
): { shown: string[]; toggle: (v: string) => void } {
  const [local, setLocal] = useState<string[] | null>(null)
  if (local && sameItems(local, values)) setLocal(null)
  const shown = local ?? values
  const toggle = (v: string): void => {
    const next = toggleValue(shown, v)
    setLocal(next)
    onCommit(next)
  }
  return { shown, toggle }
}
```

#### Task 15-8

**TASK:** Measure a 300-row mass assign of a Select on `~/Benchmark-Large` and settle `setProperty`'s shape by *§Measurement Rules › 02-10*'s rule: **Pass** — total wall time at most 1,500 ms with no main-thread task over 100 ms, and `setProperty` stays one path per op; **Fail** — `setProperty` takes `paths: string[]` in place of `path`, one op under each file's own lock and one reply, inside this phase.

**NOW:**
- **The Path Measured:** a sweep of a Table column's cells (`useCellSweep`, `Core/Views/Table/cellSweep.ts:21-80`) opens `MassPropertyPicker` over the swept rows (`TableView.tsx:315-376`); a pick hands `pickOver`'s commits to `groupUndo(() => { for (…) commitValue(rows[index], col, next) })`, so 300 rows send 300 `setProperty` requests through `assignValue` in one synchronous loop, each laying its own pending override, and each reply settles its own override (`patchOverride`'s `.then`).
- **Why a Tall Viewport:** the table virtualizes its rows, and the sweep measures only the `.data-row` elements in the DOM (`cellSweep.ts:30-37`), so at window height it can't reach 300 rows; with the page emulated at 14,000 px tall (`Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride`) every one of 300 rows renders and the real gesture covers them.
- **Why a Fresh Select:** a pick lands only on rows not already holding it (Task 15-1's rule), and the generator fills its Selects at random (`make-benchmark-nexus.mjs:144`), so a property `addProperty` creates for the run gives exactly 300 writes.
- **Long Tasks:** the drive harness's `probed()` counts long-task entries by start time and keeps no duration (`drive-harness.mjs:32,54`), so the script observes `longtask` entries' `duration` itself.
- **The Benchmark:** `large` is 25,000 pages over 25 Collections (`make-benchmark-nexus.mjs:13`); no `~/Benchmark-*` is on disk; the generator's sweep removes a build and its index under `~/Library/Application Support/Pommora/Nexuses/<id>` (`:42-63`); `nexus:openPath` opens a Nexus (`Core/Contract/bridge.ts:66`).

+/** One value onto each path, each file under its own lock, answered once: the first refusal stops the run, and the put-back covers every file written before it. */
+async function valuesAt(
+  req: { paths: string[] },
+  one: (path: string) => Promise<MutateReply>,
+): Promise<MutateReply> {
+  const entries: PutBack[] = []
+  for (const path of req.paths) {
+    const reply = await one(path)
+    if (!reply.ok) return reply
+    if (reply.value.undo?.op === 'putBack') entries.push(...reply.value.undo.entries)
+  }
+  return ok(entries.length ? { undo: { op: 'putBack', entries } } : {})
+}

### Phase 16A — One Value Seat: The Seat, the Table, and Cards

**GOAL:** Clicking, right-clicking, and editing a value becomes one shared seat, `Core/Properties/Cells/ValueSeat.tsx`, which owns the intent dispatch, the menu chain, the open-value state, the inline editor, the pick target, and the floating panes; each surface hands it only what it genuinely does differently. The table's and Cards' hand-wired copies move onto it, `CardValue.tsx` and `useViewHost.pickTarget` leave, and the three interleavings the Findings left open — Cards' ghost hold, the table's title-action passthrough, and `lastOpened` keying — are settled and pinned. It's a phase of its own because the panel and the native menu's router keep their own copies until Phase 16B, so its head is shippable with two surfaces on the seat.

**Builds On:** P2's `ColumnType` and Filedata origin (`specOf(t).origin === 'filedata'`; `FILEDATA.createdAt.id`); P3's `blankDraws`; P4's `Core/Properties/fieldValue.ts`; P6's writer; P13's `ResolvedColumn = { id; kind; type; def? }`, `resolveColumn`/`propertyColumn`/`contextColumn` (`Core/Views/Pipeline/columns.ts`), `resolveFieldValue(row, column)`, the host's `styleById`, `styleOf(column)`, and `setStylePatch(column, key, value)`, `useColumns`' `runStyleAction(column, action)`, and Cards' `addedColumn(id)` over entries carrying `column`; P15's `pickModel.ts` (`pickGroups`, `pickOver`, `pickedValue`, `toggleValue`), `useValueWriter`/`oneShotWriter`, `cellMenuContextFor(type, style | null, filled, { hideable?: 'view' | 'row', … })`, `cardColumns.ts`, the link menus' Rename-then-Edit-Link order, and `syntheticContextDef`, which stays in `PropertyPicker.tsx` with its sites for this plan to delete.

**Order:** 16A-1 writes the seat with its tests, and it commits with 16A-2, which moves the table, its first reader; 16A-3 moves Cards. Phase 16B folds the native router, moves the panel, folds `rename`, and removes the fabricated definition; the Findings order that last fold first, and landing it last edits only code that survives (*§Departures From the Findings › Task Order*).

**Diff Convention:** a `-  …` line elides the lines of a removed range named on the line beside it (HEAD's, or the named phase's where it rewrote them), up to the `-` line after it; a `-` line written `head { … }   (HEAD :a-b)` removes the whole block that opens with `head`, the range cited; every other `-` line is literal.

+/** One value's click, right-click, and editing, shared by the table, cards, the Properties panel, and the menus that open away from a value. */
+export function useValueSeat(host: SeatHost) {
+  const tree = useSession((s) => s.tree)
+  const [open, setOpen] = useState<SeatOpen | null>(null)
+  const anchor = useRef<HTMLElement | null>(null)
+  const opens = useRef(0)
+  const close = (): void => {

+    host.onClose?.()

+  // A pane whose anchor left the page closes: its row is gone, or a compact card dropped the value it just cleared.

+    }

+      popover: ({ seat }) => float('popover', seat),

+  }

+      !label && value.kind === 'link'
+        ? linkMenuTarget(
+            resolveLink(readLinkText(value.value), host.connections?.()?.index, host.holder(row)),
+            true,
+            { hideable: host.hide?.from },
+          )
+        : null
+    if (link) {
+      const action = await hold(() => showConnectionMenu(link))
+      if (action) act(action)
+      return
+    }
+    const filled = !isBlankValue(value)
+    const context = cellMenuContextFor(column.type, host.style(column), filled, {
+      hideable: host.hide?.from,
+      barCapable: numberBarCapable(column.def),
+      onChip: chip !== null,
+    })
+    if (!context) return
+    const action = await hold(() => popMenu(cellMenuModel(context)))
+    const commit = (next: PropertyValue | null): void => host.commit(row, column, next)
+    if (!action || runFileMenuAction(action, column.def, value, chip, commit) || act(action)) return
+    const style = parseStyleAction(action)
+    if (style) host.setStyle?.(column, style.key, style.value)
+  }
+
+  const editor = (row: ViewRow, column: ResolvedColumn): React.ReactNode =>
+    open?.mode === 'editor' &&
+    open.rowId === row.id &&
+    open.column.id === column.id &&
+    column.def ? (
+      <PropertyValueInput
+        def={column.def}
+        current={resolveFieldValue(row, column)}
+        holder={host.holder(row)}
+        connections={host.connections}
+        seat={open.seat}
+        onCommit={(next) => host.commit(row, column, next)}
+        onClose={close}
+      />
+    ) : null
+
+  /** A row never lists itself among a Context's Spaces; a page row's id names no Space, so it excludes nothing. */
+  const target = (row: ViewRow, column: ResolvedColumn): PickTarget => {
+    const current = resolveFieldValue(row, column)
+    const style = host.style(column)
+    if (column.type === 'dateTime')
+      return {
+        kind: 'dateTime',
+        def: column.def ?? syntheticContextDef(column.id),
+        current,
+        dateFormat: style?.date_format,
+        timeFormat: style?.time_format,
+      }
+    if (column.def?.type === 'file') return { kind: 'file', def: column.def, current }
+    const { setStyle } = host
+    return {
+      kind: 'options',
+      def: column.def ?? syntheticContextDef(column.id),
+      current,
+      style: setStyle && style ? { current: style, set: (key, value) => setStyle(column, key, value) } : undefined,
+      contextOptions:
+        column.type === 'context' && tree ? contextOptionsFor(column.id, tree, row.id) : undefined,
+    }
+  }
+
+  return { open, anchor, host, close, intentOf, run, click, pane, menu, editor, target }
+}
+
+/** A surface's add chooser, shown in the seat's picker so a drilled-in value opens in the same pane. */
+export type SeatChooser = {
+  entries: PickEntry[]
+  resolveTarget?: (entry: PickEntry) => PickTarget | null
+  onCommit?: (value: PropertyValue | null, entry: PickEntry) => void
+  onReveal: (entry: PickEntry) => void
+  onDismiss: () => void
+}
+
+/** The seat's floating panes: one picker, which a surface's add chooser shares, and one typed-value popover. Each holds the value it last opened on through its exit; the picker mounts fresh for another value and the popover for every open. */
+export function ValueSeat({
+  seat,
+  chooser,
+}: {
+  seat: ValueSeatApi
+  chooser?: SeatChooser | null
+}): React.JSX.Element {
+  const { open, host } = seat
+  const last = useRef<{ picker?: SeatOpen; popover?: SeatOpen }>({})
+  if (open?.mode === 'picker' || open?.mode === 'popover') last.current[open.mode] = open
+  const picked = last.current.picker
+  const pickRow = picked && host.rowOf(picked.rowId)
+  const typed = last.current.popover
+  const typedRow = typed && host.rowOf(typed.rowId)
+  return (
+    <>
+      <PropertyPicker
+        key={picked ? `${picked.rowId}:${picked.column.id}` : 'none'}
+        target={!chooser && picked && pickRow ? seat.target(pickRow, picked.column) : null}
+        chooser={chooser?.entries}
+        resolveTarget={chooser?.resolveTarget}
+        open={open?.mode === 'picker' || chooser != null}
+        triggerRef={seat.anchor}
+        anchorX={open?.mode === 'picker' ? open.x : undefined}
+        onCommit={(value, entry) => {
+          if (entry) chooser?.onCommit?.(value, entry)
+          else if (picked && pickRow) host.commit(pickRow, picked.column, value)
+        }}
+        onReveal={chooser?.onReveal}
+        onDismiss={() => {
+          seat.close()
+          chooser?.onDismiss()
+        }}
+      />
+      {typed && typedRow && typed.column.def && (
+        <PropertyValueInput
+          key={`${typed.rowId}:${typed.column.id}:${typed.nonce}`}
+          popover={{ open: open?.mode === 'popover', triggerRef: seat.anchor }}
+          def={typed.column.def}
+          current={resolveFieldValue(typedRow, typed.column)}
+          holder={host.holder(typedRow)}
+          connections={host.connections}
+          seat={typed.seat}
+          onCommit={(next) => host.commit(typedRow, typed.column, next)}
+          onClose={seat.close}
+        />
+      )}
+    </>
+  )
+}
```

#### Task 16A-3

**TASK:** Cards run every value through the seat. `CardValue.tsx` leaves, its span folding into `CardProperties`; `CardsView`'s value-picker request, its held popover, its two close effects, and its own picker and popover leave, and the Add chooser shows in the seat's picker. The inline field's ghost hold moves to `CardsView` as Cards' one genuine difference beside the seat, and `useViewHost.pickTarget` leaves with its last reader.

**NOW:**
- `CardValue` (`Core/Views/Cards/CardValue.tsx`, 171 lines) holds the inline-field state (`:59`), the ghost hold while it is open (`:60-67`, a promise held through `GhostSuppress`), the intent map (`:74-94`), the click (`:98-104`), the right-click chain (`:106-131`, each menu inside `holdGhost`, Remove offered through `hideable: 'view'`), and the span with its inline editor or `Cell` (`:133-170`). Its two portal guards (`:102`, `:110`) name a picker inside the span; no pane renders there (`git grep -n "createPortal\|PickerMenu\|FieldPicker" -- Core/Properties/Cells` answers nothing, and the inline `PropertyValueInput` passes no `popover`), so both guard a state no path produces. Its one importer is `CardsView.tsx:60`.
- `CardsView` holds `ValuePickerRequest` and `PROPERTY_PICKER_KINDS` (`:79-88`), `valuePicker` (`:176`), the shared anchor (`:209`), an effect closing the picker when its row leaves or a compact card's value goes blank (`:211-219`, skipped for a chooser-opened pick through `revealOnCommit`), the picker target and held popover (`:224-232`), `commitPicked` revealing a chooser-picked property (`:233-241`), and its popover and one `PropertyPicker` shared by values and the Add chooser (`:486-537`). A chooser entry that is a Date or File swaps into that picker; any other non-drillable entry opens the popover (`:520-532`).
- `revealProperty` (`Core/Views/Host/useViewHost.ts:160-165`) returns at once for a property the view already shows, so revealing on every non-blank commit reveals only what the chooser added.
- A compact card drops a blank value's span (`shownColumnsFor`, `cardColumns.ts` since P15), so "the value went blank on a compact card" and "the pane's anchor left the page" are the same event, which the seat's anchor rule (Task 16A-1) closes on.
- `CardFace` and `PageCard` are memoized (`CardsView.tsx:742`, `:906`); the table hands its memoized rows the open cell by prop (`TableView.tsx:466-468`).
- `cardGestures.test.tsx` pins a status click, the card menu, and the link menu (`:130-212`); `cardCreation.test.tsx` holds the ghost harness (`:69-95`).

##### Departures From the Findings

- **The Seat Commits With the Table:** the seat has no production reader until the table moves onto it, so Task 16A-1 writes it and its tests, and Task 16A-2's commit lands it beside its first surface (*§Plan Constraints › Sequencing*); `seatHost` lands there too, read by the table and then by Cards.
- **`hideable` Is One Union in Both Menus:** the link menu's Remove was a boolean while P15 made the cell menu's `'view' | 'row'`, and the seat would have handed one host fact to the two menus in two shapes. `LinkMenuContext.value.hideable` and `SeatHost.hide.from` read P15's `HideFrom` from Task 16A-1, which edits the three surviving `valueMenuTarget` calls by a token each; Tasks 16A-2, 16A-3, and 16B-2 then delete those lines with their files' copies. `columnMenu.ts`' `hideable` names a different fact, a column the header menu can hide, and stays a boolean.
- **Task Order:** the Findings order the fabricated definition first (3, 1, 2, 4). Landing it first would edit `useViewHost.pickTarget`, the panel's `panelTarget` and `editRow`, the presenter's target, and the Cards popover's definition read, each of which a later task deletes; it lands last (16B-3), and the seat carries `column.def ?? syntheticContextDef(column.id)` until then. The seat (1), the router (2), and the panel's split (4) keep the Findings' order among themselves.
- **`SeatHost` Holds Every Genuine Difference:** the Findings name four members (`anchor`, `hideable`, `commit`, `rowMenu`). The seat also needs each surface's row read (`rowOf`), the holder and connections a typed value parses links against, the column style and its write (`style`, `setStyle`), Cards' centering (`centered`), the ghost hold around menus (`hold`), the panel's Clear (`clear`), and the menu seat's release of its request (`onClose`). `hideable` is `hide.from`, P15's `'view' | 'row'`, so a host can't offer Remove without saying what Remove does. No `rowMenu` hook is needed: P15's `cellMenuContextFor(type, null, …)` builds the panel's menu, so the panel's `style` answers `null`. Six members are shared by both views and come from one `seatHost` the view host builds.

A property leaf in a title or card menu keeps reaching the app-level picker through `requestPick`, anchored at the same glyph.

The table's editor keeps suppressing the ghost and hiding its row, so neither surface's behavior moves.

The table's `lastOpened` and `lastCell` and Cards' `useHeld` popover fold into it; the panel's unheld popover folds in Phase 16B.
- **The Anchor Rule Replaces Three Closes, and Reaches a Fourth Case:** a pane closes when the element it anchors on leaves the page — the table's vanished-row close, Cards' vanished-row close, and Cards' compact-blank close (a compact card drops a blank value's span) stated once — which makes `revealOnCommit` unnecessary. The same rule closes a pane whose row is redrawn under another band, since the cell it opened from is replaced: a Date pick in a view grouped by that Date (*§Behavior Changes and Disclosures*). One rule for every surface is kept over the alternative, a row-gone check plus a compact-card check, which is two rules again.

##### Behavior Changes and Disclosures

Each item is visible, classified, and carries a recommendation; the reconciliation report lists them for Nathan.

- **A Chooser-Added Date or File Remounts the Picker (Earlier Agent's Choice Made Consistent; Take):** on a card, a Date or File picked from the Add chooser opens its pane as a fresh picker at the same anchor, the per-value keying every value pick uses, where today the chooser's content swaps in place.
- **Cards' Picker Remounts per Value (Consistency; Take):** the table's keying applies to Cards: moving from one value's picker to another's mounts a fresh picker rather than reusing the open one.
- **A Date Picked Into Another Band Closes Its Calendar (Accident; Take; LC-59):** in a table or Cards view grouped by a Date, a pick that moves the row to another band closes the calendar after that one click, since the row is redrawn under its new band and the cell the calendar opened from leaves the page (`TableView.tsx:446-495` nests each row under its band, and Cards do the same). At HEAD the calendar stays open (`DateTimeValuePicker.tsx:30` commits without closing, and no picker checks its trigger is still on the page), measured against a cell no longer there, so it likely drifts toward the window's corner. **Recommended:** take it; one anchor rule covers every surface, and HEAD's open pane has lost its anchor anyway.
- **A Link Added From a Card's Chooser Opens Empty (Accident; Take):** today the chooser's popover for a Link inherits the Rename seat, which writes `[]()` into the empty field and seats the caret in its label (`ValueEditor.tsx:158-161`); every other route to a blank Link opens an empty field, which this one now does too.

### Phase 16B — One Value Seat: The Native Router, the Panel, and No Fabricated Definition

**GOAL:** The seat Phase 16A landed serves everything else that edits a value. One app-level `MenuSeat` replaces `ValuePickPresenter`, so a value picked from a menu away from it runs what a click would and nothing on the session channel decides by type; the Properties panel keeps subject loading, layout, row order, the Add rows, and revealed rows (J-5), and its value interaction moves to the seat, so its label and value menus are the seat's one row menu: a Link row's label gains Rename and Edit Link, a File value gains Remove and no Clear, and `propertyMenu.ts`' `page-value` kind and `fileValueMenu` leave. The `rename` intent folds into `popover`; and the pickers read the resolved column, so `syntheticContextDef` and its sites leave. Drive group 14 proves every surface on one seat.

**Starting State (Phase 16A's AFTER):** `Core/Properties/Cells/ValueSeat.tsx` holds `SeatHost` (`rowOf`, `commit`, `anchor`, `holder`, `connections`, `style` answering `ColumnStyle | null`, `setStyle`, `centered`, `hold`, `hide: { from: 'view' | 'row'; run }`, `clear`, `onClose`), `SeatOpen`, `useValueSeat` (`open`, `anchor`, `host`, `close`, `intentOf`, `run`, `click`, `pane`, `menu(row, column, e, label?)`, `editor`, `target`), `SeatChooser`, and `<ValueSeat seat chooser? />`; its `target` reads `column.def ?? syntheticContextDef(column.id)`, and its handler table still maps `rename`; `LinkMenuContext.value.hideable` and `valueMenuTarget`'s parameter take the `'view' | 'row'` union (Task 16A-1), and the seat hands both menus `host.hide?.from`. The view host returns `seatHost`; the table and Cards run every value through the seat; `CardValue.tsx` and `pickTarget` are gone. `runPropertyAction` and `ValuePickPresenter` read as P15 and P13 left them. The panel reads as HEAD with P13's columns and `currentOf`, P15's `useValueWriter`, P15's `hideable: 'row'` on its fallback Link menu, and P16A's `'row'` in its `valueMenuTarget` call: its label still pops `propertyMenuModel`'s `page-value` kind, and its File value `fileValueMenu`. P15's `HideFrom` (`Core/Actions/cellMenu.ts`) and `cellMenuContextFor(type, null, …)` answering a bare value are the vocabulary the panel's seat host reads.

+  const dismiss = useSession((s) => s.dismissPick)
+  const held = useHeld(pending, pending !== null)
+  // The request's row lives in its writer, so the seat reads it again after each commit.
+  const [, reread] = useReducer((n: number) => n + 1, 0)
+  const seat = useValueSeat({
+    rowOf: () => held?.rowOf(),
+    commit: (_, column, value) => {
+      held?.commit(column, value)
+      reread()
+    },
+    anchor: (el) => el,
+    holder: () => held?.holder,
+    connections: previewConnections,
+    style: () => held?.style ?? null,
+    onClose: dismiss,
+  })
+  useEffect(() => {
+    if (!pending) return
+    const row = pending.rowOf()
+    if (!row) return dismiss()
+    const intent = seat.intentOf(row, pending.column)
+    seat.run(row, pending.column, intent?.kind === 'edit' ? { kind: 'popover' } : intent, pending.trigger)
+    // The file dialog opens no pane, so nothing is left to hold the menu's anchor.
+    if (intent?.kind === 'file') dismiss()
+  }, [pending])
+  return <ValueSeat seat={seat} />
+}
```

```Core/Actions/propertyMenu.ts (after)
import type { ActionItem } from './menuModel'

// Delete is offered only inside the property's own pane.

type PropertyMenuContext = { kind: 'editor' } | { kind: 'assigned-row' }

type PropertyMenuAction = 'property:rename' | 'property:remove' | 'property:destroy'

export function propertyMenuModel(ctx: PropertyMenuContext): ActionItem<PropertyMenuAction>[] {
  switch (ctx.kind) {
    case 'editor':
      return [
        { label: 'Remove', action: 'property:remove' },
        { label: 'Delete', action: 'property:destroy', separatorBefore: true },
      ]
    case 'assigned-row':
      return [
        { label: 'Rename', action: 'property:rename' },
        { label: 'Remove', action: 'property:remove' },
      ]
  }
}

```UIX/Utilities/moveItem.ts diff
@@ after nextOrder @@
+
+/** A slot in a filtered view of the full order, as an index in the full order: it still holds every hidden id, so a raw visible index would land the drop among hidden rows. */
+export function fullOrderIndex(
+  orderedIds: readonly string[],
+  visibleIds: readonly string[],
+  draggedId: string,
+  visibleToIndex: number,
+): number {
+  const full = orderedIds.filter((id) => id !== draggedId)
+  const visible = visibleIds.filter((id) => id !== draggedId)
+  const successor = visible[visibleToIndex]
+  if (successor !== undefined) return full.indexOf(successor)
+  const last = visible[visible.length - 1]
+  return last !== undefined ? full.indexOf(last) + 1 : full.length
+}
```

#### Task 17-6

**TASK:** The type editors' shared container, `configEditor`, takes one collapse-safe rhythm: 8px between rows, carried as a top margin on each row after the first, and on the row inside a `Reveal` rather than on the `Reveal` itself, so a collapsed row's margin folds away with it and a revealed row keeps its own (L-1). The flex `gap`, which a collapsed `Reveal` still holds, leaves.

**NOW:** `configEditor` (`UIX/Menus/frames.css.ts:180-185`) is a flex column with `gap: '8px'` and `paddingTop: OPTION.gapAroundLabel` (6px); Checkbox, Link, and File render through it, none with a revealable row. `Reveal` (`UIX/Animations/Reveal.tsx:42-65`) is an outer grid `div` carrying `data-reveal` (and `data-open` while mounted) whose one child, an inner `div` with `minHeight: 0`, holds the row; the outer `div` stays mounted when collapsed, so a flex `gap` keeps a gap on each side of a collapsed row. `Reveal.tsx:61` names `[data-reveal] > *` as a contract other styles address. The inner `div` is a grid item and so its own formatting context: a margin on the row inside it stays inside the item, and a `0fr` track with `minHeight: 0` folds the item, margin included, to nothing. `number-editor.css.ts:6-9` puts its 8px on every row but the `:first-child`, which zeroes every revealed row, since each is its inner `div`'s first child (B-05-01). `MenuIndex` renders a section's rows as siblings under a `Fragment` (`UIX/Menus/MenuIndex.tsx:161-176`), so the rows and `Reveal` wrappers are the container's direct children. The `heading` row style sets `margin: 0` in a single class (`UIX/Menus/menu-row.css.ts:91-103`); the rule below outranks it.

```Core/Properties/Schema/typeRows.tsx diff
+import { PathField } from '@pommora/uix/Fields/PathField'
+import { type MenuRow, pickerRow, type Trailing } from '@pommora/uix/Menus'
+import type { PickerOption } from '@pommora/uix/Pickers/PickerControl'
+import { resolveColor } from '@pommora/uix/Theme/ramp'
+import { numberFrom } from '@pommora/uix/Utilities/numberUnit'
+import { DEFAULT_LINK_DISPLAY, type LinkDisplay } from '../../Connections/linkValue'
+import { reportRefusal } from '../../Interface/Notifications/notifications'
+import { dialer } from '../../Platform/dialer'
+import {
+  CHECKBOX_LOOKS,
+  type ColumnStyle,
+  lookIn,
+  NUMBER_LOOKS,
+  showsWeekday,
+  TIME_FORMATS,
+  WEEKDAY_FORMATS,
+} from '../columnStyles'
+import {
+  DATE_FORMAT_OPTIONS,
+  LINK_DISPLAY_OPTIONS,
+  lookOptions,
+  pickerOptions,
+  TIME_FORMAT_LABELS,
+  WEEKDAY_FORMAT_LABELS,
+} from '../displayLabels'
+import { numberBarCapable } from '../formatValue'
+import {
+  CURRENCY_CODES,
+  DEFAULT_CURRENCY,
+  type NumberConfig,
+  type NumberFamily,
+  type PropertyConfig,
+  type PropertyDefinition,
+  type PropertyType,
+} from '../properties'
+
+/** A type's settings write one of two scopes: `configure` the definition, wherever it's held; `setStyle` this view's column alone. */
+export type RowContext = {
+  style: ColumnStyle
+  setStyle: (patch: Partial<ColumnStyle>) => void
+  configure: (patch: PropertyConfig) => void
+  assetRoot: string
+}
+
+const FAMILY_OPTIONS: PickerOption<NumberFamily>[] = [
+  { value: 'number', label: 'Number' },
+  { value: 'percent', label: 'Percent' },
+  { value: 'currency', label: 'Currency' },
+]
+const CURRENCY_OPTIONS: PickerOption<string>[] = CURRENCY_CODES.map((code) => ({
+  value: code,
+  label: code,
+}))
+const DECIMAL_OPTIONS: PickerOption<string>[] = [
+  { value: 'hidden', label: 'Hidden' },
+  ...Array.from({ length: 10 }, (_, i) => ({ value: String(i + 1), label: String(i + 1) })),
+]
+const NUMBER_STYLE_OPTIONS = lookOptions(NUMBER_LOOKS)
+const CHECKBOX_STYLE_OPTIONS = lookOptions(CHECKBOX_LOOKS)
+const WEEKDAY_OPTIONS = pickerOptions(WEEKDAY_FORMATS, WEEKDAY_FORMAT_LABELS)
+const TIME_OPTIONS = pickerOptions(TIME_FORMATS, TIME_FORMAT_LABELS)
+
+const decimalsToPicker = (d: NumberConfig['number_decimals']): string =>
+  typeof d === 'number' ? String(d) : 'hidden'
+const pickerToDecimals = (v: string): 'hidden' | number => (v === 'hidden' ? 'hidden' : Number(v))
+
+const ROW = { inert: true } as const
+const DATE_ROW = { ...ROW, iconSize: 'headline' } as const
+
+const item = (label: string, trailing: Trailing, reveal?: boolean): MenuRow => ({
+  kind: 'item',
+  label,
+  trailing,
+  reveal,
+  ...ROW,
+})
+
+function numberRows(def: PropertyDefinition, { style, setStyle, configure }: RowContext): MenuRow[] {
+  const family: NumberFamily = def.number_family ?? 'number'
+  const percent = family === 'percent'
+  const fraction = def.number_fraction ?? false
+  return [
+    pickerRow(undefined, 'Format', family, FAMILY_OPTIONS, (v) => configure({ number_family: v }), {
+      ...ROW,
+      ariaLabel: 'Number format',
+    }),
+    pickerRow(
+      undefined,
+      'Currency',
+      def.number_currency ?? DEFAULT_CURRENCY,
+      CURRENCY_OPTIONS,
+      (v) => configure({ number_currency: v }),
+      { ...ROW, ariaLabel: 'Currency', reveal: family === 'currency' },
+    ),
+    item(
+      'Separators',
+      {
+        kind: 'switch',
+        checked: def.number_separators ?? true,
+        onChange: (next) => configure({ number_separators: next }),
+        ariaLabel: 'Separators',
+      },
+      !percent,
+    ),
+    pickerRow(
+      undefined,
+      'Decimals',
+      decimalsToPicker(def.number_decimals),
+      DECIMAL_OPTIONS,
+      (v) => configure({ number_decimals: pickerToDecimals(v) }),
+      { ...ROW, ariaLabel: 'Decimal places' },
+    ),
+    item(
+      'Fraction',
+      {
+        kind: 'switch',
+        checked: fraction,
+        onChange: (next) => configure({ number_fraction: next }),
+        ariaLabel: 'Fraction',
+      },
+      !percent,
+    ),
+    pickerRow(undefined, 'Value', '', [], () => {}, {
+      ...ROW,
+      ariaLabel: 'Fraction value',
+      reveal: !percent && fraction,
+      typeable: {
+        text: String(def.number_denominator ?? ''),
+        onCommit: (typed) => {
+          const n = numberFrom(typed)
+          if (n !== undefined || typed === '') configure({ number_denominator: n })
+        },
+      },
+    }),
+    pickerRow(
+      undefined,
+      'Style',
+      lookIn(NUMBER_LOOKS, style.look),
+      NUMBER_STYLE_OPTIONS,
+      (look) => setStyle({ look }),
+      { ...ROW, ariaLabel: 'Number style', reveal: numberBarCapable(def) },
+    ),
+  ]
+}
+
+/** Time stays visible under Relative — it still gates the "at <clock>" rendering. */
+const dateRows = (_def: PropertyDefinition, { style, setStyle }: RowContext): MenuRow[] => [
+  { kind: 'heading', label: 'Format' },
+  pickerRow(
+    'calendar-days',
+    'Date',
+    style.date_format,
+    DATE_FORMAT_OPTIONS,
+    (v) => setStyle({ date_format: v }),
+    { ...DATE_ROW, ariaLabel: 'Date format' },
+  ),
+  pickerRow('calendar', 'Day', style.weekday, WEEKDAY_OPTIONS, (v) => setStyle({ weekday: v }), {
+    ...DATE_ROW,
+    ariaLabel: 'Weekday format',
+    reveal: showsWeekday(style.date_format),
+  }),
+  pickerRow('clock', 'Time', style.time_format, TIME_OPTIONS, (v) => setStyle({ time_format: v }), {
+    ...DATE_ROW,
+    ariaLabel: 'Time format',
+  }),
+]
+
+function linkRows(def: PropertyDefinition, { configure }: RowContext): MenuRow[] {
+  const link = resolveColor(def.link_color, 'var(--link)')
+  return [
+    item('Underline', {
+      kind: 'switch',
+      checked: def.link_underline ?? false,
+      onChange: (v) => configure({ link_underline: v }),
+      ariaLabel: 'Underline links',
+    }),
+    item('Color', {
+      kind: 'color',
+      label: 'Color',
+      selected: link.name,
+      css: link.css,
+      onPick: (next) => configure({ link_color: next }),
+    }),
+    pickerRow(
+      undefined,
+      'Format',
+      def.link_display ?? DEFAULT_LINK_DISPLAY,
+      LINK_DISPLAY_OPTIONS,
+      (v: LinkDisplay) => configure({ link_display: v }),
+      { ...ROW, ariaLabel: 'Link format' },
+    ),
+  ]
+}
+
+function checkboxRows(def: PropertyDefinition, { style, setStyle, configure }: RowContext): MenuRow[] {
+  const chosen = resolveColor(def.checkbox_color, 'var(--checkbox-base)')
+  return [
+    item('Color', {
+      kind: 'color',
+      label: 'Color',
+      selected: chosen.name,
+      css: chosen.css,
+      onPick: (next) => configure({ checkbox_color: next }),
+    }),
+    pickerRow(
+      undefined,
+      'Style',
+      lookIn(CHECKBOX_LOOKS, style.look),
+      CHECKBOX_STYLE_OPTIONS,
+      (look) => setStyle({ look }),
+      { ...ROW, ariaLabel: 'Checkbox style' },
+    ),
+  ]
+}
+
+/** Relative to the asset root rather than to the nexus, so re-pointing the root carries it along. */
+const fileRows = (def: PropertyDefinition, { configure, assetRoot }: RowContext): MenuRow[] => [
+  item('Directory', {
+    kind: 'field',
+    children: (
+      <PathField
+        label="Directory"
+        value={def.file_directory ?? ''}
+        empty={assetRoot}
+        onCommit={(dir) => configure({ file_directory: dir })}
+        onBrowse={() =>
+          void dialer()
+            .ask('assets:chooseDir', 'property', def.file_directory)
+            .then((picked) => {
+              if (reportRefusal(picked) && picked.value !== null)
+                configure({ file_directory: picked.value })
+            })
+        }
+      />
+    ),
+  }),
+]
+
+const NONE = (): MenuRow[] => []
+
+// One arm per property type, so a type added is a compile error here rather than a blank pane: the option types edit in the option list, and Text and a registry Context carry no settings.
+const TYPE_ROWS: Record<PropertyType, (def: PropertyDefinition, ctx: RowContext) => MenuRow[]> = {
+  number: numberRows,
+  dateTime: dateRows,
+  link: linkRows,
+  checkbox: checkboxRows,
+  file: fileRows,
+  select: NONE,
+  multiSelect: NONE,
+  status: NONE,
+  text: NONE,
+  context: NONE,
+}
+
+export const rowsFor = (def: PropertyDefinition, ctx: RowContext): MenuRow[] =>
+  TYPE_ROWS[def.type](def, ctx)
```

```Core/Properties/Schema/typeRows.test.ts diff
+import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest'
+import type { MenuRow } from '@pommora/uix/Menus'
+import { dateDefaults } from '../columnStyles'
+import type { PropertyDefinition, PropertyType } from '../properties'
+import { type RowContext, rowsFor } from './typeRows'
+
+const ctx = (over: Partial<RowContext> = {}): RowContext => ({
+  style: dateDefaults('full'),
+  setStyle: vi.fn(),
+  configure: vi.fn(),
+  assetRoot: 'Assets',
+  ...over,
+})
+const def = (type: PropertyType, fields: Partial<PropertyDefinition> = {}): PropertyDefinition =>
+  ({ id: 'prop_x', label: 'X', key: 'X', type, ...fields }) as PropertyDefinition
+
+type Item = Extract<MenuRow, { kind: 'item' }>
+const items = (rows: MenuRow[]): Item[] => rows.filter((r): r is Item => r.kind === 'item')
+/** The rows a viewer sees: a row revealed as `false` is collapsed. */
+const shown = (rows: MenuRow[]): string[] =>
+  items(rows)
+    .filter((r) => r.reveal !== false)
+    .map((r) => String(r.label))
+const trailing = (rows: MenuRow[], label: string) => {
+  const t = items(rows).find((r) => r.label === label)?.trailing
+  if (!t) throw new Error(`no row "${label}"`)
+  return t
+}
+const pick = (rows: MenuRow[], label: string, value: string): void => {
+  const t = trailing(rows, label)
+  if (t.kind !== 'picker') throw new Error(`"${label}" is no picker`)
+  t.onPick(value)
+}
+const typed = (rows: MenuRow[], label: string, text: string): void => {
+  const t = trailing(rows, label)
+  if (t.kind !== 'picker' || !t.typeable) throw new Error(`"${label}" takes no typing`)
+  t.typeable.onCommit(text)
+}
+
+describe('rowsFor', () => {
+  it('a Number shows Currency only for currency, hides Separators and Fraction for Percent, and offers Style only where a bar has a ceiling', () => {
+    expect(shown(rowsFor(def('number'), ctx()))).toEqual(['Format', 'Separators', 'Decimals', 'Fraction'])
+    expect(shown(rowsFor(def('number', { number_family: 'currency' }), ctx()))).toEqual([
+      'Format',
+      'Currency',
+      'Separators',
+      'Decimals',
+      'Fraction',
+    ])
+    expect(shown(rowsFor(def('number', { number_family: 'percent' }), ctx()))).toEqual([
+      'Format',
+      'Decimals',
+      'Style',
+    ])
+  })
+
+  it('the fraction Value row shows only while Fraction is on, refuses text that only partly parses, and a blank clears it', () => {
+    const c = ctx()
+    const rows = rowsFor(def('number', { number_fraction: true, number_denominator: 10 }), c)
+    expect(shown(rows)).toEqual(['Format', 'Separators', 'Decimals', 'Fraction', 'Value', 'Style'])
+    typed(rows, 'Value', '12abc')
+    expect(c.configure).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
+    typed(rows, 'Value', '')
+    expect(c.configure).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ number_denominator: undefined })
+  })
+
+  it("a Number's format writes the definition and its Style the view", () => {
+    const c = ctx()
+    const rows = rowsFor(def('number', { number_family: 'percent' }), c)
+    pick(rows, 'Format', 'currency')
+    pick(rows, 'Style', 'bar')
+    expect(c.configure).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ number_family: 'currency' })
+    expect(c.setStyle).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ look: 'bar' })
+  })
+
+  it('a Date shows its Day row only for the worded formats, and each pick writes the view', () => {
+    expect(shown(rowsFor(def('dateTime'), ctx({ style: dateDefaults('monthDayYear') })))).toEqual([
+      'Date',
+      'Time',
+    ])
+    const c = ctx({ style: { ...dateDefaults('full'), weekday: 'none' } })
+    const rows = rowsFor(def('dateTime'), c)
+    expect(rows[0]).toEqual({ kind: 'heading', label: 'Format' })
+    expect(shown(rows)).toEqual(['Date', 'Day', 'Time'])
+    pick(rows, 'Date', 'short')
+    pick(rows, 'Day', 'long')
+    expect(c.setStyle).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ date_format: 'short' })
+    expect(c.setStyle).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ weekday: 'long' })
+  })
+
+  it("a Link's underline, color, and format write the definition", () => {
+    const c = ctx()
+    const rows = rowsFor(def('link'), c)
+    const underline = trailing(rows, 'Underline')
+    if (underline.kind !== 'switch') throw new Error('Underline is no switch')
+    underline.onChange(true)
+    pick(rows, 'Format', 'link-full')
+    expect(c.configure).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ link_underline: true })
+    expect(c.configure).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ link_display: 'link-full' })
+    expect(c.setStyle).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
+  })
+
+  it("a Checkbox's swatch paints the Nexus's checkbox color when unset; its Color writes the definition and its Style the view", () => {
+    const c = ctx({ style: { ...dateDefaults('full'), look: 'switch' } })
+    const rows = rowsFor(def('checkbox'), c)
+    const color = trailing(rows, 'Color')
+    if (color.kind !== 'color') throw new Error('Color is no swatch')
+    expect(color.css).toContain('var(--checkbox-base)')
+    color.onPick('blue-1')
+    pick(rows, 'Style', 'checkbox')
+    expect(c.configure).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ checkbox_color: 'blue-1' })
+    expect(c.setStyle).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ look: 'checkbox' })
+  })
+
+  it('a File offers its directory field and nothing else', () => {
+    const rows = rowsFor(def('file'), ctx())
+    expect(shown(rows)).toEqual(['Directory'])
+    expect(trailing(rows, 'Directory').kind).toBe('field')
+  })
+
+  it("only the Date rows carry glyphs, and the option types, Text, and Context answer none", () => {
+    for (const type of ['number', 'link', 'checkbox', 'file'] as const)
+      expect(items(rowsFor(def(type), ctx())).every((r) => r.icon === undefined)).toBe(true)
+    expect(items(rowsFor(def('dateTime'), ctx())).every((r) => r.icon !== undefined)).toBe(true)
+    for (const type of ['select', 'multiSelect', 'status', 'text', 'context'] as const)
+      expect(rowsFor(def(type), ctx())).toEqual([])
+  })
+})

#### Departures and Disclosures

##### Departures From the Findings

- **`FLUSH_GHOST` States the Flush-Slot Knob Once (17-1):** the Investigation's reading spells `{ dwellMs: REVEAL_DWELL_MS, graceMs: 0 }` at both calls, which would state one tuned knob twice; the pair and its reason sit once beside the chip that draws the slot, and each caller adds only its own `suppressed`.
- **Neutral Names Reach the Lane Keys and the Highlight Class (17-3):** the drop kinds alone would leave `'assigned'`/`'all'` lanes and `allHighlight` speaking the Properties pane's words inside a kit model the visibility pane also uses; the Properties pane's own classes (`assignedFill`, `allRow`, `allHeading`) name its look and stay.
- **Both Panes' Drop Handlers Switch (17-3):** the Findings name `PropertyFrame.handleDrop`; `VisibilityFrame.handleDrop`'s `if`/`else` over the same union takes the same Hard Rule, with its one-line reason for having no `reorder-rest` arm.
- **The Kit's Drag Test Pins a Literal (17-3):** `paneDrop.test.ts` read Title's reserved id from Core; under `UIX/Menus` it pins `'pinned'`, since what it tests is the pinned-row rule, not Title.
- **No Shared Order-Row Component (17-4):** the Findings move the helpers "with one shared order row". The three rows already share `rowEye`; what each spells for itself is one class expression. A component wrapping the box and the eye was drafted for this phase and came to about +28 lines (five props at each of three sites under Biome's 100-column wrap, and a `div`/`LineRow` branch for the date row, which doesn't drag) against the one line it saves per site. Under *Less Stuff* and the 10-22-2026 directive the helpers move whole, and the per-row duplication that costs work at render, each option resolved three times, folds to one. The simplification reviewer is briefed to challenge it.
- **`compactTitle` Joins `frames.css.ts`, Not `OptionSlot.tsx` (17-5):** vanilla-extract compiles a `style()` only inside a `.css.ts` file, so the class can't fold into a component file; the kit's frame styles hold `optionLead`, the span it sits inside, which is scout 05's stated alternative.
- **`OptionDraft` Keeps Its `edit` Prop (17-5):** the draft reads two of the hook's members; P1 made the hook's API type module-private, so the prop is typed by those two members, and neither call site changes shape.
- **The Rhythm Is Anchored on the `[data-reveal]` Wrapper and Carried by Its Row (17-6):** the Findings put the rhythm "on `Reveal`'s `[data-reveal]` wrapper". The wrapper stays mounted through a close, and `data-open` stays set until the close settles (`Reveal.tsx:21,36-40,46`), so a margin on the wrapper either holds 8px under a collapsed row or, keyed to `data-open`, snaps away after the animation. The selector finds each revealed row through its wrapper and sets the margin on the row itself (`[data-reveal] > * > *`, the depth `Reveal.tsx:61` names as a contract), which the `0fr` track folds with the animation.

- **`LOOKS` Already Serves the Narrowings (17-7):** P3 routed the frame's three narrowings through `lookIn` over `LOOKS`' rows; `typeRows.tsx` carries the Checkbox and Number two, and the option footing's stays in the frame, so nothing further lands here.
- **`FormatRows` Stays Its Own Compact Block (17-7):** it isn't one of the five editors, and it draws in `ruleFrame`'s compact density above every editor; moving it into `configEditor` would change its look (I-1).

- **The Layout Pins Are the Drive's (17-7, 17-11):** jsdom computes no layout, so "a revealed Number row keeps its margin" and "a collapsed Day row leaves no gap" are the drive's pixel checks; vitest pins the DOM the rule addresses (`PropertyFrame.test.tsx`' container shape case) and every row's content (`typeRows.test.ts`).

##### Behavior Changes and Disclosures

- **The Number Editor's Revealed Rows Gain Their 8px (L-1, Nathan's Intent):** Separators, Fraction, and, when shown, Currency, Value, and Style sat flush against the row above; every row now sits 8px from the next.
- **The Date Editor Takes the Shared Rhythm (L-1, Nathan's Intent; LC-55):** a collapsed Day row leaves no stray 4px. The Date rows also space at 8px where they spaced at 4, under the 6px top padding every other editor already has: a third visible change the Findings' L-1 entry doesn't name, which follows from "every editor shares one layout" as the Investigation explained it to Nathan. The drive's `g15-date-*` screenshots show it.
- **A Denominator of Zero or Less Is Refused (L-3, Nathan's Intent):** typing one leaves the field reading the denominator it held; P7's decode already reads a stored one as unset.
- **An Editor Whose Property Leaves Returns to the List (O-5, Nathan's Intent):** a delete, a Remove from another surface, an outside edit, or a sync that takes the property out of this Collection shows the list, where the pane read "Property not found."
- **An Editor That Gave Way Reopens If Its Property Returns (Earlier Agent's Choice; Take; LC-60):** the pane keeps naming the editor it gave way from, so if the property comes back before anything else is opened (an undo of an outside Remove, a sync, or re-adding it from All Properties after a Remove made elsewhere), its editor slides open again. O-5 says nothing about a return; the frame's own Remove and Delete reset the view, so a property removed or deleted from this pane doesn't reopen. **Recommended:** take it; the same derived view is what lets a just-created property's editor open the moment the tree holds it, and clearing the view on every departure would need a second rule watching the schema.
- **The Header's Icon Button Is Spoken "Edit Icon" (L-4, Nathan's Intent):** on all five surfaces the kit header serves.
- **Nothing Else Visible:** no row moves, no wording changes, and only Date's rows carry icons (I-1, L-2, I-076); the ghost slot's dwell and grace, the inline rename, both panes' drags, the order lists, and the option editor behave as at P16's head.
- **O-5's Rule (17-11):** its outcome is recorded here when the drive runs; if the remedy lands, the editor of a newly created property opens once the tree holds it, so the type list stays on screen for those frames instead of the list, and the frame gains `assigned` (+13 lines, in the line total's conditional row).

+
+Every Page carries the id key (`ID`, holding a kind-marked ULID assigned at creation), maintained by Pommora and not user-creatable, and may carry `banner:`, which assigns its banner. **Filedata** is what a view reads off the file itself under the reserved ids, and Pommora writes none of it: **Title** is the file's name, **Creation Time** the instant the `ID` ULID encodes, **Last Modified** the file's modification time as the filesystem reports it, and **Location** the folder holding the page. The first three show as columns beside properties, and all four sort and filter, the two times as dates. A write the user makes to the page moves Last Modified — a value edit or a text edit — while a rename, a move, and a schema edit that rewrites the page for a reason of its own leave it where it was.

-**Schema Mutations:** The registry mutations live in `Core/Properties/registryProperty.ts` and its siblings; their entry points queue on one lock on the `.nexus` folder, which quitting waits on, and every operation that writes both the registry and pages states its intent in a journal first so a crash replays forward on the next open, and the Try Again a property rename, a format change, a property delete, an option rename, or an option removal offers replays what that property still owes at once, an option removal offering it only while the journal holds its record.

-| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

-Neither Remove nor the global delete is cross-file atomic; each is a per-file fan-out whose safety net is written first and which re-runs cleanly after a partial run. Remove is the daily path; the global delete is the rare destructive one.
+**Property Changes:** Property changes run one at a time, and quitting waits for the one in flight. Creating a property mints a Nexus-wide definition, assigns it to the Collection it was made in, and writes nothing to a page until a value is set. Assigning one adds the Collection's reference to it and refills the values a Remove stashed there; reordering changes the Collection's order, or, in All Properties, the Nexus-wide display order. A label rename, a Label Format or Value Format change, and an option rename rewrite the key or word in every page in a Collection or the Archive and every Space that holds it, leaving each page's Last Modified where it was, while adding, reordering, and recoloring options change only the definition. An option's Clear strips its word from every file and stash holding it and keeps the option. A format change or a Clear asks first once it reaches more than one Item, naming them, and a Value Format change is refused when it would give two options one key or give an option a key another option held before the change.
+
+**Remove and Delete:** Removing a property from a Collection unassigns it, clears it from the Collection's views, its Sets' views, and the View Tiles showing them, and moves each page's value into the Collection's stash before stripping it; a page it can't rewrite — unreadable, without an ID, or sharing another page's ID — keeps its value and counts toward Try Again. Re-adding the property refills the pages still in the Collection, writing a trashed page's value into its Trash copy. Deleting a property is the rare destructive path: a Trash record holding the definition, the Collections that assigned it, every value by its holder's id, and each Collection's stash lands first, then the definition leaves the registry, and its values, stashes, and every saved view, View Tile, and Matrix filter rule naming it are stripped. An option's Delete strips its word from the files and stashes holding it, drops it from every configuration naming it, and drops a filter rule left with nothing to match. Both deletes always ask, naming the Items holding what they reach when any do. A deleted property comes back from the Trash pane or the notification's Undo, under a numbered name when its own was taken in the meantime.
+
+**The Stash:** A removed property's values wait in its Collection's settings file, under `property_stash`, beside the time they were removed. They're kept for the **History Timeframe**, and the next open, or a change to that timeframe, clears what has outlived it.
+
+**Unfinished Changes:** A change that rewrites many files notes what it owes in a device-local notes file before it starts, and doesn't start when the note can't be written. A file it can't reach is counted in its notice with Try Again, which finishes every owed change at once, and the next open finishes whatever a closed session left. Until then, a create, rename, Label Format change, or restore onto a name still owed is refused with Try Again. An option's Clear writes no note, and a file it misses is named in a warning without Try Again.

Some keys hold sections that merge a level deeper, key by key within them; `settings.json` merges per setting and a level deeper within each, so the Open In Preview switch and its rules merge apart, as the Matrix filter's do; a metadata month file merges per page and per field, so one device clearing a page's entry and another setting a field on it keeps that field; the property registry merges per definition and per field, so a type respelled on one device and a rename made on another both survive. One of these files that doesn't parse stays on its device until it does, and one arriving that way leaves a local copy that parses in place, capturing the arrival, so the local copy ships over it.

-Removing a property from a Collection moves its values off the Collection's pages into a stash (`property_cache`) in the Collection's own settings file, where re-adding the property restores them. The stash stays there, and its entries are kept for the History Timeframe (`historyDays`), the setting that sets how long page history snapshots and captures are kept; after that, they're cleaned out. That setting measures the age of saved page text, and a stash entry is a removed property's values waiting to be re-added, so one number sets how long both are recoverable. The Archive already separates these cases: Archive History Timeframe (`archiveHistoryDays`) sets how long archived pages keep their snapshots, follows History Timeframe until it's picked, and never exceeds it. The stash has no such setting, so removed values can't be kept longer than page history, or cleaned out sooner, without changing page history too.[^77]
